To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

papers.title: Structural Perturbations and Full Field Evolution in Tapered Spun Ring-Core Fiber Amplifiers
papers.abstract: We theoretically investigate the complex full-vector modal field evolution in tapered spun ring-core fiber amplifiers subject to structural perturbations, utilizing a combined coupled-mode theory and rate-equation model. To provide a comprehensive characterization, we introduce a normalized complex modal-state fidelity factor that simultaneously incorporates intensity, phase and polarization into a single quantitative measure. We demonstrate that the twist pitch of the structure can be purposely tuned to either suppress or leverage the effect of specific geometrical perturbations. These findings provide insight into the physical conditions governing modal stability, establishing a robust mechanism for highly efficient in-fiber OAM mode conversion.

papers.title: Linear stability of viscous stratified shear flows with arbitrary equations of state
papers.abstract: A mathematical framework is developed to analyse the linear stability of viscous stratified flows with arbitrary equations of state. The model accommodates equations of state of the form $p=\Phi(T,\rho)$ or $\rho=\phi(T)$, together with a set of governing dimensionless parameters. Density stratification is unrestricted, allowing for the study of non-Boussinesq effects. A low-Mach-number approximation is employed to filter out acoustic phenomena. The framework is applied to two viscous stratified configurations of plane Couette flow: a triple-layer density profile supporting the Taylor--Caulfield instability (TCI), and a differentially heated supercritical fluid exhibiting a distinct instability mechanism. Following validation against reference studies, we present new results showing that non-Boussinesq effects weaken the viscous TCI, whilst viscosity can further destabilise the supercritical fluid instability, in contrast to the stabilising influence of buoyancy.

papers.title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
papers.abstract: Intrinsic color centers are investigated in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation delta SCF calculations identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. A comparison of their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It exhibits the highest calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate of 43.9 MHz and ZPL quantum efficiency of 11.8% among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation yields a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a multimode photoluminescence calculation gives a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37%, indicating a dominant zero-phonon contribution. The predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) also has the smallest photon-energy separation from the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets among the candidates. These results identify VVa1+ as a promising intrinsic color center for fiber-based quantum communication, with quantum frequency upconversion offering a route from its strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands.

papers.title: Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves Probing Phase Transitions in the Standard Model and Beyond
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are unique messengers of physics in the early Universe and possible sources for the observed data from pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). It has been demonstrated that SIGWs have the potential to probe cosmological phase transitions via measurement of the equation of state and sound speed of the cosmic thermal bath, which have non-trivial time dependence during phase transitions. In this work, we improve on existing studies of SIGWs in a time-dependent background with time-dependent initial conditions and an entropy-conserving thermal history of the Standard Model (SM). We provide possible physical explanations for features of the gravitational wave spectrum from phase transitions, the most prominent of which for a scale-invariant curvature spectrum is a step due to entropy dilution. We show that current and future gravitational wave observations across a wide range of frequencies can probe phase transitions in the SM and physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). Signals from the QCD crossover appear around 10 nHz, inside the observable window of PTAs. We perform data analyses using NANOGrav 15-year data, showing a mild preference for the QCD crossover over standard radiation domination for two choices of curvature spectra. BSM phase transitions in the TeV range lead to signals around mHz, which are accessible in future space-based experiments such as LISA, Taiji and TianQin.

papers.title: Angular momentum transport in a newborn protostar--disc system: magnetic braking, spiral arms and the magneto-rotational instability
papers.abstract: Angular momentum transport in young protostar--disc systems involves magnetic braking, magneto-rotational turbulence and gravitational instability, mechanisms that are usually studied separately and on different scales. We present a three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic simulation, including Ohmic and ambipolar diffusion, that follows the collapse of a $1~M_\odot$ dense core continuously from the cloud scale to the formation of the protostar, and then the resulting protostar--disc system for $\sim 64~\mathrm{yr}$ at a resolution of $\sim 10^{-4}~\mathrm{AU}$ at the protostellar surface. We decompose the azimuthally averaged angular momentum budget into Reynolds, Maxwell and gravitational torques, each split into a radial and a meridional component, over a quasi-steady phase of the evolution. The collapse produces a thick disc an order of magnitude more massive than the protostar, whose specific angular momentum decreases as it accretes. Accretion through the disc is vertically layered, with accreting and decreting layers at the same radius, a pattern set layer by layer by the torques. The transport separates into three regimes delimited by the coupling of the magnetic field to the gas. Magnetic braking operates in the envelope. Maxwell stresses dominate inside $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{AU}$, where the field recouples and the magneto-rotational instability develops. In the ambipolar dead zone that makes up the bulk of the disc, the Reynolds stress dominates, carried by $m=2$ spiral arms in a marginally unstable disc, with the gravitational stress as a secondary contributor. Meridional transport is as important as radial transport, so that a one-dimensional viscous model fitted to the net mass flux would require a negative $\alpha$ over part of the disc.

papers.title: Kinetic Non-Equilibrium Receptivity Analysis of Hypersonic Flows via a Complex Linearized Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme
papers.abstract: In the near-space regime, local rarefaction near the leading-edge shock and wall degrades Navier-Stokes-based stability and receptivity analyses due to velocity slip, temperature jumps, and non-equilibrium transport. The unified gas-kinetic scheme (UGKS) provides a multiscale kinetic description spanning continuum to rarefied regimes. Building on this, a complex linearized UGKS (CLUGKS) is developed: first-order perturbations of the discrete UGKS residual are formulated under a time-harmonic assumption with complex amplitudes, converting disturbance equations into a steady elliptic system solved via pseudo-time marching with LU-SGS acceleration. Consequently, kinetic shock structures, wall slip, temperature jumps, and non-Fourier heat fluxes are inherently captured without hybrid coupling. Three benchmarks verify the framework: a standing acoustic wave at an isothermal wall, a Mach 2 normal shock interacting with an obliquely incident acoustic wave, and freestream acoustic receptivity of a hypersonic blunt wedge. The scheme is applied to argon blunt-wedge flows at equivalent altitudes of 40 km and 50 km. At 40 km, UGKS and Navier-Stokes wall responses agree well in period and phase, while wall slip sustains a weakly positive spatial growth rate in UGKS downstream. At 50 km, intensified rarefaction produces a kinetic temperature precursor and a thickened, merged shock layer; while wall-pressure responses remain close, significant deviations emerge in temperature and heat-flux disturbances. These findings show that while continuum models capture dominant wall-pressure signatures under moderate rarefaction, resolving kinetic non-equilibrium across the shock-particularly its thermal footprint-is essential at higher altitudes.

papers.title: Stress-controlled avoided-crossing evolution of an optical microresonator induced by inter-fibre side coupling
papers.abstract: Analogies between quantum mechanics and photonics provide a powerful means of transferring concepts and phenomena between the two fields. Photonic analogues offer a distinctive advantage by allowing us to engineer and continuously vary parameters fixed by the microscopic structure of quantum systems, revealing richer behaviour. Building on these analogies, the recent demonstration of widely tunable microresonators formed by side coupling between optical fibres marked a significant advance in the development of reconfigurable resonant photonic systems. However, those methods offered no direct way to reach the centre of the avoided crossing, where the uncoupled fibre cutoff frequencies coincide and the modes hybridise most strongly. Here, we introduce an additional tuning degree of freedom by axially stretching a straight fibre coupled to a bent fibre. At essentially fixed coupling geometry, this lets us sweep the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero. As the avoided crossing is approached, the induced microresonator's resonance band widens. Beyond the crossing, the band narrows and, strikingly, appears to "hang" below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency. Our experimental results agree with coupled-mode theory and indicate the feasibility of 100 MHz-scale control of the straight-fibre cutoff frequency and the resonator spectral height over a tuning range of about 100 GHz, using a relative elongation of order $10^{-3}$.

papers.title: Density dependence of effective Lambda-nucleon interactions
papers.abstract: Orbital-dependent $\Lambda$ binding energies in hypernuclei such as $^{208}_{\Lambda}$Pb, $^{40}_{\Lambda}$K, and $^{48}_{\Lambda}$K are important objectives of planned experiments at J-PARC and JLab and provide information on the density-dependent features of effective $\Lambda N$ interactions. To investigate this relation we introduce the environmental density $\bar{\rho}_\text{env}$, defined as the overlap integral of the \Lambda and nuclear core densities, as quantitative measure of the nuclear environment experienced by the $\Lambda$ in each orbital. Calculations are performed within the deformed Skyrme-Hartree-Fock framework, comparing several phenomenological and microscopic $\Lambda N$ interactions. We find an approximately linear relation between the orbital-dependent binding energies and $\bar{\rho}_\text{env}$, offering a quantitative means to test and refine effective $\Lambda N$ interactions using future orbital-dependent binding-energy data.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Modeling of Destination-Constrained Dynamic Systems via Doob's $h$-Transform
papers.abstract: Existing work on modeling destination-constrained dynamic systems has mainly focused on discrete-time formulations with linear destination constraints or Gaussian destination distributions. Since practical systems are more naturally modeled in continuous time and often subject to nonlinear/non-Gaussian constraints/distributions, this paper proposes a unified measure-transformation framework for continuous-time modeling of systems subject to deterministic or distributional constraints on a nonlinear function of the terminal state. The framework starts from an unconstrained Itô stochastic differential equation, typically derived from physical laws to describe the system's forward evolution without destination information, and takes its induced path measure as unconstrained measure. Doob's $h$-transform is employed to transform this measure into a constrained path measure incorporating destination information through an injected drift. The resulting system is proved to satisfy the constraints while preserving the laws of the unconstrained state process conditioned on the destination information. The transition density is derived, and the path measure of the distributionally constrained system is proved to uniquely minimize Kullback--Leibler divergence from the unconstrained path measure among those satisfying the same distributional constraint. Its injected drift is further shown to converge pointwise to that of the deterministically constrained system as the destination distribution shrinks to the prespecified value. For linear time-varying unconstrained systems, a simplified form of the constrained systems is derived in terms of the conditional expectation of the terminal state, leading to the development of trajectory-generation algorithms. Numerical simulations evaluate the proposed framework under both types of destination constraints.

papers.title: Input-to-State Safety and Small-Gain Theorems for Large-Scale Nonlinear Systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies the safety verification problem for a general class of large-scale systems characterized by multiple safety indicator functions. Each safety indicator function satisfies a trajectory-based input-to-state safety (ISSf) estimate that provides a lower bound on its value along system trajectories in terms of the initial state, external inputs, and the other safety indicator functions, whose influence is quantified by continuous and nondecreasing gain functions. Within this framework, we establish a safety-oriented small-gain theorem and its corresponding corollaries that enable compositional and scalable safety verification of the interconnected system, provided that the interconnection gain functions satisfy a small-gain condition on the negative real axis. This condition concerns only the neighborhood of the safety boundary, thereby facilitating the application of our results to safety verification of multi-agent systems under distributed control. Our proof combines small-gain techniques with the lower-bound structure of ISSf estimates and develops an inductive comparison argument that establishes the ISSf property for the overall system throughout the maximal interval of existence. As an application, we establish robust safety for the natural distributed "half-spring" controller, theoretically supporting the computationally efficient and inspiring approach to safety-critical control of multi-agent systems in the presence of obstacles and external disturbances.

papers.title: Asteroseismology of the Gaia SB2 HD 70510: From Radial Modes to Component Masses
papers.abstract: Double-lined spectroscopic binary (SB2) orbits give mass ratios and projected component masses, but the absolute masses depend on the unknown inclination. HD 70510 is a Gaia DR3 SB2 in which regular $\delta$ Scuti pulsations constrain the properties of one component. We analyze nine sectors of TESS photometry and combine stellar evolution and pulsation modelling with a two-star spectral energy distribution (SED) fit to the unresolved Gaia and 2MASS photometry. Five high-signal-to-noise peaks form a sequence consistent with the radial fundamental mode and four consecutive overtones. Two stable pulsation clocks show the sign and amplitude expected from the orbital motion of the Gaia primary, identifying it as the pulsator. Combining the radial-mode and binary-SED fits with the Gaia SB2 orbit gives $M_1=1.594^{+0.026}_{-0.026}\,M_\odot$, $R_1=1.482^{+0.014}_{-0.012}\,R_\odot$, and an age of $171^{+112}_{-99}$ Myr. We obtain an orbital inclination of $i=82.1^{+3.5}_{-3.4}$ deg and a companion mass of $M_2=1.121^{+0.029}_{-0.028}\,M_\odot$. These intervals are statistical and remain conditional on the adopted radial-mode identification and stellar and binary-SED models. The primary lies close to the zero-age main sequence, while the roughly 6000-K companion contributes 14-28% of the unresolved optical-to-near-infrared flux. HD 70510 shows how regular pulsations can provide component masses for non-eclipsing TESS binaries with Gaia DR3 SB2 orbital solutions.

papers.title: Plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekulé distortion: Electron-hole asymmetry of the effective interlayer tunneling
papers.abstract: The effective interlayer tunneling (EIT) is a key quantity in determining the out-of-phase plasmons of a bilayer structure. Using the tight-binding model and the random phase approximation, we investigate plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekulé distortion. Both O/O and G/O bilayers exhibit strong electron-hole asymmetry in the EIT. For the O/O bilayer, the gap of the out-of-phase plasmon remains almost constant as the electron concentration varies, whereas it increases rapidly with increasing hole concentration; hole doping can also lead to stronger anomalous dispersion than electron doping. For the G/O bilayer, enhancing the Kekulé distortion $\Delta_0$ can weaken the EIT, as reflected by the reduced interlayer hybridization caused by the lifted layer degeneracy, especially for the electron-doped case. For the electron-doped G/O bilayer, the EIT is almost turned off when $\Delta_0=0.3$ from the perspective of the dispersion. Our results imply that switching the doping type between electron and hole can tune the performance of out-of-phase plasmon-based devices by modulating the EIT.

papers.title: Optimal Regulation and Information Institutions with Hidden Network Equilibria
papers.abstract: Aggregate outcomes can conceal network configurations that expose households to uninsurable risk and require different public services. We study a regulator's joint choice of a corrective activity charge and an information institution in a two-population network game. Although aggregate behavior follows an exact stable law, distinct specialization equilibria require different targeted interventions. With purchased Gaussian monitoring, primitive conditions imply a discontinuous switch between strong regulation without purchased information and informed specialization. The regulator may alternatively obtain signed certification or elicit a privately known state through a report backed by committed random audits. We characterize the three institutions' optimized values and the cost thresholds at which credible disclosure replaces government monitoring. The institutional choice also changes optimal regulation: even when certification and truthful reporting reveal the same state, costly audits favor less specialization and a higher corrective charge. This ordering and monotonicity in audit costs hold under an explicit interiority condition without global concavity of the audit problem. The institutional comparison is solved in the benchmark without feedback from anticipated policy, while the policy switch and strict institutional rankings admit local persistence under additional regularity conditions. Results depend on enforceable verification, restrictions on data access, and an explicitly limited institutional menu.

papers.title: Joint Activation and Weight Quantization for Learned Image Compression
papers.abstract: Learned image compression (LIC) models achieve competitive rate-distortion performance with increasingly large networks, making network quantization important for efficient deployment. Directly quantizing LIC models remains difficult in post-training quantization (PTQ) because compression performance is highly sensitive to quantization noise. Existing methods typically focus on optimizing either the weights or the activations, resulting in substantial rate-distortion degradation. To address this limitation, we introduce a two-stage pipeline that uses SmoothQuant to balance activation and weight ranges, followed by GPTQ to adapt the transformed weights. The proposed joint search framework optimizes the balancing transformation and adapted weights under the rate-distortion objective, accounting for the coupling between the two stages. Experiments across multiple LIC architectures and activation quantization configurations show that the joint search strategy consistently reduces rate-distortion degradation after quantization.

papers.title: Residual-Closed-Loop SAGE-Brent Estimation for Unknown-Order Wideband Underwater Acoustic Channels
papers.abstract: Grid mismatch in wideband channel estimation leaves structured cancellation residuals after strong-path subtraction. These residuals generate spurious correlation peaks or mask weak arrivals, turning continuous parameter errors into path-count errors. We propose RC-SAGE-Brent, a residual-closed-loop estimator that jointly refines continuous delay-scale parameters and corrects the unknown-order path set. Within each feedback cycle, ambiguity-constrained alternating Brent searches suppress strong-path cancellation residuals. Candidate validation, resolution-constrained pruning, and full-domain residual redetection then revise the active path set. For linear frequency modulation (LFM) probes, an observable signal-to-residual ratio adaptively scales the model-order penalty to mitigate overestimation caused by delay-scale coupling. Theoretical analysis links off-grid parameter errors to local cancellation-residual curvature and weak-path detectability. Factorial ablations, paired comparisons against standard sparse and off-grid estimators, and measured channel replay demonstrate improved path-set recovery and waveform reconstruction while delineating the operational boundaries of the method.

papers.title: Emergent Quantized Zak Phases without Dimerization in a Multicomponent Fermionic Extended Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: Quantized Zak phases are commonly associated with dimerized systems, such as the noninteracting Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) model. In interacting systems, however, interactions can induce effective dimerization of particle clusters even in the absence of explicit dimerization in the underlying lattice. In this work, we study a one-dimensional multicomponent fermionic extended Hubbard model under a resonance condition between the on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions. We find that quantized Zak phases emerge for odd fermion numbers $n\geqslant 3$, protected by the inversion symmetry of the effective Hamiltonian. Furthermore, in the presence of a tilted field, fermion clusters exhibit Bloch oscillations, during which their Zak phases can be extracted from the evolution of a Gaussian wave packet over one Bloch period. Our results reveal an interaction-induced mechanism for realizing quantized Zak phases in multicomponent fermionic systems without explicit lattice dimerization.

papers.title: Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Battery-Assisted Grid-Import Smoothing in AI Data Centers
papers.abstract: Rapid AI data-center power fluctuations challenge grid integration. Sustained grid-import smoothing requires allocating limited battery power and energy under uncertain demand. We formulate risk-aware BESS scheduling that coordinates advance reserve commitments and demand-responsive dispatch, accounting for operating costs, grid-ramp penalties, and their conditional value-at-risk. We develop battery scheduling decision-focused learning (BS-DFL) with a constraint-aware neural optimization layer trained directly from this objective without optimal-solution labels. The trained layer is then frozen to guide demand-predictor learning through scheduling costs and ramping risk, enabling solver-free rolling-horizon scheduling. In a 10,000-minute simulation using loads derived from measured AI workloads, BS-DFL reduces mean absolute minute-to-minute grid-import changes by 71.70% and total scheduling cost by 18.01% relative to an MSE-trained predictor coupled with a mixed-integer linear programming solver, with an average decision time of 18.77 ms.

papers.title: Walrus Technical Report
papers.abstract: We present Walrus, a unified 8B speech-and-audio foundation model handling speech recognition (including code-switching and multi-talker speech), speech-to-text and speech-to-speech translation, text-to-speech, emotion recognition, audio captioning, and general audio understanding. Our main contribution is not a new architecture but a data-centric training recipe; we use a standard decoder-only backbone initialized from Gemma 4, so that gains can be traced to the data. For speech generation, Walrus predicts low-bitrate discrete speech tokens, and a lightweight token-to-waveform decoder converts them into high-fidelity audio. The recipe is a three-stage data curriculum that moves from broad multilingual data to multi-talker, code-switching, and domain-specific data. At each stage, task-aware and dataset-aware weighting balances tasks with very different token budgets and protects core skills from forgetting. Trained on over 600M samples covering more than 20 tasks and 100 languages, Walrus leads on most multilingual, multi-talker, and code-switching ASR, speech translation, and audio understanding benchmarks, outperforming both open speech language models of comparable size and dedicated task-specific models. On most benchmarks, it even matches or surpasses the $4\times$ larger Qwen3-Omni's performance. Results suggest that data engineering is a primary driver of quality in multi-task speech and audio modeling.

papers.title: Non-Gaussian limit distributions of giant-component sizes in inhomogeneous networks
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the size distribution of giant components in percolation and epidemic spreading models on highly inhomogeneous networks often fails to converge to a Gaussian distribution in the thermodynamic limit. Instead, when appropriately scaled, the distribution converges to a non-Gaussian limit distribution (NGLD). This scaling behavior aligns with the generalized central limit theorem (GCLT), which governs sums of random variables following heavy-tailed distributions. For scale-free networks, the scaling exponent is determined solely by the degree exponent of the network, independently of the control parameter. In contrast, on the Farey graph, a deterministic hierarchical small-world network, the scaling exponent varies continuously with the control parameter.

papers.title: Construction of the $f_4$ meson family
papers.abstract: Motivated by the experimental observations of $f_4(2050)$ and $f_4(2300)$ and the establishment of $a_4$ family, we investigate the $f_4$ family by combining the mass spectrum under the modified Godfrey--Isgur model with two-body strong-decay calculations in the quark-pair-creation model. The common pair-creation strength is fixed by the measured total width of $f_4(2050)$. The mass spectrum analysis and decay information both favor the nonstrange $2\,{}^3F_4$ assignment for $f_4(2300)$. The largely strange $2F$ partner is predicted at $2453$ MeV with a total width of $216$ MeV, decaying mainly into $K^*\bar K^*(1410)$ and $K^*\bar K^*$. Predictions are also given for the $3F$, $4F$, $1H$, and $2H$ flavor pairs. At the adopted mixing angles, the $H$-wave states are more than twice as broad as nearby $F$-wave states of the same flavor. The results of this work may serve as useful guidance for future experimental studies.

papers.title: Aeroelastically Constrained Optimal Path Planning of a Fixed-Wing Airborne Wind Energy System
papers.abstract: Multi-megawatt fixed-wing airborne wind energy systems (AWES) use an aircraft with large, slender wings that deform over the pumping cycle. To harvest maximum energy, the cycle is usually designed by means of dedicated reference trajectory optimization routines. It is well known that such routines rely heavily on the system model and that close alignment between the model and the physical system is required for the results to hold in practice. Nevertheless, the wing is usually treated as rigid and structural limits are respected indirectly through upper bounding of states and inputs. In this work, we directly enforce bounds on the elastic deflection and twist of the wing in the power-maximizing periodic optimal control problem. To that end, we model the wing by root-clamped modes, loaded by strip-theory aerodynamics and by the gravitational and inertial loads of the manoeuvring aircraft. To keep the problem tractable, the modal dynamics are replaced by their quasi-static equilibrium, which enters every discretization interval as algebraic constraints. For a multi-megawatt reference aircraft, the elastic twist near the wing tips reaches $1.03^\circ$ along the optimal rigid-wing trajectory. With a twist limit of $0.6^\circ$, the optimal trajectory delivers $31\,\%$ less mean power than the rigid-wing one, mainly through a lower tether tension during reel-out. Rigid-wing trajectory optimization can thus overestimate the power that the wing limits permit. Forward simulations that retain the modal dynamics demonstrate that the quasi-static deflection and twist deviate from the dynamic ones by less than $2\,\%$ of their limits. This work shows that elastic deformation can be accounted for in the trajectory optimization and that, depending on the wing limits, it can strongly reduce the achievable power.

papers.title: Priority-Aware Firm and Flexible Capacity Quantification for Large-Load Interconnection
papers.abstract: We study how to unlock existing transmission capacity to accelerate large-load interconnection under differentiated quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. We establish an efficient framework to quantify firm and flexible hosting capacities and assess marginal values of grid upgrades. Specifically, we define multiple flexible capacity tiers with differentiated QoS limits and design a two-layer priority rule to allocate curtailment among tiers. We then formulate a mixed-integer chance-constrained model to jointly quantify firm and flexible capacities under QoS and priority constraints. To improve computational efficiency, we derive an equivalent aggregate formulation that eliminates individual curtailment variables and priority binaries without changing the feasible capacity set. Numerical results show the computational advantage of aggregation. Multi-tier flexible capacity increases total admitted capacity by 45.0\% over the firm-only hosting capacity.

papers.title: Efficient control of multi-agent robust MDPs through tensor trees
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a tensor-based framework for controller synthesis of stochastic multi-agent systems under temporal logic specifications that couple the agents, such as one agent reaching its goal only after another agent has reached its own. The agents are modeled as robust Markov decision processes (RMDPs), whose transition probabilities are only known to lie in an ambiguity set, for instance due to abstraction errors, learned models, or uncertain parameters. We show that the decoupled nature of the ambiguity sets allows one to decompose the computation of a lower bound on the satisfaction probabilities into per-agent factors, so that only the per-agent ambiguity sets need to be stored. This leads to improved memory complexity compared to monolithic approaches. We compare our approach with state-of-the-art approaches based on approximate simulation relations and with interval MDP abstractions. On a four-agent ordered reach-avoid benchmark, our approach certifies a lower bound twice as high as the simulation relation- based approach with 20 times less memory, and needs about 200 times less memory than the interval MDP abstraction, even at a resolution with about a million times more joint cells.

papers.title: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms
papers.abstract: We have prepared pairs of atoms at densities exceeding $ 10^{16}/\rm{cm}^3$ corresponding to $n\lambdabar^3>10$ and studied how they interact with light. In this regime, the coherent part of the electric dipole-dipole interaction is larger than the dissipative part, and a single photon emission can transfer large momenta (larger than ten times the single photon recoil) to the atoms. For off-resonant laser light, the atoms are dressed with an electric dipole moment of $\approx$ 1 Debye and interact coherently. This light-induced dipole-dipole interaction has been previously observed only in the far-field mean-field regime. For two atoms, the resonance is shifted by the two-body Lamb shift which is dominated by the near-field part of the dipolar interaction. Dipolar resonance shifts have been observed before only for many atoms interacting with the far-field part of the dipolar interaction. Our work sheds new light on photoassociation processes and paves the way for studying driven quantum systems with strong electric dipole-dipole interactions.

papers.title: Overcoming Dynamic Range Limitations in Computational Hyperspectral Imaging
papers.abstract: Computational hyperspectral imaging offers compact spectral sensing, yet imaging high-dynamic-range (HDR) scenes remains challenging. Accurate spectral reconstruction requires encoded measurements to remain within the calibrated linear-response range and above the noise floor. Due to unequal spectral responsivities across the encoding mask, individual channels reach their reliability limits at vastly different incident signal levels. Measurement reliability therefore depends on both exposure time and encoding channel, making it challenging for a single exposure to preserve spectral information in highlights and shadows simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate a physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework that operates directly in the encoded measurement domain. An analytical reliability prior and learned spatially varying, channel-specific adjustments jointly determine adaptive fusion weights. Measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision further constrains relative channel responses for downstream spectral inversion. The set-wise formulation accommodates varying numbers and configurations of input exposures. We further implement the framework on a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera, incorporating full-field sensor-response characterization and channel-aware reliability gating. Simulated HDR benchmarks show lower reconstruction errors than representative fusion methods, while controlled spectral measurements and practical HDR scenes confirm improved spectral fidelity and extended usable dynamic range. Measurements using an optical-density target further establish a 16.0-dB increase in spectral reconstruction dynamic range relative to the best fixed single exposure.

papers.title: Projection-Based Partial Correlation Inference Beyond Sparsity
papers.abstract: Valid inference for partial correlation in high-dimensional Gaussian models is challenging when the conditioning variables exhibit dense dependence and conventional sparsity assumptions are inappropriate. We develop a target-specific projection framework for estimating and testing a population partial correlation without requiring coordinate sparsity. A population quadratic criterion characterizes the information retained by a linear reduction and is maximized by a one-dimensional projection. Under a rank-one alignment condition, this optimal projection preserves the original partial correlation. To obtain a feasible procedure, we estimate the optimal direction using diagonal ridge regularization on an independent training sample. Under conditions on regularized effective dimension and target-specific ridge bias, we establish a quantitative direction-estimation rate in the covariance-induced prediction norm. We further show that, under alignment, the induced partial-correlation error is second order in the direction error. These results yield oracle equivalence and asymptotic normality for the feasible split-sample estimator, as well as asymptotically valid testing of the original zero-partial-correlation null. Exact finite-sample \(F\)-calibration holds under the projected null. An explicit coordinate-dense Gaussian model verifies the required rates even when the dimension exceeds the sample size. Numerical experiments illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed procedures.

papers.title: Toward Pseudorange-Based PNT with Starlink: A Mock Fused LEO GNSS Implementation
papers.abstract: We present experimental results from Starlink for pseudorange-based positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), emulating a system that fuses a primary communications mission with a secondary low-Earth orbit (LEO) PNT mission. Legacy global navigation satellite system (GNSS) constellations faceinherent vulnerabilities and signal limitations, prompting growing interest in broadband LEO constellations---such as SpaceX's Starlink---for resilient PNT. However, opportunistic use of stand-alone Starlink signals fails to achieve GNSS-competitive accuracy due to frame timing irregularities and reliance on uncorrected poor-quality publicly available ephemeris data. To overcome these limitations, we present a mock implementation of a fused LEO GNSS architecture. Our method extracts time-of-arrival observables from live Starlink Ku-band downlinks and pairs them with high-fidelity, beam-specific orbit and clock models distributed as if provided natively by the constellation operator. In a field campaign, and despite constraints imposed by consumer-grade receiver hardware, the method yields 95% error bounds of 2.33 m horizontally (semi-major axis), 3.37 m vertically, and 11.19 ns in timing, with the actual solution errors falling well within these bounds.

papers.title: CP-MLPs: A Tensor-Rank Theory of Tied and Untied MLP Blocks
papers.abstract: Transformer feed-forward blocks combine several design choices: squared activations, gating, and tied versus untied parameter sharing, whose separate contributions to expressivity remain poorly understood. We introduce CP-MLPs, a tensor framework in which each multiplicative unit contributes a rank-1 interaction with three roles: detecting an input feature, reading a value, and writing to the output. Tied gated blocks such as ReLU$^2$ force the detector and value roles to share the same direction; untied gated blocks such as ReGLU and SwiGLU let them differ. We show that this distinction yields exact, degree-wise tensor-rank separations: untied detector-value units are strictly more width-efficient for indefinite quadratic interactions and role-asymmetric monomials, while tied units are structurally matched to symmetric pure-power targets. The width advantage of untying therefore depends on the target structure. Experiments show loss plateaus below the exact-representation width, but these plateaus alone do not establish a positive approximation gap: arbitrarily accurate approximation is governed by border rank. In trained gated MLPs, untied blocks retain an advantage in selected comparisons at matched input-projection budget. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: MouldIt: Data Efficiency of Multi-Task Temporal Representation Learning in Injection Moulding
papers.abstract: Smart industrial solutions that can address multiple tasks require models that understand the underlying processes. We examine representation learning for modeling the injection moulding process as an example of such solutions. We consider its data efficiency and multi-modal benefit compared to classical machine learning alternatives. To this end, we synthesize a process-informed dataset based on a real reference cycle of an Erlanger Träger part. We then introduce MouldIt, a temporal convolution and attention based variational autoencoder that reconstructs in-mould signals, while classifying parts as acceptable or as one of our synthetic failure modes. We evaluate MouldIt on two tasks, known-class classification and unknown-class detection, across nine dataset sizes in single-modal and multi-modal settings. We compare it with an accept-all baseline and the classical methods k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forests, and principal component analysis, which we adapt to support both tasks. MouldIt outperforms classical methods across both tasks from 4000 cycles in the single-modal setting and from 2000 cycles in the multi-modal setting. It achieves part sorting losses of 6.0 $\pm$ 0.7% and 1.0 $\pm$ 0.3% in the single-modal and multi-modal settings respectively, ranking first across all baselines and a combination of principal component analysis and random forests.

papers.title: Correlations between $\ensuremath{\mitΥ(n\text{S})}\xspace$ production and the underlying event in $\ensuremath{p\!p}\xspace$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
authors: Baidyanath Sahoo (On behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration)
papers.abstract: Recent studies from various experiments at the LHC and RHIC suggest that small collision systems exhibit quark-gluon plasma (QGP) like signatures that were typically observed in large systems. While QGP like signatures have been observed in the soft sector, strong constraints on possible partonic energy loss were established in the hard sector. At the same time, there are multiple pieces of evidence pointing to correlations between hard and soft particle production in proton-proton collisions. The correlations between hard and soft particle production in $pp$ collisions are studied in events with $\Upsilon$ mesons, which provide a valuable hard probe to study such effects. The multiplicity and distributions of kinematic variables of charged particles produced in association with an $\Upsilon$ meson are measured using 139 fb$^{-1}$ of data at $\ensuremath{\sqrt{s}}\xspace = 13$~TeV collected by the ATLAS experiment at the LHC. The measurement is performed separately for the first three $\Upsilon$(nS) states in intervals of their transverse momentum. At low transverse momentum, the associated charged-particle multiplicity is observed to be systematically lower in collisions where $\Upsilon$(2S) or $\Upsilon$(3S) is produced compared to $\Upsilon$(1S), with the difference decreasing as the $\Upsilon$ transverse momentum increases.

papers.title: Investigation of the timing performance of double-sided $p$-type 3D silicon sensors produced by CNM
papers.abstract: We investigate the timing performance and spatial uniformity of double-sided $p$-type 3D silicon sensors produced by the Centro Nacional de Microelectrónica (CNM). Three sensor layouts are studied: hexagonal and square geometries with an inter-electrode spacing of \SI{30}{\micro\meter}, and a hexagonal geometry with an inter-electrode spacing of \SI{50}{\micro\meter}. The sensors are characterized using a \SI{1064}{\nano\meter} infrared laser and a custom two-stage wide-band readout. Measurements with a $^{90}$Sr source are used to establish a minimum-ionizing-particle-like reference for the laser signal. The timing resolution improves with increasing bias voltage for all three layouts. Two-dimensional laser scans are used to study the position dependence of the timing response and to quantify its uniformity. Among the investigated devices, the square \SI{30}{\micro\meter} geometry shows the best overall timing performance at the highest measured bias voltage.

papers.title: Stability Analysis of Single- and Multi-Snapshot ESPRIT
papers.abstract: Spectral estimation seeks to recover unknown frequencies from $T$ snapshots, each consisting of $\Omega+1$ noisy Fourier measurements. Super-resolution refers to the recovery of frequencies whose minimum separation $\Delta$ is smaller than $1/\Omega$. We establish state-of-the-art stability bounds for single- and multi-snapshot ESPRIT when the frequencies form well-separated clumps, with the largest clump containing $n^\star$ frequencies. In particular, for single-snapshot ESPRIT, our error bound scales as $$ \mathcal{O}(\Omega^{-1}\mathrm{SRF}^{2n^\star-2}\cdot\mathrm{Noise}), $$ where $\mathrm{SRF}:=(\Omega\Delta)^{-1}$ denotes the super-resolution factor, provided that the noise level satisfies $\mathrm{Noise}\lesssim(\Omega\Delta)^{2n^\star-2}$. In comparison with the minimax bounds [ arXiv:1904.09186 ] and the computational resolution limits [ arXiv:2003.02917 , arXiv:2211.15208 ], our result shows that single-snapshot ESPRIT achieves the optimal stability scaling in the super-resolution regime. For multi-snapshot ESPRIT, we establish error bounds under both deterministic noise and Gaussian white noise, attaining the best-known SRF dependence under weaker conditions. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical error bounds.

papers.title: Herding with Multiple States: When the Prior Matters
papers.abstract: In sequential observational learning with more than two states, the same information structure and preferences can yield learning for some full-support priors and herding for others. This disproves a conjecture of Kartik, Lee, Liu, and Rappoport (2024, working-paper version). In the counterexample, the cascade region has nonempty interior, yet learning occurs for generic full-support priors outside it. Focusing on information and preferences, we introduce two necessary conditions for learning. Escapability requires that signals can provide arbitrarily strong evidence that any given action is ex post suboptimal; pairwise escapability is its pairwise variant. If escapability fails, herding occurs for some initial prior; if pairwise escapability fails, it occurs for every full-support prior. For a class of environments with interval optimality and monotone likelihood ratios, escapability completely characterizes learning and herding independently of the full-support initial prior. With location-shift signals, this characterization reduces to pairwise distinguishability, a generalization of unbounded beliefs (Smith and Sørensen, 2000).

papers.title: Where does the neutrino Mass Ordering preference come from?
papers.abstract:
After the recent JUNO result, the comparison of the effective mass splittings measured in $ ar
u_e$ disappearance at reactors and in $
u_\mu$ disappearance has become one of the leading handles on the neutrino mass ordering. In this paper, we study which data sets drive the present preference for the ordering, combining JUNO and Daya Bay with $
u_\mu$ disappearance data from NOvA, T2K, MINOS, and IceCube/DeepCore. While the combination disfavors the inverted ordering at $1.9\sigma$, this preference comes from a balance between several small preferences. In particular, the combinations of reactor data with T2K or with NOvA point to opposite orderings. The values of the mass splitting preferred by these two experiments differ by about $3.5\%$, comparable to the difference expected between the two orderings, and thus a shift of this size in a single experiment is enough to reverse the preference. Moreover, in the context of this combination of reactor and $
u_\mu$ disappearance data, further JUNO data would not bring the rejection of the inverted ordering beyond about $3\sigma$, as the comparison is then limited by the precision of the $
u_\mu$ disappearance experiment. Improving the $
u_\mu$ disappearance measurements requires control of the neutrino energy reconstruction, and thus the modeling of neutrino-nucleus interaction physics, at the percent level.

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
papers.abstract: Many-query analyses, in which a computational model is repeatedly evaluated, play an important role in uncertainty quantification and optimization for engineering design. However, many-query analyses can be prohibitively expensive when considering high-fidelity numerical models, especially those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Surrogate modeling replaces costly simulations with cheap approximations, enabling practical uncertainty quantification and design workflows. Machine learning (ML) approaches to surrogate modeling have gained significant traction in the development of surrogate models due to their non-intrusive nature; they do not require access to the underlying simulation code. The Operator Inference (OpInf) approach, in particular, fits reduced operators to state and corresponding time derivative data. However, high-fidelity training data is scarce due to limited computational budgets, and OpInf models trained on such scarce data often exhibit high variance, a critical liability in high-risk engineering design. We propose Multifidelity Operator Inference (MF-OpInf), which reduces this variance by supplementing scarce high-fidelity snapshots with abundant low-fidelity data drawn from coarser discretizations of the same problem. MF-OpInf handles data across varying fidelity levels by utilizing a multifidelity linear regression framework to estimate the reduced operators. Numerical experiments on model PDE problems demonstrate that MF-OpInf predicts PDE solution fields with higher accuracy compared to the high-fidelity-only OpInf with the same computational budget.

papers.title: First-order asymptotic expansions for spectral convergence of normalized graph Laplacians constructed from samples on manifolds
papers.abstract: Under i.i.d. uniform sampling from a closed Riemannian manifold embedded in Euclidean space, we derive first-order asymptotic expansions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of symmetrically normalized graph Laplacians constructed via Gaussian kernels and provide concentration inequalities for the remainder terms. As a direct consequence, we establish the corresponding weak convergence results. Unlike most related works, our analysis does not impose a multiplicity-one assumption on the eigenvalues, thereby extending the applicability of the framework to general manifolds with potentially nontrivial eigenvalue multiplicities.

papers.title: Stochastic evolution of interacting directed strings
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic dynamics of a system of $N$ polymer rings on an infinite cylinder with only excluded volume interaction, using simulations and also analytically. The strings can diffuse in the transverse direction by local Rouse-like moves where an up-kink changes to a down -kink, or vice versa. The motion is biased if the rates of flip are not equal. In the initial state, we start with a step initial condition: all the sites with a positive $y$ coordinate are empty, and the sites with $y \leq 0$ are occupied with a uniform density. We study the scaling form of the density profile in the hydrodynamic limit. The scaling form is a function of $y/\sqrt{t}$ in the unbiased case, and a function of $y/t$ in the biased case. In the unbiased case, in the steady state on a torus, the marginal probability distribution of the positions of the strings on a line with fixed $x$-coordinate is exactly same as that in the ground state of quantum-mechanical spin-less fermions on a line. The biased problem is equivalent to a growing surface in $2+1$ dimension, which is expected to be in the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class.

papers.title: The DIS structure functions $F_4$ and $F_5$ at NLO and their impact on $τ$-neutrino scattering
papers.abstract: We present next-to-leading-order calculations of heavy-quark contributions to the deep-inelastic scattering structure functions $F_4$ and $F_5$ within the Aivazis-Collins-Olness-Tung scheme, implemented in the open-source library APFEL++ and evaluated using CT18NLO parton distribution functions. These structure functions are suppressed by lepton mass effects in light-lepton processes, but become important in $\tau$-lepton and neutrino scattering at facilities such as SHiP, IceCube, and DUNE. We furthermore quantify the direct impact of $F_4$ and $F_5$ on the charged-current $\tau$-neutrino cross section, for the first time presented here, showing they can suppress it by up to $-40\%$ near the kinematic boundary at low $Q^2$ and large $x$.

papers.title: Self-interacting dark matter and neutrino masses from MeV-scale lepton-number breaking
papers.abstract: We show that a scalar whose vacuum expectation value (vev) breaks lepton number at the MeV scale, generating the light-neutrino masses through the inverse seesaw, can also serve as the light mediator of self-interacting dark matter. Dark matter is a pseudo-Dirac fermion whose mass splitting arises from the same vev and is predicted to be proportional to the self-interaction coupling times the vev. A strong central interaction between the dark states requires this splitting to be sizable. The CP-even mediator decays into neutrinos at a rate fixed by the neutrino masses, independent of its mixing with the Higgs boson. Fixing the coupling by the relic abundance and evaluating exact partial-wave cross sections, the model reproduces the velocity dependence of the self-interaction cross section inferred from dwarf galaxies to clusters along a narrow band, $m_s\simeq1.9~{\rm MeV}\times(m_\chi/{\rm GeV})$, extending up to $m_\chi\simeq12$~GeV with a best fit at $m_\chi\simeq7.6$~GeV and $m_s\simeq15$~MeV, and on a sequence of resonant islands of comparable fit quality at higher masses. The cluster data bound the dark matter mass from above, so that the allowed masses extend from about $3$ to $70$~GeV ($95\%$ confidence level), with correlated mediator masses of $6$-$28$~MeV. Combining constraints from the effective number of neutrino species, SN~1987A and direct detection, we find the lepton-number-breaking scale confined to a window of a few hundred MeV and a strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering. The allowed parameter space is testable by future measurements of $N_{\rm eff}$, low-threshold direct detection and the neutrino mass ordering.

papers.title: Optimal Trading Speed on Blockchain
papers.abstract: On blockchain-based exchanges, faster blocks weaken the priority-fee competition among arbitrageurs and shift rents from the block producer to them. Equilibrium liquidity peaks at an interior block speed; beyond a threshold, an active liquidity provider cream-skims and passive capital shrinks. Evidence from the Base Flashblocks upgrade, a tenfold block-speed increase, confirms the predictions. Priority-fee bids decrease sharply and arbitrageurs' net profit rises. The active liquidity provider rebalances faster, avoids toxic flow, and earns a higher profit. Pool depth falls and effective spreads widen despite closer tracking of external prices.

papers.title: Emilia2: A Large-Scale Dataset for Controllable Long-Form Speech Generation
papers.abstract: Generating long-form speech requires models to keep content, speaker identity, turn-taking, and expressive style consistent over time. Yet most open training corpora contain examples lasting only tens of seconds and open long-form benchmarks cover at most two speakers per recording. We introduce Emilia2, a 229K-hour multilingual dataset for controllable long-form speech generation. From in-the-wild data, Emilia2 constructs short utterances, single-speaker long-form speech, and multi-speaker dialogues, preserving transcripts, speaker identities, pauses, and acoustic transitions. Examples longer than five minutes account for 50.0% of single-speaker long-form hours and 66.8% of dialogue hours. To support expressive control, Emilia2 provides natural language instructions for 4.77M examples and nonverbal-vocalization tags for 933K examples. We also introduce Emilia2-testset, 23 hours of bilingual recordings of up to 30 minutes and four speakers, each speaker paired with reference audio. We train autoregressive (AR) and non-autoregressive (NAR) models on Emilia2. Our 0.6B-backbone NAR model achieves the lowest Chinese CER and English WER on TTSD-Eval (5.27%/9.93%) among compared systems, while our AR model is on par with Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-VD on InstructTTSEval (zh/en: 76.2/78.3 vs. 77.1/77.9). These results validate Emilia2 as a comprehensive data foundation for long-form speech generation and minute-scale expressive control. Demo: this https URL .

papers.title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
papers.abstract: Mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides exhibit high Li conductivity, but the relationship between oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport remains unclear. Here, crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials are used to examine $\mathrm{Li}_yM\mathrm{O}_x\mathrm{Cl}_{6-2x}$ ($M$ = Nb and Ta [Group 5] and $M$ = Ti, Zr, and Hf [Group 4]). Increasing oxygen content changes isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and subsequently more highly connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks. In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over $x \approx 0.67$--1.5, where the Li sites form a three-dimensional percolating network. Potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations reveal that fast Li-ion transport requires a low-dimensional framework supporting long-range migration through undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, together with similar energies across Li sites. Finally, we perform fine-grid compositional search, which identifies $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{0.67}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.67}$, $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{0.75}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.5}$, $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$, and $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$ as stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities of up to $\sim 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{s}$. These findings establish how oxygen content controls framework and Li-ion transport, guiding the design of lithium oxyhalide electrolytes.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of asymptotic traveling waves in a time-fractional bistable reaction-diffusion equation
papers.abstract: We study asymptotic traveling waves for a reaction-diffusion equation with a Caputo time derivative. For general $C^1$ bistable imbalanced nonlinearities, we prove the existence of an asymptotic traveling wave connecting the two stable states. The asymptotic wave speed is unique, and the asymptotic profile is strictly increasing and unique up to translation. The proof uses continuation from a stationary front and the sliding method. For a cubic nonlinearity, we also derive an asymptotic formula for the speed near the balanced case, with an explicit leading coefficient. Finally, we perform numerical simulations to compare the speed predicted by the asymptotic formula with the front propagation speed in the original equation.

papers.title: Nuclear medium and final state interaction effects in $η$ production induced by $ν_μ(\barν_μ)$ at SBN and DUNE energies
papers.abstract: We investigate nuclear-medium modification and final-state interaction in charged- and neutral-current $\nu_\mu(\bar{\nu}_\mu)$-induced $\eta$-meson production on $^{12}\mathrm{C}$ and $^{40}\mathrm{Ar}$. The nuclear medium is described within a local density approximation, incorporating in-medium modifications of the $N^*(1535)$ resonance, which is known to play the dominant role in $\eta$ production through its $N \eta$ decay channel. The subsequent propagation and absorption of the $\eta$ meson in the nucleus are simulated using a Monte Carlo approach. We find that nuclear-medium modifications and final state interaction lead to substantial suppression of the production cross section, highlighting the importance of nuclear effects in interpreting $\eta$ production data. Our results provide valuable theoretical input for the analysis of $\eta$-production at the ongoing SBND and MicroBooNE experiments and the forthcoming DUNE experiment.

papers.title: Topological flat bands from nonlinear periodic motion
papers.abstract: We use the Lax formulation of classical integrable systems to characterize the topology of nonlinear periodic orbits. For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom, we express the chiral-symmetric Lax operator along a periodic orbit in a frequency basis. Energy conservation makes both bands of the resulting tight-binding model exactly flat. The harmonic oscillator corresponds to a fully dimerized topological Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, while nonlinearity generates long-range hopping through higher harmonics. In the symmetric double well, the winding number changes as intrawell periodic orbits give way to an orbit spanning both wells, and the zero-energy edge mode of the semi-infinite chain disappears. We derive the edge-mode profile and show that its localization length diverges logarithmically as the separatrix is approached. At the separatrix, the period and the hopping decay length diverge while the band gap remains finite; this singular limit of the periodic motion allows the winding number of the infinite frequency chain to change. Canonical quantization of the Lax operator also connects the chiral winding numbers to supersymmetric quantum mechanics: for a bound system on the real line with simple turning points, their sum over all periodic orbits at a common positive energy equals the Witten index. We also apply the construction to periodic nonlinear waves through traveling-wave reductions. The finite-period winding number becomes undefined in their solitary-wave limits.

papers.title: Fractional-Order Hybrid SIR Forecasting of COVID-19 in Bangladesh and the United States: Memory Effects and Out-of-Sample Evaluation
papers.abstract: Fractional-order epidemic models are often justified by memory, yet whether memory improves forecasts is rarely tested out of sample. We extend a hybrid SIR framework, in which a daily transmission rate is reconstructed from reported cases and then forecast, to Caputo fractional order $\alpha\in(0,1]$. We prove well-posedness, conservation, positivity and a linearized threshold at disease-free states, and derive a Grünwald-Letnikov reconstruction that reduces exactly to the integer-order one at $\alpha=1$. Our main theoretical result shows that for $\alpha<1$ the influence of the unknown initial infectious count vanishes, but no faster than $t^{-\alpha}$; after 332 daily steps it is about $4.4\times10^{8}$ times larger at $\alpha=0.9$ than at $\alpha=1$. In out-of-sample forecasting over 27 weekly origins, the effect of memory depends on the setting. In Bangladesh the integer order gives the lowest error for linear and constant-rate forecasts in 47 of 48 settings. In the United States, where reported cases reached about 18% of the population, a fractional order lowers the linear forecaster's error in all 12 comparisons in 2021 but raises the constant-rate forecaster's, with no difference significant after Holm adjustment. Against standard baselines, the SIR-based linear forecaster was more accurate than the classical SIR model and a neural network without SIR structure, and competitive with ARIMA: in the United States the fractional linear forecaster had the lowest error of all methods (seven-day MAPE 7.54% against 9.14% for ARIMA), whereas in Bangladesh ARIMA had the lowest MAPE, with no significant difference from ARIMA in either country. The choice of a fractional order should rest on out-of-sample evidence rather than in-sample fit.

papers.title: Revisiting the dispersions and quality factors of nanoshell plasmons
papers.abstract: The dispersions and quality factors of a metallic nanoshell's plasmons may be readily tuned by varying the thickness of the nanoshell. This is because 1. Thickness determines the hybridization between the two nanoshell boundaries and 2. Thickness affects the electronic surface scattering rate and, therefore, the non-radiative decay rates of the plasmonic resonances. We find that prior theoretical works, focused primarily on the thin-nanoshell and retarded regimes, obtained qualitatively incorrect results for both the plasmonic dispersions and the associated plasmonic quality factors. Some of these errors have been pointed out in subsequent works, though the corrected results have not been reported, to our knowledge. Beyond obtaining the correct results (correct dispersions and quality factors as a function of nanoshell thickness), we scrutinize the assumption (used by many prior works) that Matthiessen's rule may be used to combine the effects of bulk and surface-mediated plasmonic scattering processes. To do so, we extend prior work by Dingle to the nanoshell geometry. Although we find qualitative agreement with the Matthiessen's rule approach, we find that Dingle's theory systematically predicts higher quality factors across the range of nanoshell thicknesses we consider.

papers.title: Drive and damping govern resonant electron energy redistribution in a kinetic model informed by helium discharges
papers.abstract: Energetic electrons exchange energy with electrostatic waves in low-temperature plasmas, but wave amplitude alone does not determine the direction or cumulative effect of that exchange. We analyse nonlinear electron redistribution using a single-mode kinetic model parameterized by published helium-discharge measurements. Frequency and pressure comparisons are combined with a controlled damping scan and explicit particle-current and energy diagnostics. Across the frequency cases, the inferred resonant drive varies by a factor of 2.7 while background damping varies by only about 9%. Reducing pressure from 33.3 to 10.66 Pa at 37 MHz increases the net drive by a factor of 2.24. In the damping scan, the peak wave energy and residual parallel-energy deficit both decrease by approximately 93%, consistent with quadratic field-amplitude scaling at the reported endpoints. An integrated energy identity connects retained wave energy, background loss and distribution recovery, and distinguishes cessation of wave growth from reversal of energy transfer. Quantitative timescale and directional-distribution tests define the connection between this reduced model and discharge kinetics. The analysis provides a common interpretation of resonant redistribution, coherent current and energy exchange, together with observables for testing that interpretation in kinetic simulations and phase-resolved measurements.

papers.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
papers.abstract: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

papers.title: Hidden interfacial magnetism in RuO$_2$ heterostructures revealed by a superconducting spin switch
papers.abstract: RuO$_2$, once the flagship altermagnetic candidate, is now believed to be nonmagnetic in the bulk, yet weak, static and spatially inhomogeneous magnetism emerges at its surfaces and interfaces. Where this magnetism resides, what stabilises it, and whether it is connected to these states remain open questions. Here we address these questions at the Nb/RuO$_2$ interface using a superconducting spin switch. A GdN/Nb/RuO$_2$ trilayer allows interfacial exchange-field alignment to tune the superconducting transition temperature of Nb, probing interfacial magnetism inaccessible to conventional magnetometry. The switch reveals a hidden magnetic subsystem, which we attribute to a thin RuO$_x$ redox layer formed as Nb scavenges oxygen from RuO$_2$. This layer behaves as a weak and magnetically hard ferromagnet with vacancy-induced anisotropy. Furthermore, supercurrent amplifies the switching efficiency, making the probe sensitivity tunable in situ. Superconducting spin switches thus emerge as a quantitative low-temperature probe of hidden magnetism at buried interfaces.

papers.title: Joint Air Corridor and BS Coverage Planning for Large-Scale High-Density Low-Altitude Aerial Networks via Channel Knowledge Maps
papers.abstract: This paper studies the joint air corridor and base station (BS) coverage planning problem for high-density low-altitude aerial networks supported by terrestrial cellular infrastructures. In the considered system, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operate within a structured air corridor planned over a grid-based airspace, and each BS serves selected corridor grid cells by sharing its communication resources among all UAVs therein. Each BS's traffic load depends on both the number of covered corridor cells and the UAV density, thereby affecting the communication rate available to each UAV. We exploit the channel knowledge map (CKM) to characterize the channel gains between BSs and candidate airspace cells and evaluate desired signals and inter-cell interference for environment-aware offline planning. Based on CKM, we jointly optimize the corridor layout and BS coverage to minimize a weighted objective balancing corridor length and the supportable average UAV density along the entire corridor, subject to minimum communication rate requirements for all UAVs along the air corridor. The joint design is formulated as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP), which can be optimally solved using off-the-shelf solvers. For large maps, we develop a scalable suboptimal algorithm based on Lagrangian relaxation and A* search. Specifically, we incorporate BS resource constraints into A* corridor search via Lagrangian relaxation, and then jointly optimize BS coverage and UAV density along the generated corridors under the original rate constraints. Numerical results demonstrate the benefits of the proposed joint design in supporting high-density UAV operations and show that the proposed algorithm obtains high-quality solutions with substantially reduced computation time.

papers.title: Development of a versatile modular system to study the ablation and plume expansion in a thin film
papers.abstract: Time-resolved investigation of laser ablation of thin films requires stable, repeatable, and efficient experimental environment. Conventional approaches often rely on multiple laser-ablation shots acquired at different delay times to reconstruct the temporal evolution of the process, thereby assuming shot-to-shot reproducibility. This work presents a novel modular experimental setup that addresses these challenges and enables a systematic pump--probe study of laser--matter interaction. The setup provides reliable single-pulse measurements with controlled sample positioning inside the high vacuum chamber, as well as integrated data recording, which improves redundancy and ease with which experiments can be performed. Further, the setup serves as an advanced diagnostic tool for investigating the time evolution of laser--matter interactions, ablation dynamics and laser-produced plasmas in a single laser shot, in various configurations with a temporal resolution better than 15 ns. Using this capability, we show that for a fixed ablation geometry, the transient reflectivity and transmission response depends strongly on the probing side, indicating that probing direction is an independent diagnostic variable whose omission can lead to incomplete or misleading picture of the ablation dynamics. This experimental technique can advance the understanding of surface modification and plume expansion, which are relevant to fundamental studies and also for range of applications, including laser cleaning of tokamak viewports and mirrors, pulsed laser deposition (PLD), surface structuring and laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT), among others. The present setup is versatile enough to perform these studies under different ablation configurations without implementing major changes in the experimental configuration.

papers.title: The unified bound dark energy--bound dark matter model confronted with DESI DR2, ACT and SPT-3G, and the Unite supernovae measurements
papers.abstract: The unified bound dark energy-bound dark matter (BDE-BDM) model derives the whole dark sector from a single supersymmetric SU(3) dark gauge group, whose lightest meson is the dark energy and whose heavier bound states, created with a velocity $v_c$ when the group condenses, are the dark matter. Because the condensation scale $\Lambda_c$ is fixed by gauge-coupling unification, the dark-energy sector has no free parameter beyond those of $\Lambda$CDM, and the dark-matter sector adds only $v_c$. We confront the model with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), the Planck, ACT DR6 and SPT-3G D1 CMB spectra, the combined ACT and SPT CMB lensing and the Unite supernovae. The measured condensation scale, $\Lambda_c=43.74\pm0.11$ eV, lies inside the window $34^{+16}_{-11}$ eV predicted by unification, and the dark energy thaws without ever crossing the phantom divide, reaching $w_0=-0.9267\pm0.0003$ today; it thus reproduces the DESI distances that $w_0w_a$CDM fits with a phantom past. BDE-BDM gives the best fit to the DESI DR2 BAO of the four models, reducing $\chi^2_{\rm BAO}$ by 20% with respect to $\Lambda$CDM, more than $w_0w_a$CDM, and over the full data combination it is statistically equivalent to both $\Lambda$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM, with $\ln B=-0.50$ and $-0.15$, while having two fewer dark-energy parameters than $w_0w_a$CDM. Within bound dark energy, bound dark matter is moderately preferred over cold dark matter, $\ln B=+3.2$ with $\Delta\chi^2=-9.0$, mostly from the CMB. The data now constrain the bound velocity from both sides, $v_c=0.37\pm0.14$, which places the free-streaming cutoff of the matter power spectrum at $k_{1/2}=1.49\,h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and lowers the amplitude of structure to $S_8=0.807\pm0.007$. Future high-redshift and Lyman-$\alpha$ forest data, together with growth and lensing measurements, will therefore provide the decisive tests of the unified dark sector.

papers.title: Metamorphic testing of learned AC optimal power flow surrogates reveals representation dependence
papers.abstract: Evaluating a learned AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) surrogate on one grid serialization cannot show whether its accuracy depends on that encoding. We test this dependence with thirteen metamorphic relations, each specifying when a transformation is valid and how to compare its outputs. Our audit covers 17 model and pipeline configurations: two released trained checkpoints and 15 random-weight architecture or mechanism controls. Every configuration violates at least six relations, even at reporting tolerances ten times tighter or looser. For GridSFM-Open v1.1, source inspection and intermediate-tensor interventions point to an indexing bug and three noncanonical or numerically unstable preprocessing choices; a repaired checkpoint remains untested. In a separate case500 training experiment, augmentation lowers transformed-view error in three of four models and median discrepancy and constraint-violation P95 in all four. These benefits depend on the training protocol: some relations worsen, and every evaluated prediction remains AC infeasible. A GPU/CPU eigensolver mismatch accounts for most of the large raw-Laplacian-baseline gain. We recommend reporting representation consistency alongside accuracy, feasibility, and cost. These results establish neither deployment readiness nor universal invariance.

papers.title: Investigating Composite Modeling in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Design
papers.abstract: Scientific design often requires balancing competing objectives that are expensive to evaluate through experiments or simulations. Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) addresses this challenge by using probabilistic models to guide the selection of promising designs. In many applications, tunable inputs map to observable intermediate responses, which are then combined through known functions to compute the final objectives. Prior work on Bayesian optimization of composite functions shows that learning from these intermediate responses, which we call Composite modeling, can substantially improve sampling efficiency in single-objective optimization, compared to methods that condition only on black-box observations of the objective function. The benefits of Composite modeling in MOBO, however, remain understudied. In this work, we study the benefits of Composite modeling in MOBO and investigate the factors driving variation in its gains. We first establish single-objective conditions under which intermediate observations provide no additional predictive information beyond objective values, where composite and black box methods use the same warped Gaussian process prior.
