Across more than 30,000 participants from ABIDE (autism spectrum disorder), ADNI (Alzheimer's disease), and the UK Biobank (depression), IC-GNN achieves the highest performance compared with 15 baseline methods. We further demonstrate that these individualized communities are reproducible within scans and across sessions, and carry predictive power on their own. Furthermore, IC-GNN identifies disease-related shifts in community organization that align with established literature, highlighting a promising approach for modeling individualized community structure for disease prediction and biomarker discovery.

papers.title: INTENT: Out-of-Sample, Out-of-Time, and Cold-Start Evaluation on User Event Sequences
papers.abstract: Banks now train foundation models on ordered sequences of customer events such as transactions, app sessions, and authorizations. Deployed, such a model predicts forward in time, often for customers and merchants absent from training, yet each is evaluated on private data, so no two can be compared. Public benchmarks for such sequences rarely test a period the model has not seen; recommendation studies usually hold out each user's last events instead. We present INTENT (INTEraction, Novelty, and Transfer evaluation for next-action prediction), a public benchmark that scores a model in seven cells defined by whether the user, the period, and the target item appeared in training. An audit of 59 public dataset families retains five datasets; the most common defect is the lack of a calendar timestamp that orders events. No date lies within the time span of all five datasets, so each is split at its own cutoff, chosen by one rule fixed before any model is evaluated. Summed over the datasets, every cell holds at least 111,769 users. In reference results the cell determines the best model: a transformer leads on seen items after the cutoff but scores zero on new items, a variant that embeds item metadata helps mainly on MicroLens, and repeating the user's last item leads on new items in four of five datasets. This parameter-free control also shows that on three datasets most of the score lost after the cutoff reflects changed behavior rather than the model. The pipeline, the cutoff rule, and the per-cell user counts are publicly available.

papers.title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem
papers.abstract: We solve the ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schrödinger operator. The proof uses the intrinsic symplectic structure of the dual center of Ge--Jitomirskaya [28] and extends the Kotani--almost-reducibility strategy of Ge--Jitomirskaya--You [30] from two-dimensional centers to arbitrary finite center dimension.

papers.title: Control Barrier Functions for Counting Tasks in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly operate in dynamic environments and execute complex tasks that require coordination, posing significant computational challenges. Counting tasks, which require a minimum number of agents to satisfy a given condition, arise naturally in such systems. Examples include surveillance tasks, where at least m drones must continuously monitor a critical area, and emergency-response tasks, where at least m robots must converge to an incident location. The identities of the agents assigned to these tasks may change dynamically depending on their states, input bounds, and individual objectives. In this work, we propose a control barrier function (CBF)-based framework for enforcing counting invariance and counting convergence tasks, without explicitly assigning agents or enumerating all possible subteams. We develop a recursion-based method for constructing differentiable CBFs for counting tasks. The resulting CBF constraints are incorporated into quadratic programs, enabling online controller synthesis. Numerical experiments demonstrate scalability to large multi-agent systems, while a multi-drone emergency-response case study illustrates the satisfaction of counting tasks.

papers.title: Monochromatic or rainbow triangles in the triangular lattice
papers.abstract: Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus conjectured that for each non-equilateral triangle $\operatorname{T}$, every 2-coloring of the plane contains a congruent copy of $\operatorname{T}$ with monochromatic vertex set. We confirm this conjecture for triangles with a ratio $\sqrt{7/3}$ between two side lengths. We further prove that every coloring of the plane, regardless of the number of colors used, contains congruent copies of 36 specific triangles with monochromatic or rainbow vertex sets, partially answering a question of Gehér, Sagdeev, and Tóth. Both these results were obtained by considering finite configurations on the triangular lattice.

papers.title: Combinatorial optimization with bounded subdeterminants
papers.abstract: We take a first step toward a broader study of classical combinatorial optimization problems through the maximum subdeterminants of their standard integer programming formulations, yielding new positive results for several famous (NP-hard) problems. An integer matrix is totally $\Delta$-modular if every square submatrix has determinant of absolute value at most $\Delta$. For every fixed $\Delta$, it has been known that maximum clique, maximum stable set, and minimum vertex cover can be solved in polynomial time on instances for which the coefficient matrix of the natural formulation is totally $\Delta$-modular. We extend this list by showing that the same holds for many other problems, including the weighted versions of maximum cut, the traveling salesman problem, feedback vertex set, odd cycle transversal, dominating set, max 2-sat, induced matching, and cluster vertex deletion, as well as for $k$-colorability and graph isomorphism. Our proofs reveal several new ways in which bounded subdeterminants impose combinatorial structure: they bound the size or maximum degree of the input graph, bound packings of cycles and other obstructions, or yield decompositions into tractable graph classes such as forests, chordal graphs, graphs of bounded treewidth, and graphs of bounded linear mim-width.

papers.title: Mars Seed: A Reference Architecture for Biomanufacturing Habitats from Martian Resources
papers.abstract: Human exploration of Mars will require enormous quantities of materials for the first crewed missions and substantially more for permanent habitation, making flexible and scalable technologies for in situ resource utilization (ISRU), including biological ISRU, of significant interest. However, no existing mission architecture quantitatively evaluates whether in situ biomanufacturing can realistically deliver materials at the scales required for human settlement. Here, we present Mars Seed, an end-to-end reference architecture for using biomanufacturing to produce bioplastics at scale entirely from in situ resources on Mars. We provide a complete analysis of a space bioprocess in which feedstocks are generated entirely from Martian resources, converted biologically into polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) bioplastic, and purified to produce material suitable for constructing human habitats. We show that the upfront power and upmass costs of deploying the equipment required for this bioprocess are recovered within two synodic periods relative to Earth-shipped alternatives. Further, because the process relies entirely on feedstocks sourced from Martian materials, production can continue until equipment failure without requiring additional materials from Earth, enabling scalable conversion of local resources into useful materials. Mars Seed demonstrates that biological ISRU can be mass- and power-competitive with Earth-shipped alternatives, establishing biomanufacturing as a practical component of Mars mission architecture rather than an aspirational capability.

papers.title: Numerical Investigations on Bitumen Liberation from Oil Sands Lump
papers.abstract: The dynamic liberation and digestion of viscous oil-solid aggregates under turbulent flow is a critical transport phenomenon in multiphase chemical processes, including slurry transport, soil remediation, and industrial extraction. A primary industrial application of this phenomenon is oil sands hydrotransport, where pipelines are widely utilized to simultaneously transport and extract bitumen from lump ore. However, optimizing operating conditions requires a fundamental understanding of the localized hydrodynamic mechanisms governing detachment. To address this, a three-dimensional (3D) Eulerian-Eulerian (E-E) CFD approach coupled with k-omega SST turbulence model has been utilized to investigate bitumen detachment dynamics from complex solid matrices. Six numerical cases were analyzed across lump diameters (D) of 4 and 5 cm and particle Reynolds numbers (Re_p) between 2000 and 4000. The simulation results reveal that bitumen liberation is a shear-driven process, occurring only when the shear stresses exerted by the flow on the lump surface exceed a critical threshold value. The bitumen liberation rate increases with higher Re_p and smaller D, due to enhanced local shear forces and reduced particle shielding. Based on these mechanistic insights, a novel semi-empirical shear-driven model was formulated. The proposed model demonstrates excellent predictive accuracy when validated against experimental liberation data, with an error less than 8.3%. Overall, these findings clarify the fluid-particle interactions governing bitumen detachment and offer a robust, physics-based tool for predicting recovery efficiency in industrial hydrotransport operations.

papers.title: Elicitation of the parameters of a multi-criteria sorting model
papers.abstract: Multiple-criteria decision aiding (MCDA) proposes models and methods for different types of decision problems such as choice, ranking or sorting. Such models involve various parameters that must be elicited. In the elicitation process, all necessary information has to be taken from the decision-maker. For this, several direct and indirect elicitation methods are suggested in the literature. In this work, we concentrate on direct elicitation: we aim at providing a rigorous elicitation procedure for the parameters of the Non-Compensatory Sorting model (NCS), which has been characterized by an axiomatic analysis. A basic version of the NCS model is considered, i.e., a model with two categories and no vetoes. The parameters are the set of sufficient coalitions of criteria and the profile separating the two categories. Regarding the sufficient coalitions, we propose several questioning algorithms that engraft questions on classical graph exploration algorithms such as depth-first search. Such algorithms are implemented and evaluated by simulation. For eliciting the limit profile, we design a questioning algorithm using dichotomy. Questioning algorithms can be optimal in the worst case or on average. An optimal algorithm in the worst case has been proposed by Hansel in the framework of monotone Boolean functions. We implement and evaluate this algorithm as a variant of the depth-first search approaches. Regarding optimal questioning strategies on average, we evaluate decision trees for up to four criteria. On the other hand, we assess how more general is NCS as compared to MR-Sort, a particular case of the NCS model in which sufficient coalitions can be represented by additive weights.

papers.title: The Left Ripple of Byte-Pair Encoding: Certified Lookbehind for Every Dictionary
papers.abstract: Berglund and van der Merwe formalized byte-pair encoding and bounded how far an appended string can change a tokenization, leaving the converse open: how far can a string prepended on the left change it, which dictionaries make that ripple infinite, and can it be computed efficiently when finite? We answer all three for every dictionary. The origin radius, how far a prepend can change covering spans, is decided with radius certificates by a product of two runs of the automaton that guesses the final tokens, in time polynomial in the dictionary written out, and it is infinite exactly when one periodic word has two canonical tilings with no common boundary. Under their ordering condition it is infinite exactly when some rule (t, t) finds its two copies adjacent at its own stage, and such a rule makes any dictionary infinite. A finite radius makes every window of a width read off the radii have a cut, and the radius is finite exactly when such cuts are dense. The token machine completes for every dictionary, and the tokenization is subsequential, extending what Berglund, Martens and van der Merwe proved for proper ones under one pass per rule. A streaming tokenizer emits after every symbol exactly the tokens that no continuation changes, in polynomial time, answering a question of Dalirrooyfard and Ye. Boundedness of the label measure, the edit distance of the token sequences, is decided for every dictionary in polynomial time as well, and under the ordering condition the largest distance one edit causes over dictionaries of m rules lies asymptotically between m^2/10 and m^2/2. GPT-2's merge table carries 244 effective self-pairs, so its origin radius is infinite from the forty-second merge on, and that of cl100k, o200k and Llama 3 from their first. Every measured number is its program's output, and what is not executed is named.

papers.title: Aster: A Flexible and Robust Collection of Numerical Tools for N-Body Problems
papers.abstract: The Aster library is an open-source collection of numerical tools designed for large-scale gravitational N-body simulations. Aster provides a flexible environment to its users, enabling it to be used in the analysis of a broad range of astrophysical problems. The library implements efficient force calculation algorithms, including a spatial tree solver optimized with coordinate-dependent identifiers, which has been fine-tuned for both CPU and GPU architectures. Despite its high degree of modularity, many parts of the library have been optimized with SIMD instructions, heavy parallelization, and support on dedicated hardware. Aster also offers a wide variety of numerical symplectic integrators, such as SABA (from first to tenth order), the classic leapfrog algorithm, and the more advanced Wisdom-Holman (WH) integrator, while also providing a vast collection of mathematical tools, e.g., post-newtonian expansions (1PN, 2PN, 2.5PN), data collection and graphing systems, a built-in renderer, and presets for faster instantiation of large amounts of bodies. In this work we will discuss in depth the details of each module as well as the results of several performance- and accuracy-related tests, probing the library's capabilities in different physical applications.

papers.title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English
papers.abstract: Languages of India need 1.6 to 14 times as many tokens as English on GPT-4o's tokenizer for the same content, which makes them more expensive and slower to serve. We train tokenizers from scratch on human-written text in about 200 languages. Havon v3 is a byte-level BPE tokenizer with 262,144 tokens and a pre-tokenizer that keeps combining marks with their letters and chunks scripts written without spaces. On FLORES-200 devtest it needs fewer tokens than GPT-4o's o200k_base on all 25 languages of India (median 0.74 of GPT-4o's count) and on 172 of 204 languages, but 7% more on English. Havon v4 adds a second, multi-word training stage (SuperBPE) to v3. At exactly GPT-4o's vocabulary size of 200,019 tokens, v4 needs 6.1% fewer tokens than GPT-4o on English and fewer on 161 of 204 languages and all 25 languages of India (median 0.74); at the same size, v3 needs 9.4% more on English and wins on 133. With 262,144 tokens, v4 needs 9.6% fewer tokens on English and fewer on 182 of 204 languages, and with 524,288 tokens it needs fewer on 203 of 204. The gains are largest for English, Hindi and the Romance languages; scripts without spaces, such as Khmer, Burmese and Tibetan, gain little and lose subword merges. Havon v5 replaces v4's Python-only code sample with permissively licensed code in 15 languages: on code it needs 1.03 to 1.22 times GPT-4o's tokens, against 1.11 to 1.29 for v4, while keeping all 25 languages of India (median 0.74, all significant under a sentence-level bootstrap) and English (0.94). These are compression results only: we have not yet evaluated a model trained with v4 or v5.

papers.title: The Indic Token Tax in 2026: Measuring Tokenizer. Disparity and Its Cost for the Languages of India
papers.abstract: Commercial language model APIs bill per token, so a tokenizer that needs more tokens for the same content in one language makes that language more expensive, slower, and able to fit less text in a fixed context window. We measure this disparity for nine public tokenizers, including those of GPT-4, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5, DeepSeek-V3, Mistral-Nemo and four Sarvam models, on all 25 languages of India available in FLORES-200 (2,009 professionally translated sentences aligned with English) and on 13,732 human-translated Hinglish-English social media pairs from PHINC. On GPT-4o's tokenizer the same content needs between 1.57 times (Hindi) and 5.01 times (Odia) the tokens of English, and 13.7 times for Santali in Ol Chiki script; GPT-4's tokenizer needs up to 12.8 times. Sarvam-30B/105B is the only third-party tokenizer that stays below 2.6 times on every language (median 1.53). In an illustrative scenario using official list prices accessed on 5 November 2026 and stated assumptions, a support bot handling 100,000 chats a month on GPT-4o would cost about INR 56,640 in English and INR 102,829 in Marathi; these are estimates, not measured production costs. Against an openly licensed Hindi and Marathi morphological segmentation set, no tokenizer places more than 35% of its word-internal boundaries on morpheme boundaries (boundary F1 at most 0.48). In a companion paper we present a tokenizer that reduces this tax. Code, pinned artifacts and raw token counts are available at this https URL .

papers.title: Continuous-Time Set-Transformers for Asynchronous WiFi-IMU Indoor Localization
papers.abstract: Indoor localization commonly combines WiFi received signal strength indicator (RSSI) fingerprints with inertial measurements. However, these sensor streams are sampled asynchronously at different rates; therefore, observations rarely align in time and may be missing or stale. Most existing methods resample the data onto a shared clock and process each modality using a separate branch. We instead present a continuous-time transformer that represents observations as an unordered set of timestamped tokens. Each token encodes its measurement, modality, and elapsed time since acquisition. A single attention block jointly fuses information across modalities and time, avoiding both resampling and modality-specific branches while remaining invariant to token order. During training, we randomly mask entire modalities and individual observations, enabling the model to operate under missing or outdated inputs. We validate the modality-specific encoders on their respective benchmarks and evaluate the fused model on both simulated and real datasets, including a crosssession dataset collected on unseen days. The proposed approach improves upon an open WiFi fingerprinting baseline under cross-session drift, remains competitive with learned fusion and dead-reckoning baselines, and degrades gracefully as observations become missing or stale. These results suggest that a single continuoustime transformer provides a practical framework for indoor localization from asynchronous sensors.

papers.title: SNIF: a Self-Navigator Intelligent Filter correcting off-center and spin-history artifacts in quasi-random radial MRI
papers.abstract: For self-navigation and self-gating in MRI, self-navigators are extracted from the complex values of the k-space center, called DC-signal, through a temporal frequency analysis. However, this signal often carries artifacts. This paper introduces a Self-Navigator Intelligent Filter (SNIF) that models the physical origin of the k-space center artifacts to properly estimate them and thus more accurately remove them. The artifact affecting the DC-signal $S_{DC}$ generally has two main origins: the jitter of the k-space center (''off-center artifact'') and the cumulative history of the spins (''spin-history artifact''). Both add noise-like artifacts to the signal. The off-center effect can be modeled as a perturbative signal $S_0$ and the spin-history effect as a convolution kernel $h$ so that the measured DC-signal is $S_{DC} = S_m + S_0 \star h$, where $S_m$ is the motion-related component which effectively contains the expected self-navigators. Methods to compute $h$ and $S_0$ were developed, which gives the possibility to extract $S_m$ from $S_{DC}$. They were implemented and evaluated on thoracic UTE datasets acquired on a healthy volunteer. Qualitative visual comparison and quantitative spectral analysis of the DC-signal before and after SNIF demonstrate that the method improves both the accuracy and the precision of the extracted respiratory and cardiac self-navigators. By considering the physical origin of the DC-signal artifacts, SNIF makes both respiratory and cardiac self-navigators more sensitive to motion, which supports finer MRI motion tracking.

papers.title: Beyond the Document: Compiled Context and Governed Agents for Any Work Product
papers.abstract: A document preserves the visible result of professional work but often discards the research, calculations, assumptions, evidence, and authorization boundaries behind it. We study a different unit of delivery: a Portable Agent Format (PAF) package that carries a work product together with compiled context, evidence, provenance, and rules for subsequent interaction. To test whether this context remains useful beyond the process that produced it, we evaluate four new packages, created after the hosted and offline readers were fixed: an investment proposal, fund research, financial-statement analysis, and an engineering incident review. Two packages were produced by specialized agents and two through a general-purpose assistant's packaging skill. Across 400 frozen questions and 12,000 evaluated responses, a hosted governed reader succeeds on 96% of questions versus 86% with instructions plus raw-file retrieval (Holm-adjusted p < 10^-7). On the 260 answerable questions per condition, success is 94% versus 79%; the gap varies by package. Source-material chat and instructions alone reach 48% and 74% overall. A separate 0.8-billion-parameter offline reader succeeds on 69% overall, but 54% on answerable questions. Its -1 response rate is 2.9%, combining materially wrong and unauthorized answers, versus 56% with the source and instructions alone. Ablations suggest advantages for the integrated selector and package-adapted writer, without isolating representation from training effects. The same run exposes a failure: offline retrieval resolves none of the 40 historical-record questions in one financial-data package. These findings support treating compiled knowledge as part of the delivered work product, while leaving independent standards interoperability and end-to-end governance conformance unproven.

papers.title: Entropy: the Route from the Gaussian Field to the Statistical Mechanics of the Thermal Radiation
papers.abstract: Maximum Entropy or canonical typicality applied to the electromagnetic field can provide starting points for arriving at the Bose distribution of the photon numbers of thermal radiation, but they rely on statistical postulates whose experimental testability is controversial. Here we start from experimentally verifiable assumption of Gaussianity of the electromagnetic field. We analyze the field by projecting it onto orthonormal time-frequency basis functions with unitary bandwidth duration product that represent field's orthogonal time-frequency modes. Through the Glauber-Surashdan representation, we see that the joint density operator of the modes in the photon number basis factorize into diagonal density operators with geometric coefficients of individual modes, while the mean photon occupations of the modes remains still unknown. The independent imposition of Clausius' relation on each one of the entropies and energies of the modes leads to Bose's mean photon occupancy. Thus, our main claim is that for the first time Bose statistics is recovered in the paper under explicit, experimentally verifiable statistical assumptions, without assuming any statistical postulate that is not directly experimentally verifiable. From the mean occupation numbers, the Boltzmann distribution of the energy of matter particles of the material that generates/absorbes the radiation is then derived by retracing in the backward direction the Einstein-Feynman detailed balance.

papers.title: Opacity of Discrete Event Systems under Sensor Attacks
papers.abstract: Many information control problems in discrete event systems can be addressed using strong opacity, weak opacity, and non-opacity. These opacities depend on observations. If cyber attackers can attack sensors (or observation channels), then opacities will change. An opaque system may become not opaque, or a not opaque system may become opaque. Therefore, it is important to investigate opacities under sensor attacks. In this paper, we consider opacities under sensor attacks for two settings. The first one is the user has prior knowledge of sensor attacks in which the opacities are called as W-CA-opacities. The second one is the user has no prior knowledge of sensor attacks, and opacities are called as N-CA-opacities. For the former, we construct an augmented automaton that integrates the information of sensor attacks and then converts W-CA-opacities into classical opacities to solve the verification problem. For the latter, we construct the observers for the given system without sensor attacks and with sensor attacks, respectively. We then do the parallel operation on these two observers to obtain a method of verifying N-CA opacities. Furthermore, by adopting the detector technique, we find polynomial algorithms for verifying weak opacity and non opacity for both settings.

papers.title: Explanation-Aware Fairness Beyond Output Parity: Joint Output-Attribution Regularization for Medical Image Classification
papers.abstract: Output-level fairness does not constrain whether demographic groups rely on similar predictive contributions in representation space. For a nonlinear encoder with a linear head, we show that outcome-conditioned output score disparity equals the signed sum of feature attribution differences across subgroups by allowing small prediction gaps to arise through cancellation effect. We test whether an attribution disparity penalty complements output-level equalized odds based fairness surrogates. Across 960 DINOv2-LoRA models on HAM10000 and Harvard-GF datasets for gender and race fairness, attribution augmentation increases utility-fairness trade-off performance for hypervolume in six different settings with paired 95% confidence intervals and relative gains of 1.49-10.57%. Under a predefined utility constraint, augmented model families also achieve 9.0-38.7% lower equalized odds difference, lower attribution disparity, and reduced cancellation ratio while preserving predictive utility. These results support attribution fairness as a complementary explanation-aware constraint on output fairness.

papers.title: Mean-field BSDEs with jumps under quadratic-exponential growth
papers.abstract: This paper studies the well-posedness of mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short) with Poisson jumps, where the generator has quadratic growth with respect to $Z$ and exponential growth with respect to $U$, where $(Y,Z,U)$ denotes the solution of this BSDE. First, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of local solutions to mean-field backward stochastic differential equations with jumps (BSDEJs, for short) by using a fixed-point argument. Then, based on these local results, we discuss the solvability of global solutions in the following two cases: in the first one, the generator has linear growth with respect to $Y$ and the corresponding marginal distribution $\mu_1$; and in the second one, the generator has subquadratic growth with respect to the marginal distribution $\mu_2$ and linear growth with respect to the marginal distribution $\mu_3$, corresponding to $Z$ and $U$, respectively. Finally, by employing a Girsanov transformation we establish a comparison theorem for mean-field BSDEJs under quadratic-exponential growth conditions.

papers.title: Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: For real affine hyperplane arrangements, we prove Lam's determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix restricted to bounded chambers. The proof combines Lam's comparison of twisted intersection forms with the period determinant formula of Varchenko, Loeser-Sabbah and Douai-Terao. For normal crossing arrangements, we introduce the taut path algebra and the chamber intersection algebra and establish a Koszul duality between them, yielding an explicit multivariate formula for the inverse Varchenko matrix. After specializing the parameters to $q$, its restriction to bounded chambers is a scalar multiple of the $q$-intersection matrix, proving a determinant conjecture of the authors. We also discuss how the Koszul duality results generalize to affine oriented matroids.

papers.title: The Gene Is Not the Gate: Conceptualizing the Semantic Genome of Quantum Software
papers.abstract: Quantum software spans applications, program representations, compilers, runtimes, and hardware-facing control. Existing abstractions describe these artifacts and layers, but they do not capture the semantic responsibilities that must remain valid as a computation is transformed across the stack. This limits systematic reasoning about cross-layer correctness, evolution, and reuse. We present QGenome, a semantic foundation for quantum software genomics. We define a quantum software gene as a typed, reusable responsibility characterized by an explicit contract, execution context, concrete expressions, and supporting evidence. QGenome organizes genes across five software strata and ten responsibility families grouped into computational semantics, coordination, realization, and assurance. Typed genes compose into pathways and genomes through dependency, refinement, provenance, and phenotype relations, enabling responsibilities to be traced across alternative implementations and execution contexts. We illustrate the taxonomy using representative public artifacts across the quantum software stack and define principles for contextual validity, genome evolution, environmental adaptation, and capability expression. Rather than presenting a complete taxonomy or an automated extraction technique, QGenome establishes a falsifiable framework and a concrete research agenda for gene mining, lineage recovery, cross-layer regression testing and repair, and evidence-grounded quantum software agents.

papers.title: Reliable Computation of the $L_{\infty}$-Norm of Linear Time-Invariant Systems Depending on One Parameter
papers.abstract: The $L_{\infty}$-norm of a linear time-invariant system is a central quantity in robust control, used in robust stability tests, stability margins, and $H_{\infty}$ controller design. Physical models depend on parameters, such as masses, stiffnesses, or gains, so the $L_{\infty}$-norm becomes a function of these parameters. This computation reduces to studying the real critical points of a plane algebraic curve whose coefficients depend on the parameters. Previous approaches based on cylindrical algebraic decomposition describe the $L_{\infty}$-norm on the whole parameter space, but their cost grows very quickly with the number of parameters. In this paper, we propose instead to compute a generic parametrisation of the solutions, valid outside an explicitly characterised set of non-generic parameter values. In the case of one parameter, this parametrisation is obtained by interpolation from a certified solver for the non-parametric case. The resulting algorithm is fully certified, relying on a priori bounds and multimodular computations rather than on Gröbner bases. It is illustrated on examples from the robust control literature.

papers.title: State-constrained optimal control with the theory of functional connections: squared slacks and junction exponents
papers.abstract: For optimal control problems with an affine state constraint, we combine the theory of functional connections (TFC), which writes every function satisfying prescribed linear conditions as an explicit expression in terms of a free function, with the squared-slack substitution $b - a^\top x(t) = s(t)^2$. Every trial trajectory then satisfies the endpoint conditions and the path constraint identically. The accuracy depends on the regularity of the slack function at the junctions with a boundary arc. Along an optimal trajectory, the constraint residual vanishes like $(t_1 - t)^m$, where the junction exponent $m$ is equal to the order $p$ of the constraint if and only if the $p$-th derivative of the constraint jumps at the junction, and thus a single polynomial slack converges algebraically. The \emph{multiple-arc TFC method} that we introduce, with unknown junction times and with residuals $(t_1 - t)^m \sigma(t)^2$ on the free arcs, represents the optimal trajectory exactly and converges geometrically when the arcs are analytic. In a linear-quadratic class, an exact cost identity shows that the cost of every trial trajectory is an upper bound of the optimal cost. We compare both approaches with direct collocation and indirect shooting on the Bryson-Denham problem, on a rendezvous problem with an approach corridor and on the six-dimensional atmospheric reentry of a space shuttle with three state constraints.

papers.title: SpatialSR: Spatial Resolution-Centric Pipeline for Arbitrary-Scale Remote Sensing Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Although remote sensing image arbitrary-scale super-resolution (RSI-ASSR) methods support reconstruction at arbitrary or continuous scales, they predominantly condition on the relative scale factor and have not sufficiently investigated the absolute spatial resolution itself as a reconstruction prior, thereby disregarding the inherent spatial context of objects, which frequently leads to spatial-related distortions and compromised performance in downstream remote sensing applications. To address these challenges, we introduce SpatialSR, a SRe-centric arbitrary-scale RSISR method that leverages the spatial resolution (SRe) of remote sensing images (RSI) as an essential prior for super-resolution reconstruction. Distinct from existing SR methods, SpatialSR aims to restore high-resolution remote sensing images with a target SRe (typically set to 0.1m/pixel to align with the metadata of commonly used downstream task datasets). Specifically, we design a Spatial Resolution Estimation Module (SREM) to estimate the SRe of low-resolution (LR) images, thereby dynamically determining the required arbitrary scaling factor. Next, we employ a pretrained SRe-to-image diffusion model to extract SRe-specified texture-style codes, which are further incorporated into a carefully designed Resolution-aware Style Consistency Module (RSCM) to constrain the SRe-aware texture consistency of reconstructed images. Furthermore, to overcome the high computational expense inherent in diffusion-based SR methods, we wrap the iterative diffusion process as a Trajectory Consistency (TC) loss, which enables comparable reconstructed texture quality of the generative model in SpatialSR within a single step. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed SpatialSR achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on commonly used RSISR and downstream (image classification and segmentation tasks) datasets.

papers.title: MICRO: A Surgery-Phase Retinal Image Rigid Registration Benchmark and One-Step Frequency-Structure Similarity Registration Learning
papers.abstract: Precise multimodal retinal image rigid registration (MRIRG) is essential for aligning cross-modal vessel structures, offering critical guidance for ophthalmic surgery. Despite its significance, the advancement of MRIRG is hindered by the lack of publicly available multimodal retinal image rigid registration datasets spanning various ophthalmic surgery phases (e.g., preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative). To address this issue, we introduce the MICRO dataset, a large-scale MRIRG benchmark, comprising 1,365 cross-modal retinal image pairs with standardized annotations across all ophthalmic surgery phases. Moreover, existing deep registration methods achieve competitive MRIRG results via a two-step segmentation-then-detection framework, but segmentation quality heavily constrains their performance. We argue that this dependency stems from an implicit need for keypoint topology constraints, which have not been exploited for MRIRG through a one-step registration framework. Inspired by the above analysis, we propose a novel One-step Frequency-Structure Similarity Registration (OFS2Reg) learning framework for MRIRG that leverages the potential of cross-modal vessel structure similarities to construct keypoint topology constraints under a shared detection network. To be specific, OFS2Reg applies a well-designed frequency-guided structure preservation descriptor to construct coarse keypoint topology constraints in descriptors by highlighting significant vessel structures. Additionally, we develop a new cross-modal vessel structure similarity learning method that refines cross-modal keypoint topology constraints to precisely align pixel-level cross-modal vessel structures by leveraging cross-modal vessel structure similarity priors.

papers.title: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes
papers.abstract: Let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For $r>0$, we characterize the inequality $h_q(n)\ge r$ in terms of cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For $k,m\ge2$, let $I_q(j)$ count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $j$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. If $k$ is prime or $m\ge2\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}I_q(j)+2$, we prove that a cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$ linear perfect code of length $\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ exists if and only if $\gcd(m,q-1)=1$. When this condition holds, we also obtain \(h_q\!\left(\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}\right)=k(m-1).\) Restriction of scalars gives the same criterion for every $m\ge2$ when $q$ is odd, $q+1$ is a power of two, and $k=2p$ with $p$ prime. We also show that $h_q(q^k+1)=k$ exactly when $q$ is even, for every $k\ge1$.

papers.title: Proportional Neuro-Impulsive Control of SISO LTI Systems
papers.abstract: This paper explores a controller that is at the crossroads of neuromorphic, i.e., spike-based, and impulsive control systems. The controller consists of a single integrate-and-fire-like neuron that generates an input proportional to the system output when the neuron variable reaches a threshold. We prove that any static output-feedback stabilizable single-input single-output (SISO) linear time-invariant (LTI) plant can be made semi-globally asymptotically stable (sGAS) in closed loop with the proposed neuro-impulsive controller. This improves on existing fixed-amplitude neuromorphic controllers, which only achieve practical stability, but at the price of using graded spiking inputs. Moreover, we provide an algorithm for choosing appropriate controller parameters given a set of admissible initial conditions. A numerical example of an inverted pendulum linearized around its upright equilibrium illustrates the method.

papers.title: Trust, but verify, audit and attribute: a human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced research results
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems now produce research results in bulk: in October 2026 a single laboratory released more than 700 AI-generated mathematics manuscripts, only part of them with machine-checked proofs. Such volumes will be checked mostly by AI agents that call specialised software. A passing check certifies only the artefact that was checked. For proofs translated into the proof assistant Lean, it has been shown that this artefact may state something other than the author's text, and that deciding whether a translation is faithful is undecidable in general. The human researcher therefore stays in the loop, and human and AI contributions must be recorded. We propose a domain-independent, human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced results. Validated, agent-usable tools with different grounds of trust check the results; a fidelity audit asks whether each check addressed the claim as stated; the human decides at fixed points; and a dialog report attributes the work to the human and to the AI. We describe two automatic implementations of the tool layer, for mathematics (Wolfram Language, MATLAB, Lean) and statistics (Python and R), and run the mathematical one on a two-claim example. An ambiguous claim was split into two readings, one refuted and one proved.

papers.title: Code-Grounded Agentic Explanations for Static Analysis Vulnerability Findings
papers.abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools surface vulnerabilities early and their verdicts are rule-based and auditable. Yet developers routinely dismiss findings they cannot interpret. Large language models can supply the missing explanation, but designs that also hand the model the detection give up the auditability that makes static analysis defensible. We keep detection with the analyser and give the model only the explaining. A preliminary user study with 20 participants and a workshop with 19 practitioners yielded five requirements. Guided by these we redesigned SAFE, an open-source IntelliJ IDEA plugin that explains findings from any analyser reporting in the Static Analysis Results Interchange Format. It tiers explanations by demand, ties them to the reported data flow, and replaces the single-prompt backend with an agent that must consult the repository and the rule that fired before answering. A within-subjects crossover experiment with 24 participants compared the redesign against its predecessor. Perceived usability rose from 77.3 to 85.0 on the System Usability Scale. Actionability gained most among the explanation-quality items, the aspect both earlier studies flagged as weakest, and the odds of a correct remediation were 2.6 times higher. Triage accuracy and time per finding were indistinguishable, which we read as uninformative rather than as equivalence. Trust was the one measure that did not move, and the closing interviews indicate that grounding made findings easier to understand rather than easier to believe. Participants also drew a boundary no requirement anticipated, wanting the tool to find and explain while they judge and apply.

papers.title: On the Concavity of Rényi Entropy and Rényi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the concavity of Rényi entropy and Rényi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for Rényi orders $\alpha\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.

papers.title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks
papers.abstract: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. We evaluate Robo-MLT against four policy baselines and a VLM-based monitor baseline on blood gas analysis and blood sample tube sorting, with 50 nominal configurations per method and 20 sample-removal configurations. Robo-MLT achieves task success rates of 82\% and 70\%, exceeding $\pi_{0.5}$ by 30 and 22 percentage points, respectively. After an operator removes the sample being handled, the system revises the remaining plan and continues processing the other samples. These results indicate that, under the evaluated conditions, explicit workflow monitoring makes long-horizon laboratory manipulation more reliable and recoverable.

papers.title: Point defects and primary radiation damage in Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys from molecular dynamics
papers.abstract: Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are candidates for nuclear structural applications. We used molecular dynamics with the EAM-21 potential, stiffened at short range, to study five HEAs that have been irradiated experimentally: Fe37Ni34Cr16Mn13 (ES1), Fe35Ni35Cr15Mn15 (P35), Fe46Ni22Cr15Mn17 (Y3), Fe27Ni28Cr18Mn27 (Kumar) and Fe30Ni30Cr10Mn30 (C30). They were compared with pure Ni, Fe60Ni40, the Fe70Ni10Cr20 model alloy of 316L, and Fe50Ni34Cr16, which is ES1 with Mn replaced by Fe. We calculated stacking fault energies, threshold displacement energies, point-defect formation and migration energies, and 1015 displacement cascades from 5 to 40 keV at 300 and 823 K. The stacking fault energy follows the Ni content: 19-44 mJ/m^2 in the alloys and 113 mJ/m^2 in Ni. Compared with the Mn-free alloys, the HEAs have lower threshold displacement energies (48-56 against 64-74 eV) and lower dumbbell formation energies, and Mn is the element most transported by interstitials. All the concentrated alloys leave about the same number of Frenkel pairs, 56-72 at 40 keV, half the number in Ni. At 40 keV, 54-58% of the interstitials are in clusters in the HEAs, against 67-71% in Fe60Ni40, Fe70Ni10Cr20 and Fe50Ni34Cr16 and 82% in Ni. At the same cluster size, clusters of 4-12 interstitials are faulted about half as often in the HEAs, and this does not follow the stacking fault energy. The surviving interstitials are enriched in Mn in the HEAs and in Ni in the Mn-free alloys, and depleted in Cr. The results support direct loop formation in cascades in Fe60Ni40 and Fe70Ni10Cr20 and less of it in ES1.

papers.title: Spectral-Domain Information Geometry of Stationary Covariance Models: Gaussian and Elliptical Extensions
papers.abstract: This paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance structures. We begin with the infinite-dimensional setting, where stationary covariance structures can be characterized without finite-window boundary effects. By formulating the covariance structure as a bilinear form on a suitable class of test functions, we establish its spectral representation and show how finite-dimensional Toeplitz covariance matrices arise as restrictions to nested observation subspaces. For zero-mean proper complex Gaussian wide-sense stationary (WSS) processes, we show that the normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric. In logarithmic spectral coordinates, this metric becomes the standard $L^2$ inner product, yielding an explicit Fisher--Rao distance that is also recovered as the asymptotic normalized affine-invariant Riemannian distance between Toeplitz covariance matrices. We then extend the framework to elliptical observation models by separating global covariance scale from shape. The shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and is characterized by a dimension- and radial-model-dependent coefficient. We derive a condition under which this coefficient converges to its Gaussian value as the observation dimension tends to infinity. The resulting limiting spectral-shape geometry is the centered $L^2$ geometry of log-spectra and is invariant to positive rescaling. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence results and the recovery of the Gaussian shape coefficient.

papers.title: CapBuddy: Efficient Physical Memory Management for Capability-based Resource-controlling Microkernel
papers.abstract: Capability-based resource-controlling microkernels securely multiplex hardware by exposing low-level resource abstractions guarded by capability systems. Such a design helps provide an application-specific resource management policy to achieve high performance without sacrificing security. However, the misuse of capability-protected secure abstractions can introduce performance overhead in user-level resource management, affecting the runtime performance of dynamic applications in emerging scenarios. In this paper, we focus on the secure abstraction of physical memory in microkernels with capability-based resource management delegation to investigate an appropriate design for dynamic memory management. We propose CapBuddy, an approach to building an efficient buddy system on capability-protected secure abstractions of memory, to bypass the performance overhead of the capability system by offloading functionalities that can run offline from the critical path of serving a memory request. We implemented a prototype system on the seL4 library OS, and the evaluation results show that our approach improves the performance of the seL4 user-level buddy system by 20 to 54.5 times and achieves the same order of magnitude as Linux. Further burst experiments evaluate CapBuddy's scalability and show that it maintains low median allocation latency as the number of concurrent clients increases.

papers.title: The Ordinary Days of Extraordinary Blazar 3C 454.3
papers.abstract: The blazar 3C 454.3 (z = 0.859) is one of the brightest and most variable flat-spectrum radio quasars in the sky. Here, we present a multi-wavelength analysis of this enigmatic object in its quiescent states during June 2022 and May 2023 coincident with its first X-ray polarimetric and hard X-ray observations with International X-ray Polarimetric Explorer (IXPE) and Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array (NuSTAR). Though no X-ray polarization was detected, NuSTAR detected the source on all occasions during this period. We generated five broadband spectral energy distributions (SEDs)of the blazar using quasi-simultaneous observations taken with the Fermi-Large Area Telescope, NuSTAR, and Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. The hard X-ray flux measured by NuSTAR exhibited mild flux variations. The SEDs were modeled with a one-zone leptonic emission framework using the JetSet package. The optical-ultraviolet spectrum of 3C 454.3 revealed an upturn which we reproduced with the standard accretion disk model. The X-ray to gamma-ray spectrum of 3C 454 was found to be well explained by the external Compton (EC) process with the seed photons provided by the BLR and accretion disk. These results provide intriguing clues about the multi-wavelength behavior of 3C 454.3 during its quiescent activity state.

papers.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studies document changes to evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

papers.title: Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps
papers.abstract: HI intensity mapping is a promising probe of the large-scale structure of the Universe, but is limited by foregrounds and instrumental systematics. For the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) L-band data, it is found that emission line stacking measurement reveals a type of systematics related to the instrument beam. Using simulations with a full-sky electromagnetic beam model, we show that the chromaticity and sidelobes of the MeerKAT beam modulate the frequency-smooth foreground emission and introduce oscillating structures that persist after foreground removal. The beam rotates with respect to the sky between two types of scans, and combining datasets with different beam orientations before foreground cleaning makes the residuals stronger. In MeerKLASS L-band data, processing these two types of scans separately significantly suppresses the oscillating residuals while preserving the stacked HI signal. The ratio of the HI signal amplitude to the systematic fluctuation amplitude increases by 81%. We find an oscillating structure in PCA mode 11 in our previous data processing, but simply removing this mode does not improve the stacked spectrum due to the signal loss. Our strategy can help mitigate spectral ripples that are induced by the beam in future MeerKAT and SKA-Mid surveys.

papers.title: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses
papers.abstract: Caustics provide a universal connection between classical ray focusing and structured wave patterns. We theoretically investigate this connection in non-linear matter waves focused by a short-duration anharmonic lens acting on a Bose-Einstein condensate. A semi-classical description shows how the leading cubic aberration transforms the harmonic focal point into a fold caustic, whose local wave field is described by an Airy canonical integral. Three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that mean-field interactions modify the near-focus density and longitudinal momentum distribution, producing a secondary momentum-space feature absent from the non-interacting evolution. We quantify the information about the effective interaction strength carried by the $1D$ distribution using classical Fisher information and maximum-likelihood estimation. We obtain a relative uncertainty of $2.7\times10^{-3}$ for a sample of $10^5$ detected points along $z$. These results establish a framework for studying interaction-driven departures from single-particle caustic universality and promote matter-wave lenses as a sensitive probe of mean-field interactions.

papers.title: Explicit resonance and bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays
papers.abstract: We investigate the bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays. For general multiple-delay systems with a quadratic potential, we establish a Hamiltonian formulation with a \(P_{n,m}\)-boundary condition and derive explicit Maslov index and nullity formulas. For the special case of two distributed delays, we extend the analysis to general nonlinear potentials. These results yield explicit resonance criteria, bifurcation conditions, and Rabinowitz type and Fadell-Rabinowitz type alternatives for $\mathbb{R} $-distinct solutions.

papers.title: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have demonstrated strong generalization in robotic manipulation, yet processing dense visual tokens often incurs high inference latency. Visual token pruning offers a practical way to reduce this cost, but identifying a compact set of tokens that preserves reliable action generation remains challenging. Existing methods largely rely on static or immediate heuristic cues to estimate token importance. We introduce APS-VLA, a framework that learns visual token selection from robot demonstrations while keeping the pretrained VLA backbone frozen. A lightweight Decision Influence Estimator scores tokens conditioned on current visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioception. Its training combines two complementary signals: action supervision matches both the full-input policy predictions and demonstrated actions, while an auxiliary visual transition objective uses demonstrated actions to predict subsequent visual features from the selected representation. At deployment, the estimator performs a single hard selection and packing step before the policy's native action-generation procedure; the auxiliary predictor is removed. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO and with $\pi_{0.5}$ and XR-1 on RoboCasa365 demonstrate inference acceleration with modest changes in task success. Across five real-world tasks on two dual-arm platforms, APS-VLA reduces mean policy inference latency from 137.25 to 93.25 ms, achieving a $1.47\times$ speedup with an average success rate of 61%, compared with 60% for the unpruned baseline. Together, these results support APS-VLA as a modular, plug-in framework for efficient robotic control across VLA architectures, preserving the underlying policy parameters and native action-generation procedure.

papers.title: Artifact Filtering versus Artifact-Compensated Training in JPEG to JPEG AI Recompression
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of recompression of images from JPEG to JPEG AI format. We show that direct recompression from JPEG to JPEG~AI trained on uncompressed images is accompanied by the preservation of the JPEG image artifacts in the resulting JPEG~AI image. In order to avoid it, we evaluate an approach where an artifacts removal neural network is first applied to the input JPEG image as an external pre-filter. However, in this case, the processing time is increased by 29 times. Therefore, we propose an artifact-compensated training for JPEG AI and show that it is able to combine pre-filtering against target distortions with efficient compression without increase in the processing time.

papers.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

papers.title: TypedInk: Knowing When Not To Draw
papers.abstract: Can a scientific figure generator know when it does not have enough evidence to draw? Complete-source illustrators map a finished methodology section to a schematic, or a table to plotting code, and are never asked this question because their input is assumed complete. The research record is rarely that complete: an outline, a draft paragraph, a table, or a one-sentence intent, in any combination, and painting measured numbers with an image model when the table is missing is a hallucinated result. TypedInk infers a figure type from {diagram, plot, plate} from a possibly incomplete source and dispatches to the renderer that can honor that type's evidence contract, refusing dispatch when the contract cannot be met. On the six gold plots in TypedFigBench (5 views, n=30), TypedInk's code path inks every gold table token when a table is observed (12/12), refuses the 12 hidden-table views instead of inventing numbers, and marks 6 intent-only views illustrative, with no execution failures. An always-draw coder with no such gate inks 30/30 charts, including all 18 with no table, and recovers zero gold numbers on any of them; two vision-language raters (not humans; human replication is future work) still judge those always-draw charts submittable 17/36 times, against TypedInk's refusal 0/36 times. A diagnostic field ablation of the type router (16 illustrations, 5 views each, n=80) locates where this failure would originate if unchecked: an outline alone yields type accuracy 0.31 and sends every gold plot into an integrity violation, and a chat-model planner narrows but does not close the gap (overall accuracy 0.85, still integrity-failing on 25% of outlines). Diagram-label recall is 0.47 on the full record and 0.19 on an outline. Gold plates are typed at dispatch (oracle integrity-fail 0.00) and rendered as stills.

papers.title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development
papers.abstract: Coding agents increasingly receive UI screenshots as part of bug reports, yet degraded image quality - caused by low resolution, compression artifacts, or small rendered text - can prevent them from identifying the relevant UI elements and source files. Vision-language models become less reliable as image quality deteriorates, while OCR-assisted approaches may propagate recognition errors from degraded inputs. Both approaches are limited when the visual evidence required for localization is no longer clearly observable in the query screenshot. We propose augmenting coding agents with repository-rendered reference images: crisp screenshots generated from the same codebase that the agent is tasked with modifying. These references provide readable visual evidence of the application's UI while preserving the current, potentially bug-containing implementation state. Because they are generated from the available repository rather than requiring a known bug-free version, they can be produced automatically for reproducible application states without manual image annotation. We evaluate the approach on a controlled benchmark derived from SWE-bench Multimodal by injecting visual UI bugs into a real web application. We vary screenshot degradation and reference-image provision and measure whether the coding agent identifies the correct source file. The results show that reference images improve file localization especially for degraded image quality, increasing the gold file match rate under fourfold downsampling with JPEG compression. We confirmed with further analysis that the proposed approach recognizes text approximately 12 percentage points better than language biased OCR under the same degradation.

papers.title: Representations of the Loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a new family of non-weight modules $\Omega(\lambda,\zeta,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\sigma, h)$ over the loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra $\mathcal{G}$, which is a Takiff-type extension of the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro algebra. We establish criteria for irreducibility, determine their isomorphism classes, and classify all $\mathcal{G}$-modules that are free of rank one. Moreover, we determine all self-extensions of these modules: for every such module $M$, $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{U(\mathcal{G})}(M,M)\cong \mathbb{C}^{6}$, and we construct explicit $1$-cocycles realizing every cohomology class. Every nonsplit self-extension of a simple module is indecomposable of composition length two. Restricting these modules to the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro subalgebra $\mathcal{H}$ yields new $\mathcal{H}$-modules. Among them the $\sigma$-type modules $\Psi(\lambda,\zeta,\sigma,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,h)$ constitute a new family with no counterpart in the non-loop or non-Takiff case. For the degenerate case $\sigma=0$, we establish criteria for irreducibility and isomorphism, and describe certain maximal submodules and their simple quotients. Finally, we construct and classify a new class of tensor product $\mathcal{H}$-modules.

papers.title: GRAP: Gender Rubric-Aware Probing for Analyzing Gender Bias in LLMs
papers.abstract: As LLMs increasingly mediate everyday interactions, subtle gender biases in open-ended responses pose growing societal risks. Existing probing methods have two key limitations: they rely on fixed-format tasks, such as pronoun resolution or occupation association, that alignment-tuned models can easily handle; and they compare raw group-level rubric scores, ignoring per-dimension variance and obscuring which bias dimensions reliably distinguish gender groups. We introduce GRAP (Gender Rubric-Aware Probing), a framework that uses a lightweight logistic probe to identify the most discriminative bias dimensions from responses scored across 10 rubric dimensions, operating task-agnostically on open-ended instruction following.

papers.title: Multi-TeV vector dark matter in the $U(1)_X$ Higgs portal model
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy-mass vector dark matter within the framework of the $U(1)_X$ gauge Higgs portal vector model, by jointly integrating experimental constraints from relic density measurements, direct detection searches, and indirect detection observations alongside the perturbative criterion to derive bounds on the model parameter space. Within the weakly interacting massive particle scenario, we assess the relative contributions of $s$-channel and $t/u$-channel processes to thermal dark matter annihilation. For parameter configurations lying in the $s$-channel resonance region, each fixed value of the scalar mixing angle $\sin\alpha$ corresponds to a well-defined upper limit on the heavy dark scalar mass $m_{h_2}$. This upper limit decreases monotonically with increasing $\sin\alpha$, with a critical threshold of $\sin\alpha \lesssim 0.05$ beyond which perturbative constraints entirely exclude the full resonance corridor. By contrast, the non-resonant parameter regime dominated by $t/u$-channel annihilation processes is found to be excluded for $m_V \simeq 1$ TeV and above under the combined joint constraints from relic density requirements and perturbative consistency. Our results indicate that the perturbative consistency of the scalar sector, enforced via the two-loop renormalisation group equations, imposes bounds on the parameter space in the heavy mass regime that are comparable to, and in some benchmark regions more restrictive than, current experimental limits. Nevertheless, even under the application of these stringent perturbativity constraints, the model still admits a viable set of parameter points spanning a broad multi-TeV mass range.

papers.title: Understanding-First AI Engineering: Purposes, Reference Architecture, and Architectural Patterns for Human Understanding
papers.abstract: AI systems can produce reliable results without developing human understanding. However, human understanding remains valuable for shaping subsequent AI-supported work, forming preferences, governing collective choices and satisfying curiosity, even when human participation is unnecessary for correcting errors. We propose understanding-first AI engineering, which treats purpose-specific human understanding as a first-class design principle guiding requirements, design and operation. The purposes of understanding are organised into four complementary rationales: reflective agency, effective action, collective governance and epistemic value. A reference architecture connects production, verification, use, and learning and exploration through shared records, supporting understanding through explanation and participation. Five candidate architectural patterns guide choices about parallel learning, explanatory models, goal exploration, audience-specific views and distributed expertise. Qualitative scenario analysis of two hypothetical use cases demonstrates how the purpose classification, reference architecture and selected patterns guide investigation, participation and decision processes while retaining operational controls. The cases illustrate design consequences and limitations rather than establish empirical effectiveness. The approach makes human understanding an explicit engineering commitment whose justification need not depend on improving the original AI task.

papers.title: Cluster-weighted modeling for count data with excess zeros and mixed-type covariates
papers.abstract: Count data may exhibit excess zeros, within-group overdispersion, and heterogeneous relationships between the response and its covariates. Conventional zero-inflated regression models typically impose a single count-regression structure, whereas Poisson count components cannot accommodate residual within-component overdispersion. We propose a zero-inflated negative binomial cluster-weighted model that combines a structural-zero component with multiple negative binomial regression components and jointly models the response and mixed-type this http URL establish sufficient conditions for identifiability of the proposed model and its Poisson counterpart and develop an expectation-maximization algorithm for estimation. Numerical studies demonstrate improved regression coefficient estimation and clustering performance relative to the Poisson counterpart under within-component overdispersion.

papers.title: ChipOmni: A General-Purpose AI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
papers.abstract: Electronic design automation (EDA) workflows remain highly fragmented, requiring engineers to coordinate heterogeneous representations, specialised software tools, and iterative verification across multiple design stages. Although large language models have brought more general reasoning and code-generation capabilities to EDA, many existing approaches remain focused on isolated tasks and struggle to plan, verify, and repair designs autonomously within executable engineering environments. Here we introduce ChipOmni, a knowledge-enhanced, context-evolving AI agent framework for EDA. ChipOmni integrates multimodal understanding, dynamic planning, multi-agent collaboration, and verification-driven tool interaction into a unified autonomous system. By continually incorporating feedback from external engineering tools, the framework maintains an evolving task context, integrates domain knowledge, and iteratively refines intermediate designs. Across benchmarks for analog circuit, RTL, testbench, and formal-assertion generation, ChipOmni improves multiple task-specific measures over the evaluated baselines and solves all 30 AnalogCoder-Pro tasks. In a long-horizon case study, ChipOmni advances a natural-language RISC-V specification through three design levels to a micro-SoC GDSII layout that passes physical sign-off, without human intervention after initialization. Together, these results show that ChipOmni can coordinate verification-driven design across heterogeneous tasks and sustain long-horizon engineering workflows, advancing a shift from fragmented, tool-centred processes towards agent-centred, closed-loop systems.

papers.title: Two-Tier Task Offloading for Satellite-Assisted Marine Networks: A Hybrid Stackelberg-Bargaining Game Approach
papers.abstract: The proliferation of maritime activities has spurred the emergence of numerous computation-intensive and delay-sensitive marine applications and services. Given the inherent rationality, selfish nature, and limited computational abilities of marine devices, devising effective strategies to incentivize their participation in task processing become a critical challenge. In this paper, we investigate the satellite-assisted marine multi-access edge computing (MEC) and propose a two-tier task offloading scheme through a hybrid Stackelberg-Bargaining game approach to enhance offloading efficiency and maximize the utility of marine devices. Specifically, for the underwater acoustic communication, we consider the scenario where multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), managed by maritime autonomous surface ships (MASSs), upload their collected data using non-orthogonal multiple access(NOMA) to optimize channel utilization. For the data transmission above the sea surface, we consider the scenario where a low earth orbit satellite (LEOS) functions as a space edge server to provide computing services, and MASS offloads workloads to LEOS through frequency division multiple access(FDMA) to prevent co-channel interference. we define the utility of AUVs, MASSs and LEOSs, and model the offloading process between AUVs and MASSs as a Stackelberg game, while representing the offloading interaction between MASSs and LEOSs as a Bargaining game. Additionally, we propose efficient algorithms to optimize AUV offloading strategies and MASS pricing strategies, while refining the bidding strategies for both MASSs and LEOSs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms significantly outperform benchmark schemes in achieving optimal solutions.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the buckling eigenvalue-ratio conjecture in every dimension
papers.abstract: In 1999, Ashbaugh formulated the conjecture that the ball maximizes the ratio of the first two clamped buckling eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean space. We disprove this conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$ by constructing smooth connected domains with finitely many interior holes. The key observation is that a zero-value constraint on a concentric sphere close to the boundary of a ball increases the first two eigenvalues by the same relative amount to first order, whereas their ratio increases strictly at second order. A quantitative surface penalty and logarithmic cutoffs transfer this strict inequality to smooth perforated domains. The construction gives explicit geometric parameters depending only on the dimension \(d\).

papers.title: Multi-Future Drafting: Mixture Block Drafters for Tree-Verified Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Block drafters such as DFlash draft a block of future tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees such as DDTree verify the prefixes ranked highest by the product of the drafter's per-position distributions. Under tree verification, the expected number of accepted tokens is the probability mass the tree covers. We show that a product misallocates it: when the continuation can follow several futures, it splices them into chimeras, prefixes stitched together from different futures that the target never produces, and gives them as much budget as the futures themselves. Barring ties, no product-ranked tree can hold two futures that disagree in $m$ positions without $2^{m-1}-1$ chimeras, however well the drafter is trained, and in practice chimeras make up 27-33% of a 64-node tree. We propose Multi-Future Drafting (MFD), which restores the coupling with a latent variable instead of the chain rule: $K$ learned mode embeddings at the drafter's input draft $K$ coherent blocks in the same pass, and a mixture DDTree lets the verifier pick the future the target takes, losslessly and with $K+1$ extra vectors. On four Qwen targets from 4B to 27B parameters, at batch size 1, MFD reaches up to 7.8$\times$ speedup, 5-8% faster than the best single-mode tree trained identically and, on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, 9-16% faster than the released DARTree trained on the same prompts.

papers.title: Permutation-Based Pre-trained Model Merging via Reciprocal Orthogonality
papers.abstract: Ito et al. (2026) showed that sufficiently wide, independently trained neural networks can exhibit linear mode connectivity (LMC) with softmax temperature calibration, even without permutation. LMC means that a low-loss linear path connects the models' parameters. This behavior is explained by layerwise exponentially weighted connectivity (LEWC), whereby each merged layer outputs an exponentially weighted sum of the original models' corresponding representations, yielding ensemble-like predictions. However, prior work observed LEWC with substantial widening, such as 8192 units per hidden layer for MLPs and $16\times$ width for VGG-11, raising the question of whether such widths are necessary. We therefore search for permutations that encourage reciprocal orthogonality (RO), which suppresses interference between each model's weights and the other model's representations. This allows both models' computations to coexist in the merged network, promoting LEWC at smaller widths. We formulate the search as independent layerwise quadratic assignment problems and approximately solve their continuous relaxations using Frank--Wolfe. Experiments show that our method facilitates LMC with less width expansion. It also merges models trained on different data distributions, where weight matching, which maximizes weight similarity through permutations, struggles. The merged predictions approximate those of a logit ensemble of the original models.

papers.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses.
