However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

papers.title: Is a CNN-Transformer Ensemble Worth It When a Chest X-Ray Foundation Model Is Available?
papers.abstract: Ensembles of ImageNet-pretrained convolutional networks and Vision Transformers are a common way to improve multi-label chest X-ray classification. We ask whether such an ensemble is still worth its cost when a model pretrained on chest radiographs is available. On the official patient-disjoint split of NIH ChestX-ray14 (25,596 test images, 2,797 patients), we train five ImageNet-pretrained backbones and the EVA-X-S foundation model with validation-only model selection, compare five fusion rules, and estimate every difference with a patient-level paired bootstrap. EVA-X-S alone reached a test macro-AUROC of 0.828; the five-model ensemble reached 0.814 (difference -0.0136, 95% CI -0.0178 to -0.0098) at about 7.8 times the summed backbone latency and ten times the parameters. Averaging the five ImageNet models with EVA-X-S changed AUROC by -0.0056 (-0.0095 to -0.0021). With all five ImageNet backbones trained with the EVA-X-S recipe, their ensemble scored 0.817, still -0.0109 (-0.0142 to -0.0076) below EVA-X-S, and across three seeds EVA-X-S varied by at most 0.001 AUROC. Under the ImageNet models' recipe, however, EVA-X-S fell to 0.798. Our full-stacking configuration never outperformed calibrated averaging. In this setting, the tested ImageNet ensembles did not improve on a single chest X-ray foundation model fine-tuned with its own recipe.

papers.title: FaST: Factored Synthesis of Transitions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Synthetic data augmentation promises to scale offline reinforcement learning beyond fixed logged datasets, but leading diffusion-based generators model the transition tuple (state, action, next state, reward, terminal) as a monolith: no single factor can be natively redrawn in isolation. We present FaST (Factored Synthesis of Transitions), which factors transitions via the chain rule into state, action, dynamics, reward, and terminal stages, fitting each with an estimator matched to its statistical properties. Across twelve D4RL locomotion and maze benchmarks, TD3+BC and IQL agents trained on FaST transitions match the SynthER diffusion baseline while generating transitions over 90x faster. The explicit action-given-state conditional can also be re-queried for a fixed state, enabling targeted action synthesis: drawing N candidate actions per generated state and keeping the highest-advantage one under a value function fit to the same data, thereby synthesizing improved behavior during generation rather than filtering for it post-hoc. Best-of-10 synthesis beats training on real data on 11 of 12 medium and medium-replay settings (+8.9 D4RL points on average, up to +28.4), and is competitive with advantage-filtered SynthER at a fraction of its generation cost. On expert mixtures both mechanisms degrade identically, tracing the failure to the advantage estimate itself rather than to either targeting mechanism.

papers.title: khammoon: From a Linguistic Guideline to a Thai Morpheme Segmenter
papers.abstract: Thai is written without spaces between words, making segmentation a foundational step in most Thai NLP pipelines. Existing tools primarily reproduce the word-level conventions of corpora such as BEST; however, because the notion of a "word" in Thai lacks a unified linguistic consensus, these conventions struggle with productive compounding, leading to arbitrary boundaries and ambiguity in downstream representations. Instead, we propose operating at the morphological level, focusing on khammoon, the smallest atomic unit that carries meaning. Segmenting at the morphemic level provides an explicit, consistent morphological representation that eliminates compounding ambiguity. Crucially, this representation benefits downstream learning: models trained on morphemes perform on par with or exceed word-level baselines across part-of-speech tagging, named-entity recognition, and sentiment classification, demonstrating that linguistic consistency improves representation quality without downstream performance penalty. To operationalize this representation, we translate linguistic principles into a formal decision guideline with near-perfect human agreement ($\kappa \approx 0.99$), scale annotation with an LLM, and correct systematic errors with human labels. Finally, we train khammoon, a lightweight 1M-parameter convolutional BiLSTM segmenter designed for efficient CPU inference, achieving a boundary F1 of 0.992 on out-of-domain text. The guideline, datasets, model, and library are all publicly released.

papers.title: Compile-Gated Lean Proof Refactoring with Enterprise Agent Practices: A Model per Step under a US\$3 Cap, Followed by Programmatic Rewrite Rules
papers.abstract: Our closed-track entry (Arena username Vexorium-Agent) scored 86.31 points on the final board (L = 77.07, H = 81.86, Z = 100) over the 60 final problems, against 33.33 for the reference proofs, 8th at the deadline (top: 92.57), for US\$166.33 at list prices with every call counted (per problem: mean US\$2.772, at most US\$2.874; US\$3 cap). Three practices carry the entry. First, each paid stage runs the model that measured best per dollar for it among the 9 we tested in our own harness: GPT-6.1 Sol the early sessions, GPT-6.1 Terra the later ones and the tail at 70% of Sol's cost per turn, and Gemini 4 Argon the review and repair; Sol also runs the style rewrite. Second, what our development and research runs learned ships as compiler-checked programmatic rewrite rules rather than prompt text (+0.93 points from rules fixed before the release; +0.26 and +0.30, in sample, from passes built or switched on after the release). Third, every call is recorded and reviewed before each change (all 9 board scores came within -0.063 to +0.015 points of our meter's prediction). The harness, gate and many of these rules also serve our open-track entry. We report the full bill and the spread of three runs.

papers.title: Preserving Cultural Records: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Visual-Prior Routing Network for Ancient Book Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Ancient books preserve invaluable cultural heritage, yet their images often suffer from complex degradations caused by long-term ageing, environmental exposure, and physical damage. Existing ancient book image restoration benchmarks are limited in scale and rely on simplified degradation simulations, which cannot fully represent real-world degradation patterns and restrict the generalization ability of restoration models. To address these challenges, we introduce AncBench, a large-scale synthetic paired benchmark containing 100K aligned clean-degraded image pairs. AncBench models realistic composite degradations through a comprehensive degradation pipeline that considers material ageing, paper texture variation, blur, staining, water-induced geometric distortion, and local occlusion. Furthermore, we propose AncRestore, a degradation-aware visual-prior routing network for ancient book image restoration. AncRestore first learns degradation representations from degraded images and then dynamically selects and integrates suitable visual priors according to different degradation characteristics. Guided by these degradation cues, a dynamic routing mechanism combines expert-wise and region-wise routing strategies adaptively adjusts the contribution of these priors across different regions, enabling the model to recover both global appearance and local text details. Extensive experiments show that AncRestore effectively suppresses composite degradations while preserving text structures and enhancing restoration quality against other methods, highlighting its application potential for intelligent ancient book image restoration in cultural heritage preservation.

papers.title: Instance-preserving graded semantic reporting for surgical action triplets
papers.abstract: Complete-or-reject reporting of surgical action triplets can discard a correctly identified instrument and action when the target is uncertain. We introduce instance-preserving graded semantic reporting, which separates instance selection from the choice of semantic detail. Each selected instance retains its predicted mask and labels while hierarchical correctness scores guide instrument (I), instrument-verb (IV), or complete instrument-verb-target (IVT) reporting. The utility-increment rule DELTA weighs the expected gain from finer reporting against its error cost. We compare three decision rules on 5,641 test frames from eight surgical videos using fixed predictions and scores. At the 10% development calibration target, DELTA retains correct partial reports for 80.0% of candidates rejected by a matched complete-or-reject baseline (5,329/6,662). Adding IV increases source-normalized weighted correct-report yield by 19.13 to 23.13 per 100 frames across all three rules relative to separately recalibrated I/IVT controls. Weighted reporting risk changes by -0.77 to +1.01 percentage points, with complete correct-triplet counts unchanged or reduced. Graded reporting makes partial surgical predictions available as localized descriptions, with an explicit trade-off between report utility and completeness.

papers.title: An Open Implementation Flow for the Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 that Runs in the Browser, Checked Byte for Byte Against ISE
papers.abstract: The author describes an open implementation flow, from HDL to a programmable bitstream, for the Xilinx Spartan-3E (XC3S100E to XC3S1200E) and Spartan-6 (XC6SLX16, XC6SLX45), devices that only the discontinued ISE 14.7 supports. The flow runs unchanged in a web browser or in this http URL : Yosys and nextpnr compiled to WebAssembly, with nextpnr's Himbaechel framework given Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 architectures generated from Silinx's own device descriptions, bit database and timing model, and Silinx's own bitstream writer. The bit database was built by black-box observation of ISE's documented XDL and bitgen tools, using codeword-batched experiments; the router is given only switches whose bits were measured, and the writer refuses a feature it has not measured. ISE is the oracle: for the same placed and routed design, the bitstream is byte-identical to the one bitgen writes and ISE's DRC is clean. Placement and routing were first done by an in-house annealer and PathFinder router, which nextpnr replaced once it matched them. On 67 open-source designs for the XC3S1200E, compared with ISE at the same optimisation goal (45 designs built by both), the flow uses 15% fewer slices and has 14% shorter critical paths at goal Area, 21% fewer slices and 8% shorter paths at Speed, and 20% fewer slices but 12% longer paths at Fast (geometric means). XST cannot read 15 of the designs. The flow is published as the npm package silinx-fpga (Apache-2.0).

papers.title: Just AI Governance and the Forbidden-Boundary Principle
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes consequential decisions, yet predictive accuracy is not a sufficient justification for delegated authority. This conceptual study develops an integrated framework for assessing just AI across normative, data, model, and governance layers. Drawing on plural theories of justice, sociotechnical fairness research, and publicly available governance standards, it maps six justice requirements to observable evidence, decision rights, and remedies. It proposes a two-stage evaluation rule: exclude uses that fail independently justified minimum rights constraints, then compare eligible alternatives across multiple performance and governance criteria. As an explicitly limited normative analogy, Genesis chapter 2 motivates a Forbidden-Boundary Principle (FBP), under which an AI agent must not execute externally consequential actions outside pre-authorized boundaries. The resulting First-Principle Safe-Stop Protocol (FPSSP) comprises an independently governed policy monitor, a mandatory execution gate, a restricted or alternative safe-state controller, immutable-oriented audit trails, and accountable human authorization for recovery. We distinguish this normative and traceability contribution from existing Simplex and runtime assurance architectures; we do not claim a novel safety switch or formal proof of universal ethical compliance. A policy schema, threat model, test matrix, outcome definitions, and a prospective comparison design make the proposal falsifiable. No FPSSP implementation, experimental dataset, numerical improvement, or verified latency bound is reported. The framework supports future evaluation rather than constituting evidence of operational safety.

papers.title: Seeing Is Not Believing: Counterfactual Lesion Erasure Teaches a Small Medical Vision-Language Agent to Report Only What the Image Shows
papers.abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) often report a finding because the question names it; standard benchmarks miss this. From public segmentation datasets we build counterfactual views without manual annotation: the lesion erased by inpainting, a same-shape control edit elsewhere, and unedited lesion-free images. The evidence sensitivity gap (ESG) is the rate of absent-or-refer answers after erasure minus the rate after the control edit; it is zero for a model that ignores the image or reacts to both edits alike. MedScope-4B (Qwen3.5-4B, LoRA, image tools) was trained on label-derived trajectories, selected by a pre-registered rule and tested once against nine frontier and six open VLMs; four pre-registered checks then probed the mechanism. On 507 internal cases across five imaging types, MedScope-4B reached ESG 0.758 and claimed an erased lesion in 9.6% of cases, against 0.27-0.47 and 41-62% for the frontier models (all p<0.001), without significant loss of accuracy on real lesions. Without counterfactual views ESG fell to 0.279+-0.107 (three seeds); the effect replicated on MedGemma 1.5 4B and two unseen inpainting tools. At four external centres the advantage held but frontier models detected more real lesions; on a fresh external test MedScope-4B detected 0 of 48 pneumothorax films, with net utility below gemini-4-argon's (-0.36 [-0.50, -0.23]). Matching the control edit was not shown to matter; over three seeds no fresh-external ESG advantage over removal-based DPO was established; a paired-view consistency objective did not beat a matched-compute control, while that continuation alone cut erased-lesion claims on unseen tools at every seed, at a cost in sensitivity at one. Training on erased and edited images gives a small model an evidence-gated disposition that prompting does not give frontier models; it does not improve perception, and rare critical findings need coverage.

papers.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
papers.abstract: Synthesizing programs from execution traces is a fundamental challenge in algorithmic interpretability and the reverse engineering of complex systems. We bring a rough-path-theoretic perspective to program induction, treating execution traces as high-dimensional rough paths and encoding them with the path signature transform, a tool from stochastic analysis whose expectation provably characterizes the distribution of traces a program induces. On three program-induction domains, Karel, List, and RASP, our log-signature trace encoder outperforms LSTM, Transformer, and Fourier baselines in almost every setting, with its largest margins when training data is scarce. We further observe that the trace-to-program pipeline is naturally contractive: it often produces valid programs that are shorter than the ground truth. We turn this into a bootstrapping procedure that exposes redundancy in the ground-truth supervision without any external oracle, which we demonstrate on redundancy-injected versions of our datasets. Finally, the log-signature encoder induces a markedly more interpretable latent geometry than the baselines, in which the nearest neighbors of every state lie on its own execution trace.

papers.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
papers.abstract: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables \(32\times\) and even effective \(64\times\) compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups introduce intra-group dependencies that must be modeled efficiently, we analyze their impact on inference latency and generation quality and introduce a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. With these designs, our highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models across five representative text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench, and Qwen-Image-Bench). At \(1024\times1024\) resolution, our model delivers a \(20\times\) speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200. Together, these results show that highly compressed discrete representations can enable high-quality autoregressive generation at low latency.

papers.title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning agents are often deployed with policies that cannot be retrained or modified. In digital environments whose states can be copied and resumed, an operator has another option: sample several continuations from the current state, evaluate them, and continue from the endpoint of the selected branch. We call this procedure branch-and-commit. We study when it improves return, what produces the improvement, and where its computational budget should be spent. Across four environments, two frozen policies, five continuation verifiers, and a model-free selection rule, we find that the benefit of branching depends on dispersion: the difference between the best candidate return and the mean candidate return. Branching provides no benefit in low-dispersion settings, while increasing return by 12.8% in our main Craftax-Medium setting. Most of this gain comes not from selecting better actions, but from selecting among different stochastic realizations of the same action. Several competent verifiers achieve similar episode returns, suggesting that verifier quality is not the main constraint at our operating budget. Instead, computation is better allocated to states where useful dispersion is likely. On held-out seeds, gating branching using predicted dispersion retains 69% of the improvement from uniform branching while using 48% as many branching calls. These results characterize when branch-and-commit is useful and clarify what its gains represent.

papers.title: YTShorts-92K: An Interpretable Multimodal Dataset of YouTube Shorts
papers.abstract: Short-form video has become one of the dominant formats of online content, yet large-scale datasets enabling the analysis of what makes these videos successful remain limited. Existing resources often focus on post-publication popularity signals or rely on non-interpretable representations such as high-dimensional embeddings. Here, we introduce YTShorts-92K, a dataset of 92,654 YouTube Shorts collected from 345 creators and spanning 12 manually defined content categories. Each video is enriched with an interpretable multimodal feature set covering metadata, textual information, visual characteristics from frames and thumbnails, and cross-modal consistency measures. We describe the collection methodology, data cleaning process, and feature extraction pipeline, followed by descriptive analyses of the diversity of creators, topics, and extracted features. This dataset offers a reusable resource for studying short-form video content, online attention, and multimodal content analysis.

papers.title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction
papers.abstract: Generation, imputation, and prediction query different aspects of the same tabular distribution, but are usually evaluated separately. This leaves unclear which capabilities they share, how their training objectives interact, and whether one model can perform all three well. We introduce the One Table Benchmark (\ours{}), spanning 56 datasets, 46 registered methods, and 20 capability axes under aligned data splits and explicit task contracts. We compare task ranks on aligned support, train five backbones under all seven non-empty objective combinations on five datasets with three seeds, and contrast fixed-model profiles with specialist portfolios. Rank comparisons connect imputation and prediction through numerical recovery and dependence preservation, and link generation to both through predictive utility; distributional fidelity follows different, sometimes opposing, rankings. Objective interventions show the largest pooled gains from including the recipient's own objective. Generation has the broadest coverage of positive pooled auxiliary effects, while prediction shows potential to improve imputation and synthetic-data utility, with responses that vary across backbones. Cross-addition effects reveal that objective benefits need not add and depend on the objectives already present. Fixed-model comparisons expose corresponding utility--fidelity trade-offs: some generalists surpass specialist portfolios on utility, while fidelity continues to favor specialization. Frozen foundation models show strong prediction and numerical point imputation, together with promising synthetic-data utility, highlighting their potential across all three tasks. These findings motivate unified tabular models that share useful conditional information while improving categorical reconstruction and faithful joint sampling.

papers.title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
papers.abstract: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. However, for coordinate prediction in grounding tasks, existing architectures suffer from two distinct bottlenecks: discrete tokenization disrupts spatial continuity with high decoding latency, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets. To resolve these challenges, we propose PhysMoE, introducing three core contributions: (1) sharing lower layers for multimodal context while routing upper layers to specialized spatial (pixel) and linguistic (text) experts by physical modality, eliminating gradient interference; (2) encoding each coordinate as a single token by reusing the visual encoder's learned positional embeddings, injecting 2D spatial priors to natively align coordinates with visual features and ease training; and (3) differentiable Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision on pointing, accommodating affordances and irregular geometries without costly mask decoders. Compared to the base model, PhysMoE achieves a 15.7% average gain and an 8.31x throughput speedup across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks (trajectory, affordance, and localization), while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.

papers.title: Direct Multispectral Satellite Nowcasting of Gridded Surface Solar Radiation
papers.abstract: Surface shortwave radiation (SWR) can change within minutes as clouds evolve, but operational forecasts often trade spatial detail and update frequency for forecast range. We present a numerical-weather-prediction-independent, observation-to-forecast framework that converts sequences of Himawari-8 Level-1 multispectral imagery and solar geometry directly into 24 gridded SWR fields at 10-min intervals for the next 4 h. A controlled six-model experiment separates the effects of satellite information from those of temporal self-attention. In the 0-1 h window, the full-multispectral attention model achieves a mean absolute error of 37.9 W/m2 and a root mean square error of 63.7 W/m2, reductions of 21.0% and 19.5% relative to a historical-SWR baseline. Improvements extend across nine subregions and include weaker spatial bias and better structural consistency. Temporal attention does not improve forecasts from historical SWR alone, but becomes effective when supplied with multispectral cloud and thermodynamic signals. Direct multispectral observations therefore provide the precursor information required for high-frequency, spatially resolved SWR nowcasting.

papers.title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Linear probes are a standard method to study geometric structures, such as helices and circles, from the activations of large language models (LLMs), and such structure is often taken as evidence that the model computes with it. Probe accuracy alone cannot establish this, because it conflates four separate claims. These are (1) that the concept is decodable from the activations, (2) that they form a specific shape, (3) that the shape belongs to the probed concept rather than to a related concept the model also represents, and (4) that the output of the model depends on the shape. We call these claims decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use, and we test them separately with a four-stage Bayesian pipeline. Stage 2 compares candidate shapes and selects the best one only when its evidence passes a predefined threshold. Stage 3 removes a set of related concepts, specified in advance, and tests whether the shape is owned or inherited. Stage 4 intervenes on the shape to test whether the output of the model depends on it. We apply the pipeline to two-digit addition and multiplication in GPT-J 6B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Pythia 6.9B. Nearly every concept is decodable, but the decoded directions overlap substantially across concepts. Every strongly supported comparison selects a ribbon, which is a helix whose radius changes with the value, or a torus. Of 1,330 cells with an ownership verdict, 19% of shapes are owned and 81% are inherited. Owned and inherited shapes move the output about equally often. Intervening on the shape retains approximately 61% of the effect of intervening on the full probe while using at most five dimensions, against a median of nine for the probe. Our results indicate that a probe verdict alone overstates what a model computes with, and we propose that probe results be reported as verdicts on all four claims rather than as a single accuracy.

papers.title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
papers.abstract: Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Existing multimodal attribution methods typically rely on paired modalities as proxy supervision, implicitly assuming that image-text pairs are semantically aligned. Information bottleneck (IB)-based attribution methods follow this general paradigm and instantiate it through a global sufficiency-compression objective. In realistic multimodal datasets, however, this assumption is frequently violated due to partial semantic misalignment and unreliable cross-modal correspondences. Through theoretical analysis, we show that, under such misalignment, information-bottleneck-based attribution objectives exhibit a structural limitation: by assuming equal reliability across all proxy supervision signals, they induce posterior over-contraction and forced explanations. To address this issue, we propose TIB, a sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck framework that adaptively modulates attribution strength according to cross-modal reliability, without assuming semantic alignment. Extensive experiments on controlled benchmarks and large-scale datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed approach, while also validating the identified failure mode.

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Dimension Jumps in Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $2r+1$
papers.abstract: We study geometric dependence of the dimensions of planar spline spaces $S_{2r+1}^r$ through families with a single moving interior vertex and determine their dimensions throughout the admissible parameter domains. For $r=1$, we extend the Wu--Deng one-parameter classification to the interior of the central quadrilateral. The dimension increases by one at exactly two isolated points, one due to a local direction-count change and the other to a global compatibility defect. For $r=2$, subdividing one triangle of the Yuan--Stillman configuration gives a twelve-triangle family with fixed local direction counts; its dimension increases by one precisely on an open line segment. For every $r\ge3$, we construct a family with $2r+12$ triangles and fixed local direction counts, proving geometric dependence at degree $2r+1$. The moving vertex lies in an open triangle, and the dimension exceeds Schumaker's lower bound by one exactly on its symmetry axis. The lower collinear vertices may have arbitrary strictly ordered heights. The low-order proofs use exact cofactor elimination. For higher orders, weighted interpolation and block elimination bound the global defect by one, and explicit extension and obstruction arguments determine the exceptional set.

papers.title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing
papers.abstract: Knowledge editing has emerged as a promising approach for efficiently updating embedded knowledge in large language models (LLMs). It first computes an ideal target hidden state that steers the LLM toward the new output, and then edits the model parameters so that the original hidden state is mapped to this target. While most existing methods focus on the second stage of parameter editing in preserving other knowledge, we find that the upstream construction of the target hidden state also plays an important role in allocating the model's limited capacity space. We first establish a theoretical connection between interference in the parameter space and interference between target hidden states, showing that the two are positively correlated. Building on this insight, we propose a simple yet effective $\ell_1$ regularization method that prunes away unnecessary ``tentacles'' of each knowledge vector, retaining only the essential components. With fewer extraneous tentacles, each edit affects less other knowledge, enabling better coexistence. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmark datasets verify the effectiveness of our method. Code: this https URL .

papers.title: Measurement of the $^{169}$Tm$(γ,n)$$^{168}$Tm Cross Section and Implications for $γ$-Process Calculations
papers.abstract: The $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(\gamma,n)^{168}\mathrm{Tm}$ cross section has been measured at the Shanghai Laser Electron Gamma Source (SLEGS) using quasi-monoenergetic laser-Compton-scattering $\gamma$ rays over the energy range from the neutron threshold to 14.61~MeV. The photon flux and energy distribution were determined with a LaBr$3$(Ce) spectrometer, and monoenergetic cross sections were obtained using an iterative unfolding method. Below 12~MeV, the present cross sections agree well with the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluations. However, near the maximum of the $(\gamma,n)$ excitation function, the present cross sections are significantly higher than both the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluated values. The $E1$ $\gamma$-ray strength functions were derived by fitting the experimental cross sections measured at SLEGS and NewSUBARU. The stellar reaction rates for $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(\gamma,n)$ and $^{168}\mathrm{Tm}(n,\gamma)$ were calculated by incorporating these constrained $\gamma$-ray strength functions into the TALYS code. The calculated $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(\gamma,n)$ rates were adopted in a full $p$-process reaction network for the shock-heated O/Ne-rich layers of a $20 M\odot$ core-collapse supernova model to perform a sensitivity analysis. The updated rates have a negligible effect on the final $p$-nucleus abundances.

papers.title: Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits
papers.abstract: We prove that for arbitrary two-qutrit quantum states, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for the PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Therefore, under operations preserving positive partial transpose, its zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can be obtained by a semidefinite program involving only three Hermitian matrix variables. The key to the proof is to shorten the feasible dual chain by one level; to this end, we combine finite certificates verified by exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain. This result shows that a unified terminating level exists for two-qutrit systems, whereas no unified terminating level exists for all dimensions.

papers.title: ZeroPoint: Lightweight Energy-Based Decision Model
papers.abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) assign a scalar energy to every joint value of the observed and predicted variables. In decision models, the prediction is chosen from a finite list of options provided with each input. Inference then reduces to comparing the energies of the options, and training lowers the energy of the correct option relative to the others. A complete decision must also account for the possibility that no option is acceptable. However, the energies learned by a standard EBM define only relative compatibility: adding the same input-dependent quantity to all energies leaves the predictions, the Gibbs distribution, and the usual training losses unchanged. The model therefore has no learned reference level against which to decide whether any option fits. We propose ZeroPoint, an EBM that makes the empty answer a state of the model with energy zero for every input. This fixed state provides an explicit reference for the energies of all listed options, whose non-negative depths measure their compatibility with the input relative to the empty answer. The options and the empty answer share one distribution, in which an option at zero depth receives no probability. The decision to select an option or to abstain is thus part of ordinary inference, trained with the negative log-likelihood loss, rather than a separate rejection rule. The energy function is a small multilingual encoder that reads the input together with all the options and is invariant to their order. Ablations show that most of the benefit comes from training with examples in which no option fits. With the same encoder and data, the fixed zero separates inputs with and without an acceptable option slightly better than a learned rejection class and clearly better than a thresholded softmax, while leaving the choice among options unchanged.

papers.title: Specializing Meta Multi-Objectivization as Baseline for Software Engineering Optimization
papers.abstract: Given the discrete nature of many software engineering (SE) optimization problems, trapping at local optima remains a crucial issue in the optimizer designs. Meta Multi-Objectivization (MMO) is an optimization model for overcoming local optima by introducing an extra, auxiliary objective. Yet, MMO is originally designed only for configuration tuning, leaving its suitability for other SE problems in doubt, particularly regarding the choice of the auxiliary objective. In this paper, we study the possibility and resolution for specializing MMO as a general baseline across a range of SE optimization problems, making it a fundamental counterpart for future SE optimizers that seek to mitigate the issue of local optima. We do so by providing both theoretical remit and empirical evidence: we analytically show how the choice of the auxiliary objective is crucial while demonstrating the effectiveness of MMO under nine SE optimization problems comprising 212 cases when the right one can be chosen, i.e., MMO is able to outperform the other state-of-the-art and general-purpose optimizers in 79% and 94% of the cases, respectively. Drawing on the theoretical understanding and empirical findings, we then propose L2RAC, a tool that automatically recommends the best auxiliary objective choice for a given SE problem/case, hence helping to specialize MMO therein. Through extensive experiments, we reveal that, in general, L2RAC can more accurately rank the choice of auxiliary objective for MMO under a case than other guesses by up to 60%, saving as much as 99% of the cost that would otherwise be required to conduct trial-and-error when using MMO.

papers.title: Multimodal Graph Learning: A Survey of Models, Benchmarks, and Frontiers
papers.abstract: Multimodal attributed graphs (MAGs), in which nodes carry text, images, and other modalities while edges encode relations among entities, underlie e-commerce, social media, content platforms, and creative applications. Learning on MAGs has developed along two complementary lines: graph-centric methods redesign how modalities are fused, propagated, and connected within message passing, while foundation-model-centric methods pretrain transferable multimodal graph encoders or bring graph context into multimodal large language models for prediction and generation. In parallel, several benchmarks have appeared with different datasets and evaluation protocols. This survey takes an algorithm-centric and evaluation-grounded view of the field and makes three contributions. Modeling: we introduce a unified message-passing formulation and organize methods into five integration levels (feature, propagation, topology, learning, and foundation model), covering discriminative and graph-conditioned generative models; within this formulation we derive representative methods as special cases, compare their assumptions, expressiveness, and cost, and identify cross-modal sensitivity as a property that separates otherwise similar architectures. Datasets and evaluation: we review recent benchmarks, summarize their datasets and metrics, define model-independent descriptors (label homophily, average degree, clustering, and edge provenance), and map each evaluation protocol to the baselines it uses. Frontiers: we connect multimodal graph learning to AI agents, covering the multimodal graphs that agents perceive and remember and graph engineering, the practice of organizing agent workflows as explicit graphs; we then discuss open problems, concrete efforts for the community, and research directions, including when graph structure helps in the presence of strong multimodal foundation models.

papers.title: A Markovian SuASR epidemic framework with stochastic external factors
papers.abstract: Epidemic waves are often shaped by uncertain external drivers, such as environmental variability or behavioral and policy changes, that can randomly amplify or dampen transmission. Capturing this randomness requires models whose dynamics evolve under time-varying, stochastic influences. In this paper, we introduce a stochastic Susceptible-Asymptomatic-Symptomatic-Removed (SuASR) framework that embeds random external factors directly into the epidemic mechanism through an extended continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). The proposed framework is flexible enough to represent epidemic dynamics both with reinfection and with infection-induced immunity, depending on the epidemiological setting under study. Unlike standard Markovian epidemic models, our formulation explicitly tracks two concurrent infectious sources (asymptomatic and symptomatic), yielding coupled infection pathways and substantially richer transient behavior. A key contribution is analytical tractability, where we derive computable expressions for the joint distribution of asymptomatic and symptomatic infection-event counts and develop tools tailored to extreme-outbreak risk, including the distribution of the maximum infectious burden. These results enable probabilistic quantification of epidemic severity beyond mean trajectories, providing direct estimates of the likelihood of rare but consequential surges. We validate the model through extensive sensitivity analysis and an application to the H1N1 influenza epidemic, illustrating how stochastic external influences reshape outbreak profiles, total infections from both sources, and the probability of extreme epidemic scenarios

papers.title: Third Eye: Beyond Immediate Gains in Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Does a useful self-update remain useful after the model updates again? Third Eye separates immediate performance from the outcome of a further native update. We evaluate five 3-8B backbones on math and code: 64 fresh runs, three candidates per run, and three continuations per candidate. Selection and final scoring use disjoint items. In the balanced Qwen3-4B/Llama-3.2-3B comparison, immediate-selected utility is near zero, but continuation reduces it by 1.78 percentage points (simultaneous 95% interval [0.68, 2.88]). Candidate-averaged immediate utility is already negative: selection partly accounts for the apparently neutral first step. Continuation also lowers utility for SmolLM3-3B and Llama-3.1-8B; Qwen3-8B remains inconclusive. Target and out-of-distribution losses dominate retention changes. Matched recipe and recipient-donor controls identify neither a reliable mitigation nor a single mechanism. The results support evaluating persistent self-updates as adaptation transitions, with independent scoring and a no-update baseline, rather than interpreting immediate performance as their full value.

papers.title: Global Trends and Heterogeneity in Modified Adjusted Net Savings
papers.abstract: Modified adjusted net savings is a derived weak sustainability indicator obtained by subtracting education expenditure from adjusted net savings (ANS). Because ANS equals net national savings plus education expenditure minus natural-resource depletion and carbon dioxide damage, MANS isolates the savings and depletion components and is useful when education expenditure would otherwise dominate cross-country comparisons. This study documents the global distribution, long-run trends, and cross-country heterogeneity of MANS excluding particulate emission damage over 1990-2021. The accounting base is the World Bank World Development Indicators series this http URL , and MANS is constructed by subtracting education expenditure from this series. We combine global maps, aggregate time series, country-level heatmaps, distributional statistics, and income group comparisons. The results show that global MANS has increased substantially in aggregate, but its evolution as a share of nominal GDP has been more volatile and uneven across countries. Per capita MANS and global MANS totals remain concentrated in high-income and large economies, whereas low-income and lower-middle-income groups display persistently lower and more volatile outcomes. Country rankings are highly persistent, and some populous countries exhibit pronounced fluctuations associated with natural-resource dependence and structural change. The study provides a reproducible descriptive benchmark for monitoring sustainable development and highlights the need to interpret MANS in current US dollars alongside income-group and country-specific contexts. The findings are relevant for macroeconomic policy, natural-capital accounting, and the design of sustainability-oriented investment strategies.

papers.title: Dust matter cosmology in modified symmetric teleparallel $f(Q,T)$ gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear $f(Q,T)$ gravity model, $f(Q,T) = \alpha Q^n + \beta T + \gamma$, which represents a nontrivial coupling between geometry and matter in the context of a dust-dominated Universe. The model parameters $(H_0, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, n)$ are constrained using recent cosmological observations, including Hubble parameter measurements $H(z)$, the Pantheon+SH0ES dataset, and DESI BAO data. The analysis shows that the Hubble constant exhibits dataset-dependent variations, reflecting the persisting Hubble tension, while $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ are tightly constrained and $\beta$ remains weakly determined. The nonlinear exponent $n$ introduces an additional degree of freedom that enhances the model's flexibility in reproducing observational trends. The cosmographic diagnostics, including the deceleration, jerk, snap, and lerk parameters, indicate a Universe transitioning from early deceleration to late-time acceleration, with present values closely aligned with $\Lambda$CDM predictions and far-future behavior approaching a de Sitter phase. These results demonstrate that the nonlinear $f(Q,T)$ model provides a simple and viable framework to describe late-time cosmic acceleration, accommodate observational tensions, and reproduce $\Lambda$CDM-like dynamics with subtle deviations.

papers.title: Parametric Proof-Carrying Compilation for Quantum Error-Correction
papers.abstract: We present PC-QEC, a proof-carrying compilation framework for quantum error correction parameterized by both code distance and syndrome-extraction scheme. It covers all four schemes---Standard, Flag, Shor and Knill---with circuit-level distance guarantees for every legal code distance in each proved family under the declared fault and readout contracts. The circuit-level model permits single-wire Pauli faults at every operation's qubit operands, capturing data errors, readout errors and ancilla faults that propagate into multi-qubit hook errors. For each family and scheme, code-algebra proofs and fault-aware Hoare proofs compose into a finite symbolic certificate whose size is independent of code distance. We demonstrate family-wide guarantees for five code families across all four schemes. For rotated Surface code, one Standard Scheme certificate proves a distance lower bound $d$ for every odd $d\ge3$ and checks in 214\,s on average. Lean 4 mechanizes the metatheory and exact circuit-level distances for canonical Surface, hypergraph-product (HGP) and Toric code families.

papers.title: Uniform Resolvent Estimates for the Dunkl Laplacian
papers.abstract: Let \(\Lk=-\Dk\) denote the nonnegative Dunkl Laplacian associated with a finite reflection group and a nonnegative multiplicity function \(\kappa\), and let $ N=d+2\gk\geq 3 $ be the corresponding homogeneous dimension. We establish uniform \(L_\kappa^p(\mathbb{R}^d)\)-\(L_\kappa^q(\mathbb{R}^d)\) resolvent estimates for \(\Lk\) whenever \[ \frac{2}{N+1} \leq \frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q} \leq \frac{2}{N}, \quad \frac{2N}{N+3}<p<\frac{2N}{N+1}, \quad \frac{2N}{N-1}<q<\frac{2N}{N-3}, \] where the last upper bound is interpreted as \(q<\infty\) when \(N=3\). Remarkably, this admissible range coincides with the corresponding range for the Euclidean Laplacian \(-\Delta\) in dimension \(N\).

papers.title: CAFE: Closed-Loop Autonomous Task Formulation and Execution without Instance-Specific Instructions
papers.abstract: Scene-driven robot autonomy requires selecting tasks from observations as well as executing them. We study scene-driven task formulation and execution under predefined cleaning, safety, and storage/organization categories, without instance-specific goals or action sequences. CAFE maintains online memory of objects, functional zones, and execution states. A rule-guided Trigger-LLM admits formulation from accumulated evidence; Draft, Complete, and Audit propose goals, resolve execution details, and check dependencies. Outcomes update memory for correction and subsequent discovery. Evaluation in 12 AI2-THOR scenes compares three backbones and task-complexity tiers using coverage, constraint, and execution metrics. Tri-LLM records higher GCR scores than the evaluated baselines across three backbones and task-complexity tiers. Controls examine completion, auditing, zones, feedback, triggering, and prompt examples. LimoCobot traces illustrate storage, cleanup, and recovery from a failed grasp. The study examines how shared scene state connects task discovery to execution and outcome-driven revision.

papers.title: ICLayout-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Custom Circuit Layout Design
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are being explored for circuit design, but their ability to produce high-quality custom layouts has not been extensively evaluated. ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark in which agents use electronic design automation (EDA) tools to construct and optimize GDSII layouts from transistor-level circuit netlists. These layouts are evaluated using physical verification, parasitic extraction, and post-layout simulation. Layouts that pass the physical and functional checks are scored on electrical performance and area. The benchmark includes 165 tasks across 13 process design kits (PDKs), covering technology nodes from 3 nm to 180 nm. The tasks span analog, mixed-signal, and digital circuits in open-source and commercial EDA flows. The experiments evaluate 22 configurations spanning seven models on 21 public and 19 private tasks. Mean layout scores range from 4.22 to 80.26 on public tasks and from 1.43 to 67.01 on private tasks, on a 100-point scale. Higher reasoning effort does not consistently improve mean scores, and configurations with comparable scores can incur substantially different model costs.

papers.title: Evidence-Grounded Iterative Reasoning for the Diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases
papers.abstract: Overlapping imaging manifestations complicate the differential diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases (DCLDs), while limited annotated data constrain supervised model development. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can integrate imaging and clinical information, but their diagnostic reasoning remains limited by incomplete volumetric perception and insufficient grounding in disease-specific evidence. We propose DCLDs-EIR, an evidence-grounded iterative reasoning framework coupling diagnostic hypothesis refinement with multimodal evidence acquisition and verification. Multiview renderings of predicted lung and cyst segmentations characterize global cyst distributions and initialize the differential diagnosis. Competing hypotheses guide axial CT inspection to identify local findings that, together with clinical context, inform retrieval from a disease-specific knowledge graph. Accumulated patient observations and retrieved knowledge are jointly assessed for diagnostic support and refutation to revise the diagnostic state. Updated hypotheses and unresolved distinctions guide subsequent inspection, forming a feedback loop between evidence acquisition and hypothesis verification. Multicenter evaluation demonstrates that DCLDs-EIR consistently improves diagnostic accuracy over baselines and enables traceable differential diagnosis through explicit links between diagnostic hypotheses, patient observations, and disease-specific knowledge.

papers.title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs continuous intensity images from spike-domain representations. Experiments on gray-scale and color spike reconstruction show that MADSNet outperforms SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on SREDS. Compared with Spk2ImgNet, it achieves about 15$\times$ lower latency and uses only about 1/40 of the estimated energy, demonstrating that carefully designed SNN architectures can improve reconstruction quality while preserving computational efficiency.

papers.title: Priority-Aware Deficit Round Robin for AXI4 Bandwidth Fairness in ASAP-7nm Process
papers.abstract: Modern systems-on-chip place real-time clients, processor cores and bulk data engines on the same AXI4 interconnect, where they contend for shared slaves. AXI4 fixes the ordering rules and carries a 4-bit quality of service (QoS) field, but leaves the service policy to the implementer, and that policy determines how long each master waits and how much bandwidth it receives once a slave saturates. We propose a QoS-aware deficit round robin (DRR) architecture that charges each grant in beats, and benchmark it against two architectures built behind the same port list: round robin, and QoS priority with anti-starvation aging. Charging in beats recovers bandwidth fairness while leaving every burst whole, so the address phase is issued once and locality for memory access is preserved. All three are driven by the same deterministic traffic generator and taken from RTL to GDSII on the ASAP7 7-nm predictive PDK. Under a 1:16 burst-length mismatch, the round robin and QoS architectures both hold the beat ratio between the two competing masters at 1:16, while our design brings it to 1:1 at full load. Mean read latency for the priority master falls from 95 cycles under round robin to 67 with QoS and 37 with QoS-aware DRR. At 500 MHz this serves the priority master in 74 ns against 190 ns. The measurements give a per-policy price and a traffic-based guide for choosing among the three.

papers.title: Trajectory-Regularized Distribution Distillation for One-Step Generation
papers.abstract: Distilling flow matching models for one-step generation generally follows two paradigms. Trajectory alignment supervises the student with the teacher's probability flow ODE, but its performance degrades under very small sampling budgets. Distribution matching directly optimizes the generated distribution, but estimating its reverse Kullback-Leibler gradient typically requires a separate network to track the evolving student score. We propose trajectory-regularized distribution distillation (TRD), which combines distribution-level and trajectory-level supervision through a momentum-mixture policy predicted in a single student forward pass. This policy serves simultaneously as a one-step generator, an estimator of the student's marginal velocity that removes the need for a second trainable network in distribution matching, and a closed-form time-dependent velocity field supervised along the teacher ODE trajectory. Experiments on SANA-1.6B and Stable Diffusion 3.5 show that TRD outperforms representative consistency and distribution matching baselines in generation quality and training efficiency for both one-step and few-step generation, with a trade-off in sample diversity.

papers.title: Selective Surgical Action-Center Localization:Retaining Localization Gains through Supervised Scoring
papers.abstract: Surgical action-center localization requires both an accurate reference point and a decision about whether to report it. When frames with and without a reportable center are mixed, the benefit of improved localization depends on which correct candidates survive selection. We present a selective localization pipeline combining heatmap and coordinate supervision with a logistic-regression scorer. The scorer learns to identify predictions with a reportable center and a localization error within a specified tolerance. The internal evaluation uses 5,000 frames from 50 surgical sources, five source-grouped folds and two random seeds. Matched locator and scoring comparisons track correct candidates and their rejection. At an 80% acceptance quota per source and a tolerance of 0.10 times the image diagonal, our method retains 46.08 correct outputs per 100 inputs. The baseline locator with the same scoring approach retains 44.20. The gain is 1.88 (descriptive 95% source-paired bootstrap interval, 0.94 to 2.79). Under entropy-based selection, increased rejection of correct predictions offsets the higher supply of correct predictions on average. For the coordinate-supervised locator, supervised scoring reduces these rejections from 6.15 to 2.99 per 100 inputs. Evaluating retained correct outputs reveals whether a selection rule preserves or erodes an improvement in localization.

papers.title: Partition, Refine, and Detect: Preserving Novel Category Capacity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) expects the model trained on base classes to recognize both base and novel classes at inference. Typical methods rely on CLIP-style vision-language embeddings, yet the learned space is often biased toward base categories, with limited effective capacity preserved for novel concepts. Such a base-dominated representation can compress novel semantics, leading to semantic collapse and mis-calibrated confidence at inference. To address this issue, we present PR-OVD, a partition-and-refine framework that explicitly reserves capacity for novel categories and strengthens category separation, while being seamlessly integrated into different detector architectures. Specifically, PR-OVD first performs coarse partitioning to build global divisions for base, novel, and an explicit background partition in both visual and textual modalities, preventing object-irrelevant embeddings from leaking into category-specific representations. It then applies category-level refinement within each partition to sharpen decision boundaries and alleviate the lack of fine-grained region-level pretraining in CLIP. To further provide reliable visual anchors for novel categories, we design a cognitively inspired Structure Prompt (SP) that encodes both egocentric attributes and allocentric context, facilitating stable partition-and-refine learning. Extensive experiments on two OVD benchmarks show that PR-OVD delivers an average 6.5\% proportional improvement on novel categories over the state-of-the-art methods. Notably, PR-OVD also benefits other open-vocabulary tasks, including segmentation and classification, further confirming its effectiveness and generality.

papers.title: Attribute-Evidence Learning with Multimodal Prompt for Generalized Category Discovery
papers.abstract: Generalized category discovery (GCD) aims to discover novel categories from unlabeled data by leveraging limited labeled samples from old classes. Existing methods that rely solely on visual cues often neglect the multimodal nature of human perception, prompting recent approaches to incorporate textual information such as category tags and attributes. However, these approaches typically entangle global tags and local attributes within a shared global image representation, rendering attributes unreliable and potentially providing misleading cues that can drive the model toward incorrect predictions. To this end, we propose AptM-GCD, a novel multimodal framework that exploits apt textual guidance through attribute evidence learning and multimodal prompt reasoning. Specifically, we design an Attribute-Evidence Learning (AEL) mechanism that treats attributes as localized visual evidence rather than global category descriptors. By interacting attribute embeddings with patch-level visual tokens, AEL identifies reliable attribute-related regions and extracts discriminative local evidence, thereby reducing the impact of noisy or irrelevant attribute cues. Building upon the extracted evidence, we further develop a Multimodal Prompt Learning (MPL) mechanism to bridge local attribute semantics and global visual understanding. MPL converts fine-grained textual evidence into visual prompts and injects them into a multimodal prompt transformer, enabling attribute information to enhance category discrimination through contextual reasoning without enforcing direct global alignment between modalities. Extensive experiments on six datasets demonstrate that AptM-GCD consistently achieves SoTA performance across both fine-grained and generic benchmarks. Moreover, the proposed framework exhibits strong generalization ability, delivering consistent gains under unimodal and class-imbalanced GCD settings.

papers.title: StatPrompt-LLM: A Lightweight Statistical Refinement for Foundation-Style Time-Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Time-series forecasting has recently seen a paradigm shift with the introduction of foundation-style models that adapt large pretrained language architectures to sequential data. However, effectively exposing fundamental temporal structures, such as trend, scale, and temporal dependence, to these models remains an open challenge, particularly when the available observations are limited. In this paper, we conduct an exploratory empirical study across different generations of forecasting architectures and propose StatPrompt-LLM, a lightweight statistical refinement of Time-LLM. StatPrompt-LLM augments the existing Time-LLM prompting mechanism with dataset-level statistical information and introduces a zero-initialised autoregressive bypass as a complementary linear forecasting pathway. We evaluate our framework on electricity and meteorological time-series benchmarks, including ETTh1, ETTh2, and Weather, under full-prefix and reduced-prefix configurations. Under the 10% reduced-prefix configuration, StatPrompt-LLM achieved lower in-sample prediction errors than Time-LLM, with unweighted average relative reductions across datasets of 40.2% in MSE and 21.4% in MAE. Full-prefix results were more dataset-dependent. Ablation analyses revealed relatively modest and dataset-dependent changes when selected additional statistical descriptor groups were masked within the combined architecture. Computational profiling indicated additional model parameters and runtime overhead relative to Time-LLM.

papers.title: Standalone Validation of a Pulsar Evolution Subroutine for NBODY6++GPU: Seven Test Scenarios
papers.abstract: Pulsars in globular clusters provide critical constraints on the evolution of compact objects. However, the treatment of neutron stars in standard N-body codes is outdated, and requires a better implementation of magnetic field decay, spin evolution, and accretion driven recycling that shape their observable properties. We present a standalone validation of a pulsar evolution subroutine for NBODY6++GPU, systematically tested across seven controlled scenarios prior to integration into full cluster simulations. These scenarios isolate distinct evolutionary regimes, including young pulsar spin down, millisecond pulsar weak torque evolution, accretion driven recycling in X-ray binaries, environmental torques in dense cores, wide binary systems, and compact binaries in the dipole spin-down regime. Through two separate numerical implementations, we achieve cross validation demonstrating better than 0.1% agreement across all physical quantities and timescales. Our validation confirms that analytical solutions are reproduced with high precision for isolated pulsars, gigayear scale evolution (tau_c ~ 1.0 Gyr) matches observations of millisecond pulsars in clusters like 47 Tucanae, and accretion driven recycling operates with physically realistic timescales, yielding a final period of 1.0 ms and a period derivative of approximately -5.9e-19 s/s, with accretion dominance by a factor of about 14. We demonstrate that environmental torques remain negligible even in the densest cluster environments, while compact binary spin down is validated; gravitational wave orbital decay is deferred to future work. All validation codes, test suites, and integration instructions are publicly available to support future applications.

papers.title: Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation
papers.abstract: We present a software implementation (as a Python package) of approximation schemes for verifying frequency inequalities arising from the quadratic Bendixson criterion for systems of delay equations (with a single delay in the linear part). In applications to dissipative nonlinear autonomous systems, such inequalities ensure global stability. The theoretical foundations of this approach were developed in our related work. In particular, it was shown that the transfer operators involved into the frequency inequalities can be represented as integral operators with bounded kernels of the Hardy--Volterra type. Here, we use this representation to construct approximation schemes based on finite-dimensional truncations of the transfer operators. Examples of using the package are provided.

papers.title: Time Running Backwards, and Where It Stops: Superoscillations of Proper Time and the Memory of the Environment
papers.abstract: A quantum system prepared in a superposition of proper times - a clock whose worldline is superposed, or a clock at rest in a superposed gravitational potential - evolves, in each branch, by the same dynamics for a different duration. Post-selecting the control that sets the proper time turns the superposition into a superoscillation of the time-dilation factor: the system is found to have evolved for a proper time $\alpha_w t$, where the weak value $\alpha_w$ may exceed unity, vanish, or be negative - the quantum time-translation machine of Aharonov, Anandan, Popescu and Vaidman. We ask how far back such a machine can run an irreversible process. The test system is a sealed cell - excited atoms, the radiation field they emit into, and the absorbing walls, carried as one quantum object - and the witness is projective: atoms that had begun to decay before the run are found, in the post-selected sub-ensemble, more excited than when inserted. The answer is exact and depends only on the atoms' survival amplitude. With two branches the witness holds only while the decay is younger than the memory time of the environment, after which the emission becomes Markovian. Beyond it, the post-selection amplifies the minute difference between the contents of the cell in the two branches, set by the full energy spread of the atoms and their field rather than by the linewidth, and the witness fails. Reversing a decay past the memory time requires many branches, an environment with a strictly bounded spectrum, and a post-selection probability that falls exponentially with the number of environmental oscillations to be undone. The obstacle to reversal is therefore not entropy but bandwidth - the same bandwidth that makes the emission irreversible in the first place. We give four ways to superpose a clock rate, from hollow massive shells to inertial velocities.

papers.title: TrustMod-SM: A Multi-Axis Benchmark for Evaluating Trustworthiness of LLMs in Social Media Content Moderation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong potential for social media content moderation, but their trustworthiness beyond overall accuracy remains underexplored. We introduce TrustMod-SM, a benchmark of roughly 29,000 instances across eight datasets, to evaluate LLM moderators on five dimensions: trustfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and context integrity. Evaluating 16 open-weight models (0.5B-284B parameters, spanning text-only and vision-language architectures) and one closed frontier model, we find persistent trustworthiness gaps. Higher detection accuracy often coincides with greater demographic disparity, and models frequently comply with concealment or exaggeration prompts, assign high confidence to wrong predictions, rarely escalate ambiguous cases, and struggle to separate hate speech from counter-speech or reclaimed language (especially below 8B parameters). Scaling does not uniformly resolve these issues, and no single model excels across all five dimensions.

papers.title: Evaluation protocols for historical script classification: the cost of manuscript-level leakage and the role of soft labels
papers.abstract: A paleographer applies a script type classifier to unseen manuscripts. We measure how much testing on other pages of training manuscripts inflates accuracy. On VML-HP-ext (715 pages, 171 Hebrew manuscripts, 14 script classes) we compare page-level and manuscript-level splits. Page-level accuracy drops from 97% to 54% (59% at manuscript level), and is 39% on the official blind test set. The gap of 40 to 47 percentage points (pp) at patch, page and manuscript level is statistically significant and reproduces with ResNet18; on binarized patches (ink and background only) it is 34 to 42 pp, also significant. On unseen manuscripts the model is overconfident: mean confidence 70% against 54% correct pages; patch-level expected calibration error (ECE, mean gap between confidence and accuracy) rises from 0.065 to 0.444. Binarization leaves patch-level overconfidence but cuts it markedly at page level. Confidence still helps triage: in the more confident half of pages 67% are correct, 41% in the rest. Training on expert soft labels showed no evidence of an accuracy difference, though a small page-level loss cannot be ruled out. The predicted distributions are closer to the expert's assessment. ECE is lower at patch level (0.21 to 0.31) and in most runs at page level, but not significantly at manuscript level. Label smoothing (blurring the label, no expert input) also lowers ECE but comes no closer to the expert. Temperature scaling (post-training confidence correction) helps significantly only at patch level. On 97 pages of 16 manuscripts with mixed expert assessment, soft labels cut divergence from the expert by 22 to 30% (significant in four of five runs); the point estimate of accuracy is 16.5 to 23.7 pp below hard labels, but with 16 manuscripts the loss can neither be confirmed nor ruled out. We propose recommendations for the evaluation protocol; code will be released with the paper

papers.title: Wafer-scale MoS2 and HZO-based Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors with 4.4 V Memory Window for Back-End Compatible Multibit Memory
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with low-power operation and non-volatile data retention enabled by stable ferroelectric polarization switching, have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional floating-gate transistors for next-generation low-power memory applications. A FeFET with two-dimensional (2D) channel provides the opportunity for better electrostatic gate control and scalability beyond silicon. In this work, we report wafer scale 2D semiconductor-based FeFETs with Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) gate stack showing unusual p-type charge transport and stable multibit memory properties. FeFETs based on 2-3 monolayer Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) channel and a 20 nm HZO back gate oxide layer exhibit a large hysteresis with a memory window spanning 4.4 V under a operating voltage range of +3.8 to -3.8 V, and an ION/IOFF ratio of 10^5. We demonstrate that the polarization charge-induced modification of Schottky barrier width strongly affects the hole transport and memory properties of MoS2-HZO FeFETs. We further demonstrate several advantages and unique features of the FeFETs such as nondestructive data readout, non-volatile data retention under zero gate bias, low operation voltage, high write endurance and ultra-fast switching speed. These 1T memory cells can simplify the dense 3D integrated array architecture and offer additional practical functionalities, such as fast programming and erasing of large data arrays that are absent for many conventional memories. The demonstrated MoS2 and HZO-based FeFET shows great potential for on-chip complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-back-end-of-line (BEOL) compatible circuits for multifunctional devices, especially for 3D monolithically integrated architectures for AI workload.

papers.title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(\delta t)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $\kappa(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.

papers.title: BuySideFlow: A Point-in-Time Benchmark for LLM Agents in Investment Research
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate SQL and SQL--Python workflows for investment research, but ensuring point-in-time (PIT) validity remains challenging. Agents must enforce disclosure cutoffs and select the appropriate historical states and record versions throughout data retrieval and financial analysis. We introduce \textsc{BuySideFlow}, a benchmark of 408 practitioner-derived Chinese-language tasks spanning equities, funds, fixed income, and macroeconomics over a fixed snapshot from a licensed production financial database. We provide executable references and a taxonomy of temporal errors, pairing result checks with expert audits of executed workflows. We evaluate nine agent configurations on all tasks, with result accuracy ranging from 16.2\% to 36.8\%. An audit of 900 runs on 100 shared tasks confirms PIT violations in 193 of the 380 runs that pass result checks (50.8\%), showing that output agreement alone does not establish temporal validity.

papers.title: A Beltrami Mode in Extreme Fractional Hydrodynamics under Stochastic Forcing
papers.abstract: We construct an exact stochastic solution of the extreme order endpoint of adaptive fractional Navier Stokes (AFNS) hydrodynamics on the three-dimensional periodic torus. A helical Beltrami eigenfield reduces the nonlinear vector equation to a scalar Ornstein Uhlenbeck process when the white-in-time forcing is aligned with that eigenfield. The resulting invariant Gaussian law yields explicit formulas for the stationary energy, its fluctuations, temporal correlations, circulation, and helicity. Under the same forcing, the corresponding classical Navier Stokes mode has a stationary energy that diverges as the Reynolds number tends to infinity, while the Euler limit exhibits linear growth of the mean energy and has no invariant probability law. The construction isolates, without a cascade hypothesis, the statistical effect of the finite fractional dissipation retained at the extreme endpoint of AFNS.

papers.title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL
papers.abstract: While federated reinforcement learning (RL) has traditionally guaranteed high efficiency in homogeneous environments, collaboration is often hindered when agents possess distinct goals. In this paper, we flip this paradigm, framing reward heterogeneity not as a hurdle to consensus, but as a structural asset that catalyzes exploration. We first propose Personalized Federated Upper Confidence Bound Value Iteration (PF-UCBVI), which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. To eliminate the risks of explicit exploration, we then introduce Personalized Federated Exploration-Free Value Iteration (PF-EFVI), a purely greedy algorithm that leverages reward diversity to ensure state-action coverage. We prove that PF-EFVI attains logarithmic regret without explicit exploration bonuses under sufficient reward diversity. Our results reveal that agent disagreement shifts the exploration burden from temporal complexity to spatial diversity, enabling efficient collective learning without explicit exploration.

papers.title: Neural Networks with Local Converging Inputs for Solving the 3D Stokes Equations on Unstructured Meshes: Novel Techniques and Advances
papers.abstract: Neural-network surrogates for fluid-flow PDEs usually learn the solution globally, which requires large networks and many high-fidelity training simulations. Neural networks with local converging inputs (NNLCI) instead work locally. They predict the high-fidelity solution at a point from two converging coarse-grid solutions sampled near that point, which keeps the network small, needs little training data, and generalizes across geometries. Here, the two low-fidelity meshes, LF1 and LF2, have on average about 300 and 730 tetrahedra, compared with about 155,000 in the high-fidelity mesh (HF).
