In this work, we develop an NNLCI framework for three-dimensional Stokes equations on unstructured tetrahedral meshes and introduce two techniques for building local inputs near complex curved boundaries. First, input patches may extend beyond the boundary, with the outside values obtained from a local least-squares fit, so that every high-fidelity point can be predicted, including those next to the wall. Second, the local mesh spacing is estimated from neighboring centroids, which sets the stencil size consistently on unstructured meshes. For pipe flows with one to three bumps, including a circumferentially rotated bump, NNLCI reduces the relative $L^2$ error of the finer low-fidelity solution by $90\%$ to $94\%$, evaluated at all high-fidelity points. Both techniques carry over to other NNLCI problems with smooth solutions on point-cloud discretizations.

papers.title: Evolution of cooperation in enterprise resource-sharing networks with dynamic participation and adaptive decision-making
papers.abstract: Resource sharing among enterprises is an important mechanism for improving resource utilization efficiency and facilitating collaborative development. However, the emergence and sustainability of cooperative behavior depend critically on whether enterprises choose to participate in resource-sharing activities and how they balance cooperation and competition in their decision-making processes. To investigate these issues, we develop an evolutionary cooperation model on the enterprise resource-sharing network that integrates participation status, decision-making modes, and cooperative strategies within a unified framework. Specifically, enterprises dynamically switch between active and dormant states according to their aspiration levels, while Q-learning is employed to enable adaptive selection between payoff-driven and conformist decision-making modes. Meanwhile, interactions between resource-sharing and non-sharing in active enterprises are characterized by the snowdrift game. Through extensive simulations, we systematically examine the effects of the payoff parameter, the reinforcement-learning parameters, the participation and Q-learning mechanism, and network size on enterprise participation and the evolution of cooperation. The results show that an intermediate aspiration level is most favorable for sustaining enterprise participation and facilitating the emergence of cooperation. Moreover, the dynamic activation mechanism effectively mitigates the decline in cooperation under high cost-to-benefit ratios, allowing the system to sustain a decent level of cooperative behavior. These findings highlight the important roles of dynamic participation and adaptive decision-making in shaping the evolution of resource-sharing cooperation and provide a new modeling framework to understand the emergence and persistence of cooperation in complex enterprise networks.

papers.title: RBLA+: Efficient Rank-Specific LoRA Adapter Extraction for Federated Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous Clients
papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) reduces communication and computational overhead by training and exchanging compact trainable LoRA factors. Clients may use different LoRA ranks to meet adapter communication budgets and accommodate different local adaptation needs. The server must process these differences during aggregation and construct adapters at each client's rank for local training. We distinguish pre-aggregation alignment, which handles factor dimensions and scaling conventions before aggregation and rank-specific LoRA adapter extraction, which constructs client-sized pairs from the aggregated global model. Two common approaches to rank-specific extraction are direct rank truncation and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the dense update. Direct prefix truncation keeps the leading columns of one aggregated factor and the corresponding rows of the other. It is cheap but can increase reconstruction error. The dense SVD approach first forms the product of aggregated LoRA factors. It then decomposes this matrix and retains the leading singular components to construct adapters at the target rank. This gives the optimal rank-constrained approximation in Frobenius norm but incurs significant computational overhead. To address this trade-off, we propose RBLA+ as an extension of RBLA. It uses established compact QR/core-SVD decomposition to minimize Frobenius error for the extracted LoRA update without forming the dense update. It also accounts for client and server scaling conventions during upload and broadcast. Across vision and language tasks, RBLA+ improves accuracy over RBLA in multiple heterogeneous settings. In CPU benchmarks with synthetic adapters, RBLA+ has lower extraction time than the dense partial-SVD baseline. RBLA+ preserves each client's prescribed adapter size and per-round communication payload.

papers.title: IIT Patna at "ICPR 2026 TVRID Competition on Privacy-Preserving Person Re-Identification from Top-View RGB-Depth Camera"
papers.abstract: Privacy-aware person re-identification (Re-ID) from top-view cameras replaces frontal appearance with anthropometric shape, while depth sensing further reduces color-based identity cues. The ICPR 2026 TVRID competition evaluates this setting using 86 identities captured by four synchronized Intel RealSense D455 cameras with RGB and Depth streams across flat, ascent, descent, and oblique viewpoints. Performance is measured using mAP and CMC@1 across within-camera in/out, ascent-descent, and flat-oblique scenarios. The competition had 147 registered participants and 33 final submissions. Three teams from IIT Patna participated: 'abhinavkumar03' and 'sjkdgfhl_' ranked 5th and 7th among 31 ranked participants, and 'vivek katuri' reached 77.67% CMC@1 / 85.20% mAP on the RGB track. This paper presents the methods of the two top-10 teams. Methodology 1 (abhinavkumar03) achieves 93.51% mAP and 90.42% CMC@1 on Depth, ranking 4th of 28, while Methodology 2 (sjkdgfhl_) reaches 99.63%/99.35% on RGB and 86.26%/80.34% on Depth. Both substantially outperform the 57.19% track-average Depth mAP, with Methodology 1 yielding a 7.3-point gain over Methodology 2. These results demonstrate the importance of depth representation and supervision for privacy-preserving Re-ID.

papers.title: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes
papers.abstract: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. Online partial coverage increases shadow-route share over no monitoring by .701 [.574,.826] and .575 [.412,.737], while task accuracy remains .905/.913 and signed frozen message contribution remains .592/.563. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuffling changes .668 of receiver predictions and route alone retains .388 accuracy versus .25 chance. A corrected explicit-silence cost makes 18/20 policies fully silent and lowers mean sending to .050, but its strict complete-suppression gate fails because two seeds retain communication. Failed semantic-evasion and operational gates further bound the result. The evidence supports adaptive reallocation of a joint message--route code under partial monitoring, not open-world route discovery, emergent encryption, or a universal defense.

papers.title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. We argue that overcoming this paradox requires embedding \emph{learnability} along three interdependent axes: cognitive learnability (learning what to investigate), experimental learnability (learning where to search), and embodied learnability (learning how to act). Building on this view, we introduce the Embodied Science Agent (ESA), which unifies digital intelligence with physical embodiment through three synergistic components: a Digital Agent that provides cognitive and experimental learnability via memory-based reasoning and Bayesian optimisation, an Embodied Agent that provides embodied learnability via generalisable instrument control, and an Embodied Unified Interface for seamless coordination. We validated ESA in autonomous wastewater treatment experiments, navigating over 200 million possible conditions. Through 15 continuous rounds, ESA raised the final solution transmittance from 82\% to 99.7\%, corresponding to a 98.5\% reduction in residual dye concentration and near-complete decolourisation, while its learned visuomotor policies generalised across varying instrument placements, a promising step toward next-generation SDLs for autonomous scientific discovery.

papers.title: DocFS: File Systems as Agentic Reasoning Environments for Complex Multimodal Document Question Answering
papers.abstract: VLM-based agents solve complex tasks by iteratively interacting with environments, and their effectiveness depends heavily on how the environment exposes information and provides tools for acting on it. However, constructing an effective environment for complex multimodal document question answering remains challenging: documents usually span many pages, with multimodal contents distributed across hierarchical sections and linked by cross-modal associations, while existing methods organize documents into structured representations that address only the information side of the environment and lack tools aligned with the structure, limiting agents' ability to fully exploit it. We observe that file systems naturally combine structure organization with aligned tools: directories and files encode document structure, while file operations provide rich tools to access file contents. Building on this insight, we propose DocFS, a file-system-based agentic framework that reorganizes raw documents as file systems, where directories mirror the section hierarchy and explicit links connect text with figures, tables, and equations. Based on well-established file system tools such as navigation, search, and reading, agents can iteratively explore the document structure, locate relevant evidence, and understand fine-grained local information. Paired with Qwen3.5-Plus, DocFS achieves state-of-the-art performance on MMLongBench-Doc and FinRAGBench-V, outperforming the strongest baselines by 2.9 and 4.3 percentage points, respectively, and is up to 10.3x faster with up to 10.1x fewer tokens than the strongest baseline during reasoning.

papers.title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation
papers.abstract: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) reduces the computational cost of attention through token-level selection. However, its indexer still scores the entire causal prefix for each query, making indexing a dominant source of latency in long-context inference. Notably, the indexer alone can account for more than 50% of total prefill GPU time at long context lengths. To address this bottleneck, we propose ADIndex, an Adaptive and Distillation-driven Indexing method for token-level sparse attention. ADIndex integrates three key components: (i) a layer-wise calibration strategy that adaptively accommodates cross-query retrieval overlap, motivated by our observation of pronounced inter-layer heterogeneity; (ii) a group-level distillation scheme that leverages this heterogeneity to efficiently train adaptive layer-wise group indexers, capturing salient retrieval signals from individual queries; and (iii) a low-latency inference strategy that reduces repeated full-prefix scans through token bank sharing within query groups while retaining query-specific refinement. Experiments on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1 demonstrate that ADIndex preserves near-lossless task performance on LongBench, LongBench v2, and RULER while delivering substantial efficiency gains over standard DSA, including prefill and decoding kernel speedups of up to 6.22x and 3.40x, respectively, at a context length of 256K across the layer-wise reuse configurations, as well as an end-to-end serving speedup of 1.54x at a context length of 128K.

papers.title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
papers.abstract: Time-series classifiers deployed in risk-sensitive domains must be (1) accurate, (2) interpretable, and (3) able to abstain when evidence is weak. Existing methods do not deliver all 3 at once, and the obstacle is structural, rather than logistical. Meaningful temporal patterns cannot be defined without knowing segment boundaries, yet meaningful boundaries cannot be placed without knowing which patterns to expect. Existing approaches break this circularity by using fixed windows or expert-annotated vocabularies, thereby sacrificing at least one of the 3 properties. We introduce ConceptTime, which closes the loop through a single self-supervised signal. A frozen probabilistic forecaster predicts a distribution over the next observation at every timestep of the sequence. We call the mismatch between its prediction and the realized signal the predictive surprise. This signal both locates segment boundaries and characterizes each resulting segment through the forecaster. Segments are thus grounded by how they behaved relative to expectation, not by what they look like. These summaries cluster into a vocabulary of dynamical regimes that we call concepts. A lightweight head classifies from the concept sequence, and the distance to the nearest concept yields reliability by design. Across 17 public benchmarks, ConceptTime is competitive with state-of-the-art black-box accuracy, beats every interpretable baseline, and retains near-98% accuracy on Epilepsy with 1% of labels. It further remains competitive with softmax, prototype-distance, and SHAP/TimeX/TimeX++ on OOD detection and deletion faithfulness, without a single annotation, language model call, or domain expert. Code is available at: this https URL .

papers.title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. However, extending WSP to physical problems remains challenging, particularly in achieving both solution accuracy and physical consistency. In this paper, we propose Physics2Weight (PtW), a framework that extends WSP to solving partial differential equations by directly generating neural network weights and editing architectures based on governing equations and initial and boundary conditions. PtW introduces physics-constrained prompting and physics-guided architecture editing, combined with iterative weight refinement from WSP, to improve solution accuracy and physical consistency without gradient-based optimization. Experiments on four PDEs, namely the heat, advection, Burgers', and Allen--Cahn equations, demonstrate lower solution errors than conventional physics-informed neural networks, while revealing limitations in satisfying the governing equations for nonlinear PDEs.

papers.title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
papers.abstract: Enterprises increasingly use large language model agents to execute standard operating procedures (SOPs): long, branching, tool-intensive workflows. Yet there is little controlled evidence for choosing among competing agentic architectures. Holding the model, tasks, and tools fixed and varying only the architecture, we compare four designs (a function-calling single agent, a skill-augmented agent, centralized multi-agent orchestration, and a triage swarm; eight arms) across 13 enterprise SOPs, and introduce a skill-definition quality rubric to build matched high and low-quality skill corpora. Three takeaways emerge. (1)~\textbf{There is no universal best architecture; the right choice is SOP-dependent.} On a given SOP, task success ranges from under $10\%$ on the hardest to near $100\%$ on the easiest; no architecture is statistically separable in aggregate, and added structure only plausibly pays off on complex, branching SOPs (a directional, not yet significant, trend). (2)~\textbf{Added architecture cost must be justified by a task-success gain.} Every coordinated arm (multi-agent or skill-augmented) spends $1.4$--$4.7\times$ the tokens and $2.6$--$5.8\times$ the latency of the single agent for gains that are usually small and rarely significant, making the single agent the efficient default; high-quality skills do lift success (to $73.1\%$ from $67.4\%$) while degraded skills fall below it. (3)~\textbf{Implementation quality outweighs the single- versus multi-agent choice.} A plausible multi-agent implementation loses to the single agent, yet a targeted redesign of it becomes the only arm to significantly beat the baseline ($75.6\%$ vs.\ $67.4\%$).

papers.title: Reliability Analysis for Ground-Air Cooperative Wireless-Powered Internet-of-Things
papers.abstract: Battery-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices face significant challenges in maintaining long-term uplink data collection, especially in network-limited scenarios. This paper investigates a Ground-Air cooperative Wireless-Powered IoT network (GA-WPIoT), where ground power beacons (GPBs) provide radio-frequency energy supply and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) serve as flexible aerial access points for IoT data collection. Unlike conventional UAV-enabled wireless-powered solutions, GA-WPIoT decouples energy transfer and data collection, reducing the hardware and energy burden of UAVs. To capture the device-level performance variations among IoT devices, we develop a stochastic geometry-based analytical framework, where UAVs are modeled by a Matérn hard-core point process, IoT devices by a Poisson point process, and GPBs by a finite annular binomial point process. The conditional success probabilities of the GPB-device link (for energy transfer) and the device-UAV link (for data collection) are characterized, and device-level reliability distributions are obtained through the Meta-Distribution based analysis. Numerical results under suburban and urban environments reveal the impacts of UAV altitude and annular GPB deployment on reliability distributions, providing useful guidelines for GA-WPIoT.

papers.title: On the average eccentricity of Eulerian and bipartite Eulerian digraphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be an Eulerian digraph of order $n$ and minimum degree $\delta$. We prove that the average eccentricity of $D$ satisfies $\avec(D) \leq \frac{3n}{\delta+1}$, and that $\avec(D) \leq \frac{2n}{\delta}+2$ if $D$ is bipartite. We show that both bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant and the $\delta+1$ versus $\delta+2$ gap (resp.\ the $\delta$ versus $\delta+1$ gap in the bipartite case), where the average eccentricity of the extremal examples shows that $\avec = \frac{3n}{\delta+2}-2$ in general and $\avec = \frac{2n}{\delta+1}-\frac{5}{2}$ in the bipartite case for $\delta \geq 2$. We further conjecture that these values are the true maxima up to an additive constant (for $\delta \geq 3$ in the bipartite case).

papers.title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
papers.abstract: Black-box LLM fingerprinting aims to determine whether a target model was derived from a source model when only the output responses to input queries are observable. One way to reveal this relationship is to perturb each query and observe the resulting responses of both models, yielding two corresponding sets of response variations. These sets provide two complementary sources of information: the relations among response changes within each set, and the correspondence of response changes between the two sets. Existing approaches, however, have not fully exploited both. We introduce \textbf{SetPrint}, a training-free method that jointly captures both within-set relations and between-set correspondence. SetPrint expresses each response change relative to the mean change of its own set, and then compares changes from the two models that were induced by the same perturbation. On LeaFBench, SetPrint consistently outperforms existing training-free black-box fingerprinting methods. Further analyses attribute these gains to both within-set relations and between-set correspondence.

papers.title: Maze Runner: Autonomous Maze Navigation with Line-Based Localization and Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: Maze navigation requires localization from sparse, repetitive geometry, planning through narrow corridors, and control that stays safe when the estimate or the map is wrong. We present Maze Runner, an open autonomy stack in C++ and ROS 2 that addresses these needs end to end on a simulated Husarion ROSbot XL with a 2D LiDAR in Gazebo. Perception extracts wall lines from each scan with RANSAC and total least squares, with per-line uncertainty. The same line front end feeds two estimators: an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that localizes against a line map built from the maze mesh, and an EKF SLAM variant that builds the line map online. Planning runs online on an inflated occupancy grid with A* plus line-of-sight shortcutting, or with a forward-only Hybrid A*. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) tracks the plan while discrete-time Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) on world-frame LiDAR points keep the robot clear of walls and unmapped obstacles. The algorithms live in a ROS-free, unit-tested core library, and the whole stack builds and runs from a single reproducible environment. In simulation, the robot drives a 135 m route through the maze with 1.0 cm localization RMSE against the known map and 24 cm in SLAM mode, the planner returns a path in 6 ms, and the NMPC solves in 11.7 ms on average, never exceeding its 80 ms budget.

papers.title: The Four-Model Scott Complexity Spectrum: $F(4)=8$
papers.abstract: Gonzalez, Rossegger, and Turetsky introduced a spectrum-counting function $F(n)$ for the Scott complexities realized by $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_2$ theories with exactly $n$ countable models. They proved $7\leq F(4)\leq 8$ and left the exact value open. We prove $F(4)=8$. More precisely, we construct a $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_2$ sentence with exactly four countable models whose optimal Scott complexities are $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_2$, $\Sigma^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, and $d\text{-}\Sigma^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, one of each. The construction starts with a complete first-order Ehrenfeucht theory having exactly two almost-prime and two limit models, whose existence follows from a realization theorem of Sudoplatov, and then passes to a full first-order Morleyization. The proof is organized around two low-level transfer principles. First, in a small theory, a $\Sigma^{\mathrm{in}}_3$ Scott sentence forces a model to be prime over a finite tuple; after Morleyization the converse holds. Second, if a model realizes every complete finite-tuple type over the empty set, then every $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_3$ sentence true in it is true in the countable saturated model. These two principles force the four models into the four distinct Scott-complexity classes above.

papers.title: Borrowed Planckian dissipation in magic-angle twisted graphene
papers.abstract: In strange metals, the ratio of the coefficients producing signature linear-in-$T$ resistivity and the logarithmic specific heat is free of the coupling between the electrons and whatever scatters them. In the materials studied so far that coupling is fixed by chemistry. Magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene provides a dial with a displacement field $D$ that breaks the mirror symmetry separating a light Dirac cone from the flat bands, and the Dirac carriers borrow the Planckian self-energy of the flat band with a weight proportional to $D^2+D_0^2$. Resistance curves taken at eight fields are consistent with the field acting on the scattering rate rather than on the number of carriers. The slope in temperature follows $a(1+D^2/D_0^2)$ without the quartic term that a depleting Dirac pocket adds, and the elastic part varies by less than 5\% between 0.20 and 0.30~V/nm while the inelastic part grows 2.5-fold up to 0.38~V/nm. The thermally averaged Kubo formula favors flat-band weight placed symmetrically about the Fermi level over a single level. Borrowed dissipation keeps the bath exponent and transport prefactor of the flat band's own electrons but carries exactly twice their entropy per unit of borrowed coupling whenever the bath has dynamics of its own, so the field-differential ratio is $2\pi^3/21\zeta(3)\approx2.46$ for a conformal flat band and, in a numerical search, at most 2.73 for monotonic bath spectra without a high-energy rate floor. The discriminating test is the entropy measured in steps of $D$.

papers.title: Goldstone-Mediated Chiral Superconductivity in Self-Doped Electron Crystals
papers.abstract: Motivated by the observation of superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene in the proximity of electronic crystalline phases, we study the possibility of pairing mediated by electronic phonons. We focus on the vicinity of the phase boundary between trivial and topological electron crystals, where self-doping generically gives rise to a small Fermi sea of carriers with Dirac dispersion. We compute the Goldstone phonon spectra of the self-doped crystal (SDC) using a self-consistent approach, and subsequently derive the effective electronic-phonon-mediated interaction between itinerant carriers at the Fermi surface. Remarkably, we find that the Coulomb repulsion can be overscreened by the Goldstone phonons, leading to a chiral topological superconductor with an unpaired Majorana edge mode. Our conclusions are robust across the $\lambda$-jellium model and a simplified model of rhombohedral graphene, and we propose characteristic non-linear I-V signals as a test of our prediction. More generally, our results outline an intriguing route for unconventional superconductivity where both electronic correlations and topology play key roles.

papers.title: Early X-ray emission as an observational diagnostic of gamma-ray burst progenitors
papers.abstract: Identifying the progenitors of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) from the properties of their early high-energy emission detected by wide-field satellites is crucial for advancing our understanding of GRB physics and for multi-messenger astronomy. Current classification methods, which rely primarily on prompt emission properties, exhibit large scatter and are challenged by recently detected events. In this Letter, we propose a new method to classify GRB progenitors using their early X-ray emission, which is detectable by current wide-field X-ray monitors. We performed a systematic time-resolved spectral analysis of the X-ray steep decay phase for a sample of 23 collapsar-driven GRB candidates detected by the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. We fitted the spectra over the $0.3 - 150 \, \rm keV$ energy range using both a physical synchrotron model and the empirical Band function, allowing us to constrain the spectral peak energy and the bolometric flux. We find a correlation between the rest-frame synchrotron cooling frequency, $\nu_{c,z}$, and the isotropic-equivalent luminosity, $L_{\rm iso}$, that is clearly separated from the $\nu_{c,z} - L_{\rm iso}$ relation followed by merger-driven GRB candidates. A similarly distinct separation is found in the correlation between the rest-frame peak energy, $E_{p,z}$, and $L_{\rm iso}$ obtained with the Band model. Finally, we provide a prescription for classifying fast X-ray transients detected by the Wide-field X-ray Telescope aboard the Einstein Probe mission, as its narrow energy range ($0.5 - 4 \, \rm keV$) limits spectral modelling to a simple power law. We show that the photon index and X-ray luminosity of the steep decay spectra clearly separate collapsar- and merger-driven candidate events, making them powerful diagnostics of GRB progenitors.

papers.title: SPMW: A Grid-Based Programming Model for Scalable Accelerator Design
papers.abstract: Modern accelerators specialize recurring computation and replicate it across regular hardware structures to achieve high performance. Sustaining this parallelism requires equally deliberate data delivery. Yet design tools often express these structures as sequential programs or flatten them into separate hardware modules and connections. This obscures shared patterns and leads to repeated compiler work. We introduce Single Program, Multiple Connected Work Units (SPMW), a grid-based programming model for scalable accelerator design that makes grid regularity a first-class abstraction. SPMW decouples local work-unit behavior from grid connectivity and data delivery. To our knowledge, SPMW is the first programming model to retain regularity throughout the compilation process, combining behavioral HLS with structural RTL generation for both fixed-function and domain-specific instruction-programmable accelerators. We implement SPMW with a Python frontend and an MLIR-based compiler that synthesizes each distinct kernel configuration once for reuse across independent hardware instances. Preserving regularity also enables parallel compilation and functional simulation to accelerate iterative design feedback. We use SPMW to generate a 32x32 systolic array that reduces GEMM latency and parallel kernel-to-RTL compilation time by 4.36x and 619x relative to AutoSA. Our FFT achieves up to 2.65x lower latency than HP-FFT. Our mini-TPU and our SPMW implementation of the FEATHER accelerator demonstrate complex composition and outperform their RTL baselines. Parallel functional simulation provides up to 18.4x speedup over Vitis HLS C simulation on the mini-TPU workloads. SPMW is also agent-friendly: given the same design specification, all five coding agents produce SPMW designs that satisfy the correctness and latency requirements, with 7.51x lower token usage than for SystemVerilog.

papers.title: When Proofs Are Abundant, What Is a Paper For?
papers.abstract: AI systems now produce formally verified proofs of celebrated open problems, and the cost of obtaining a correct proof is falling toward zero. If correctness becomes cheap, what is left for a research paper to communicate? I argue that a paper is not exhausted by a verified statement. It is a narrative exposed to the criticism of a community, made of an intension (the author's choice of problem and perspective), a scientific chain of thought (the reasoning steps leading to the result), and the arguments supporting each step. Most published mathematics is judged on these two elements rather than on correctness alone, and machine-generated formal scripts convey neither. Borrowing from logic and type theory, I formalise the first as a Derivation-Level Intension and the second as a Directional Extension: a decomposition of a proof into cut-points whose axiomatic footprints reveal its weak links, where the result could be strengthened, and its strong links, which can be transported to other theories. Moreover, I examine five roles AI can play in the research process, including bibliographical search and critical judgment, and show that none of them removes the need to declare these two elements. I mention ways these two concepts could be useful for Journals and for training of young mathematicians in a AI era. If proofs become abundant, the scarce resource is not correctness but a community's shared understanding of why a result matters and how it could be pushed further.

papers.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict from a labelled context in a single forward pass. A recent benchmark reported that they decisively outperform tree ensembles for customer churn, but it compared them with untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and scored only ranking metrics, while a retention campaign is judged in money. We re-evaluate TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast and TabICL v2 against Optuna-tuned GBDTs on five public telecom churn datasets over 10 seeded splits. We separate three questions: whether a model ranks churners well, whether that ranking earns more expected maximum profit (EMP), and whether its probabilities can drive a threshold policy. With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more EMP than the best tuned GBDT on Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%), and these two gains also hold against each of the three tuned GBDTs separately. On Orange it is ahead in all 10 splits (14.3%), but the gain is not significant after correction (Holm p = 0.155). The splits resample the same datasets, so these results do not stand for independent operators. TabICL v2, the earlier benchmark's leader, beats the best tuned GBDT only on Iranian, not all three of them, and underpredicts Orange churn by 2.1 points on a 7.3% base rate. On the datasets and splits where we tested them, a substantially larger tuning budget and a duplicate-aware split leave the main conclusions unchanged. Retuning the baseline cuts the earlier headline gap from 6.1 to 4.0 PR-AUC points without closing it. The licence of the TabPFN-3.5 weights we used (License v1.0), not scoring cost, is what stands between its gains and production use.

papers.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. We propose the competence circuit, summarized as IKC + KC + C, that decomposes an agent's real-world impact into three pathways: intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Using the canonical fast-takeoff debate as a stress test, we formalize the conditions for intelligence-mediated fast takeoff as a conjunction jointly sufficient for fast catastrophic supremacy, showing that most rely on rapid knowledge acquisition or control attainment rather than intelligence alone. We operationalize epistemic intelligence as hypothesis-selection efficiency and validate this framework via stochastic simulation on NK fitness landscapes across six scenarios spanning the conjunctive chain. An analytic bound supported by the simulations shows that intelligence-driven speedup is capped by the ratio of competing intelligence levels regardless of task difficulty. The simulations also expose a fast-takeoff dilemma: a large intelligence-driven speedup multiplier materializes only when the hypothesis space is noisy, but the absolute timescale remains constrained by the time required for capability-critical tests, so a large multiplier need not imply rapid progress. Simulations also indicate that institutional chokepoints disproportionately slow down superintelligent agents when mandatory authorization delays are large relative to the negligible time these agents spend on unproductive search. We argue that the dominant safety levers are restricting control and enforcing knowledge boundaries rather than limiting intelligence alone, and this applies to agentic systems at any capability level. Purely digital domains weaken these bottlenecks, strengthening the case for architectures that intentionally "put physics in the loop."

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning based control of Cancer Chemotherapy treatments
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning has achieved tremendous success in recent years. Extending its scope from the traditional complex games such as Atari, Go, Pokeman, and Chess, reinforcement learning has caught researchers' attention on modelling real-life scenarios. Personalized medicine and the dynamic treatment regimen are two such preliminary research fields; researchers are focusing their mindsets currently. Estimating the optimal dynamic treatment regimens from the observational real clinical data is being popularized among the researchers, widening its scope towards more advanced versions of reinforcement learning algorithms. This research is about a research study that focused on reinforcement learning techniques that have been approached in the context of cancer chemotherapy treatments. Primarily this thesis addresses the result of the study by means of the state-of-the-art on reinforcement learning techniques used in generating the optimal policy for sequential treatments, including the existing online reinforcement learning approaches. Thereby a simulation for cancer chemotherapy via traditional Q-learning would be presented. Secondly, the study will extend towards using offline reinforcement learning in the optimal policy generation. Thus, the proposed solution follows a data-driven approach, which works on the real human colon cancer clinical data. The novelty of the proposed solution resides in the implementation of an offline reinforcement learning approach by means of a model-based architecture using the conservative Q-learning and the model-based offline policy optimization algorithm. As per the experimental results and the evaluations, it was revealed that the proposed Chemo RL model caters well the problem of cancer chemotherapy treatment scheduling and serves as a supportive model for the junior oncologists in deciding their treatment decisions.

papers.title: Fermions fields inside the geometric algebra of spacetime
papers.abstract: The (signed) basis versors of the geometric algebra of space-time form the extraspecial groups of order 32. Ignoring signs and the unit element, we show that the remaining fifteen normalized basis versors can be written as, or factorized into, a unit space bivector (of three-dimensional space) and an isoversor. Isoversors are: the volume trivector of space, the pseudoscalar, and the basis time-axis vector. Our first result is that this central product structure, already known for extraspecial groups, also holds in the geometric algebra of space-time and is crucial for exhibiting generators of continuous groups in the algebra. In a second main result, inspired by Hestenes' 1982 paper ``Space-time structure of weak and electromagnetic interactions'', we uncover two pairs of special unitary groups of order two and three (in various representations). A rich algebraic structure emerges, leading us to our third main result: the description inside the geometric algebra of space-time of thirty-two flavorless particles of matter and antimatter. The sixteen matter particles, four leptons (left/right with up/down isospins) and four triplets of quarks (with three colors in addition to chirality and isospin), are gathered four by four into quadrispinors in two different ways: particles in a quadrispinor have either the same color or the same isospin and chirality. Thanks to this twofold distribution of the sixteen matter particles inside four quadrispinors, the same continuous group based on the isoversors produces the electroweak and strong gauge symmetry. However, chirality forbids the gauge mixing of left and right particles, which motivates the restriction to SU(2) $\times$ U(1) for the electroweak interaction. Finally, as a fourth main result, we thoroughly study the dynamics of quadrispinors by generalizing the conventional treatment of bispinors in geometric algebra.

papers.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
papers.abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout. Adding a graph image yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, driven by strong precision improvements on low-complexity questions (+4.65 F1). Mixed-effects and regression analyses show that these multimodal gains do not depend strongly on model scale, but are highly sensitive to graph layout: image-only settings sharply degrade performance, hierarchical Graphviz layouts outperform less organized renderings, and decomposing large subgraphs into separated paths yields the largest improvements. Taken together, the results indicate that visual prompting primarily aids KGQA by enhancing prediction precision in low-complexity contexts, provided that visual design respects cognitive and perceptual constraints. To optimize both accuracy and inference efficiency, we argue for adaptive visual prompting policies that selectively append diagrams to small, visually sparse subgraphs with well-structured layouts, avoiding unnecessary visual clutter and token overhead on complex queries. We conclude by relating these findings to a visual notation design theory, outlining how principled diagram encoding can guide future multimodal VLM prompting.

papers.title: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. At the behavioral level, larger variants reproduce and amplify human cross-scale correlations; amplification persists after correcting the seven-scale human correlations for measurement attenuation. We then examine whether this structure is reflected internally. Contrastive direction analysis finds geometry aligned with the human matrix in larger instruct variants, but little alignment in base variants under this assay. Across models, geometry strength is associated with behavioral amplification (r = 0.68, p = 0.008; partial r = 0.69 controlling for log size). To relate internal structure to output behavior, a matched activation-probing paradigm shows that probe slopes vary less than behavioral slopes (1.38-1.77 vs 0.52-1.53). A synthetic control shows that ridge probing can inflate these slopes; after subtracting a baseline based on a reliability proxy from another analysis, adjusted slopes remain associated with behavior (r = 0.88). We term the measured probe-behavior gap readout attenuation. These results establish decodability and geometric alignment under the tested assays, without showing that the measured directions mediate the cross-persona answers.

papers.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
papers.abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, enabling comprehensive landslide reasoning. To support training and evaluation in this domain, we also present LandslideVL, the first benchmark for intelligent landslide analysis, combining visual imagery and newly introduced textual prompts. Comprehensive experiments across public datasets and LandslideVL demonstrate that LandslideFM achieves superior quantitative and qualitative performance. Most importantly, LandslideFM surpasses general-purpose VLMs in specialized landslide reasoning and scene analysis. Our code is released at this https URL .

papers.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
papers.abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro-F1 points when off-topic asides are inserted, topics are removed or sections are reordered. Ablations conducted to understand the contribution of the SAE revealed that classifiers reaching baseline performance without it were several times larger. Our findings show that compact topic monitors can be trained inexpensively in prefill and deployed during generation. More broadly, our work shows where SAEs are useful beyond safety classification. Our code, dataset and checkpoints are available at this https URL and this https URL

papers.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
papers.abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. Two controls test what answers rest on: the closed book removes the record, and instrument pairs alter one satellite's data while nothing changes on the ground. Evaluations of twelve multimodal agents reveal that leading agents complete most analyses end to end but falter when an answer requires mapping from imagery. Further analysis shows that the record moves answers from prior knowledge to the pixels but not yet to the real change on the ground: when one satellite's data are altered, half of the right answers follow the alteration. EarthRecord thus provides a principled platform for measuring and advancing agents from pixels to land change.

papers.title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
papers.abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. Provenance showed that 59-68% of error corrections involved multiple participants and that about half of all decisions incorporated the input of another participant. These results may guide design principles for multi-agent scientific systems and inform future agent harnesses, model training, and accessible autonomous experimentation.

papers.title: URL-Sim: Unified and Regulated LiDAR Simulation for High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes
papers.abstract: Reconstructing high-fidelity LiDAR simulation scenes from real-world driving logs is essential for cost-effective safety validation of autonomous driving systems. While simulators based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieve realistic scene reconstruction, their large-scale adoption is limited by slow rendering speeds. Recent 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) approaches have improved rendering efficiency through explicit primitive representation and differentiable rasterization. However, existing 3DGS-based methods remain largely restricted to rigid vehicles and produce redundant primitives through unconstrained densification. To address these limitations, we propose URL-Sim, a unified and regulated dynamic LiDAR simulation framework. URL-Sim constructs a dynamic Gaussian scene graph that decouples the modeling of traffic participants, including vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, enabling accurate reconstruction of heterogeneous dynamic objects within a single framework. It further introduces a regulated Gaussian densification strategy that ranks primitives with multi-dimensional importance scores and allocates Gaussians to the most critical regions while keeping the total primitive count bounded. Experiments on the Waymo and KITTI-360 datasets demonstrate that URL-Sim achieves higher quantitative accuracy and visual quality than existing baselines under comparable primitive budgets, and accurately recovers the geometry and poses of diverse dynamic traffic participants.

papers.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
papers.abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(\Lambda)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $\Lambda$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.

papers.title: Topology-Aware Reinforcement Learning for CAD Decomposition toward All-Hexahedral Meshing
papers.abstract: Automatic hexahedral meshing for complex CAD models has long been regarded as the "holy grail" of mesh generation. The fundamental challenge arises from feature misalignment, where orthogonal or interacting features coexist, making direct hexahedral meshing infeasible and requiring decomposition into simpler, meshable blocks. While existing decomposition methods, including frame-field pipelines and learning-based techniques, have reduced manual intervention, they can remain sensitive to geometric and topological complexity and may fail to produce valid decompositions for challenging feature configurations. Specifically, their action spaces are typically restricted to surface-based splitting, which often yields invalid or unmeshable decompositions. To address these limitations, we propose DecompRL, a deep reinforcement learning framework for CAD decomposition toward hexahedral meshing. We design a set of topology-aware internal-splitting actions that leverage both global topological structure and local geometric property to effectively separate misaligned features. Furthermore, we introduce geometric rewards together with meshability feedback to guide the learning process toward valid decompositions and high-quality meshes. Extensive experiments on ABC, Fusion360, NIST, and DeepCAD show that DecompRL achieves the highest success rate among the evaluated learning-based methods on three of the four benchmarks, while maintaining competitive mesh quality. The measured LMFF-to-DecompRL runtime ratio reaches up to two orders of magnitude; this compares the full LMFF procedure with DecompRL decomposition alone, excluding subsequent mesh generation. The largest SR improvement is observed on Fusion360, where DecompRL reaches a success rate of 59.6%.

papers.title: A novel derivative-corrected within-host viral model based on Caputo-Fabrizio fractional dynamics
papers.abstract: We study an implicit within-host viral dynamics model for uninfected target cells $H(t)$, infected cells $I(t)$, viral load $V(t)$, and damaged or removed cells $D(t)$. The model contains a parameter $\mathfrak{a}\in[0,1]$ that blends the classical instantaneous within-host dynamics with derivative-dependent correction terms. We rewrite the system as an explicit ordinary differential equation whenever a computable determinant $\Delta(H,V)$ is nonzero, derive sufficient conditions for local and global well-posedness, prove positivity and conservation of $H+I+D$, compute the basic reproduction number by the next-generation approach, and analyze long-time behavior. Under natural nondegeneracy assumptions, $I(t)\to0$, $V(t)\to0$, $H(t)\to H_\infty>0$, and $D(t)\to D_\infty$. We also derive peak conditions, a final-size identity, and discuss the biological interpretation of $\mathfrak{a}$ as a dynamical responsiveness or short-memory parameter.

papers.title: Token Importance-Aware Semantic Communication Enabled Robust Video Transmission
papers.abstract: Video applications are increasingly prevalent, yet their high data volume and temporal dependency make robust wireless transmission challenging under limited communication resources. To address this issue, we propose a token importance-aware semantic communication (Ti-SemCom) framework for bandwidth-efficient video transmission. Specifically, object and motion information is jointly extracted to identify communication-relevant regions, which are hierarchically associated with semantic tokens according to their importance. The transmitted tokens are then dynamically selected based on both token importance and the available bandwidth, prioritizing more informative video content under resource constraints. At the receiver, untransmitted regions reuse recently reconstructed references to further reduce redundant transmission. Experiments on the CAVIAR dataset show that Ti-SemCom can achieve an 88.3\% reduction in communication cost while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality.

papers.title: An ensemble of graph generative models for assisted history matching of the Brugge field case
papers.abstract: Assisted history matching remains non-unique because many geological realisations can reproduce equivalent production responses with substantial differences between individual well matches. This ambiguity increases when a field comprises several depositional settings and modelling strategies. The paper applied a graph autoencoder approach to history matching of a benchmark Brugge field that comprises different depositional zones. Each stratigraphic zone is modelled with its dedicated generative model that comprises a joint latent space for optimisation history matching loops. Graph-based generators operate directly on the active cells of the corner-point grid, so its irregular geometry is handled without conversion to a regular lattice. The optimisation search in the 160-dimensional joint latent space is done with the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy. The multi-component objective function includes static well data mismatch, dynamic production mismatch, and a geological realism penalty based on the Decoder induced latent metric. Latent space diagnostics with topological data analysis are applied prior to history matching to test whether one generator is sufficient or whether a multiple generator formulation is required. The results show that the zone-based formulation gives coherent latent spaces, preserves the main porosity and permeability relations that vary from one zone to another, and supports history matching while keeping the solutions within the learned geological manifold. The matched models reproduce field oil and water production within the prior uncertainty range and provide a comparable well-level match to previously published Brugge studies based on Ensemble Kalman Filter, Particle Swarm Optimisation with principal component analysis of parameterisation, and Multiple Kernel Learning with Particle Swarm Optimisation.

papers.title: marineGeochemFoam: A multipurpose framework for simulating reactive transport and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and at seawater-groundwater interfaces
papers.abstract: We present marineGeochemFoam, an open-source reactive transport modeling framework for simulating early diagenesis, sediment burial, submarine groundwater discharge, and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and groundwater-seawater transition zones. The code is implemented in the widely used numerical toolbox OpenFOAM and extends the capabilities of the existing diagenetic models by supporting, among other features, i) coupled reactive transport of dissolved solute and solid species, (ii) a flexible native reaction package, supporting arbitrary reaction networks with n-th order and Monod-type kinetics, and (iii) coupling with an external geochemical code, PHREEEQC, providing access to a wide range of thermodynamically based geochemical processes. We benchmarked different features of the code across various examples with increasing complexity. Successively, the code was applied to two case studies reproducing field observations from the Hanko groundwater discharge site, Finland, and the Santa Barbara Basin, California. Beyond diagenetic applications, the code also serves as a general-purpose reactive transport simulator.

papers.title: Two-Sided Amortized Resource Analysis: Verifying Resource Lower Bounds via Ill-Typing
papers.abstract: We present a two-sided type system with potential for verifying resource lower bounds of functional programs. Automatic amortized resource analysis (AARA) verifies upper bounds: types carry potential, and typing certifies sufficient resources. A lower bound, however, is a necessity statement---the program evaluates only if enough resources are available---and prior type-based approaches obtain it by switching the substructural discipline of potential, so that upper and lower bounds live in separate type systems. Matching upper and lower bounds characterize a program's cost exactly. Our system combines AARA-style potential with the two-sided type systems of Ramsay and Walpole, whose central guarantee is that ill-typed programs do not evaluate. Typing formulas may constrain arbitrary terms and appear on both sides of the turnstile; the judgment $t : A \vdash q$ states that if $t$ evaluates to a result of type $A$, then at least $q$ units of resource must be available---that is, $q$ is a lower bound. Because potential makes typing formulas non-replicable, our system follows an affine discipline instead of the replicable contexts of the original framework. We interpret types by semantic typing over value states, pairs of values and remaining resources, and we prove soundness on a safety fragment; corollaries recover the classical two-sided guarantees and the soundness of both kinds of bounds in a single proof system. A prototype type checker in OCaml verifies, on a suite of 19 benchmarks, matching pairs of bounds that characterize costs exactly, as well as lower bounds for programs whose upper bounds are unavailable. In a parallel exploration, we study a two-sided linear type system in which every value is a non-replicable resource; there, closures that capture linear resources call for dual typing formulas, and the exact accounting explains the affine design of the main system.

papers.title: Conformally Sasakian manifolds and the $k$-nullity condition
papers.abstract: We study almost contact metric manifolds that are locally conformal to Sasakian manifolds in the normalization of Olszak. We show that the local conformal factors are uniquely determined by the structure; consequently, every such manifold is globally conformal to a Sasakian manifold and its Lee form is exact. We then investigate the $k$-nullity condition $ R(X,Y)\xi=k\{\eta(Y)X-\eta(X)Y\}. $ We prove that a smooth nullity function is necessarily constant, including in dimension three. Moreover, the $k$-nullity condition is equivalent to the assertion that $f=\exp(\sigma)$ satisfies $ \mathrm{Hess}_g f=-(kf+C)g $ for a constant $C$, and hence to the fact that the conformal metrics $g$ and $g_0=\exp(-2\sigma)g$ have the same geodesic circles. We derive the range of the conformal factor, a local warped-product description, and a classification in the complete case: when the Lee form is nonzero, the complete metric is a simply connected space form of curvature $k$. Finally, we construct incomplete examples of nonconstant sectional curvature in every dimension $2n+1\geq 5$.

papers.title: Spacetime contactability in Galactic civilization networks: Contact counts and percolation
papers.abstract: The number of Galactic civilizations does not determine whether they are in contact. Allowing civilizations to appear at different times separates listening, audibility, mutual-listening, and relay networks, with a distinct reply-closing condition requiring a return signal within the sender's lifetime. For each network we derive the contact counts and estimate the connectivity threshold in a uniform population, then apply the results to a structured Galactic disc, separating the detection range $d_{\rm max}$ from the light horizon $cL$ through $\chi=d_{\rm max}/cL$. The contactability is $\eta=\pi n d_{\rm max}^{2}$, where $n$ is the active civilization surface density. Averaged over civilization appearances, the lifetime listening count is $2\eta$ for all $\chi$ and, at fixed detection range, for any lifetime distribution. Audibility and mutual-listening counts sum to $4\eta$, but connectivity depends on threshold behavior rather than counts alone. As $\chi\rightarrow0$, the listening threshold decreases from the coeval value $4.51$ to $1.32\pm0.01$. Assuming an ideal complete survey, our own non-detection gives the reference bound $\eta(R_0)\le2.75$ at the Sun's Galactocentric radius. This benchmark lies above the listening, audibility and relay thresholds throughout the range studied. Unlike the coeval model, the spacetime model can satisfy both this benchmark and a local connectivity criterion, moving the local-contact frontier outward by $3.2$ kpc. Under the same benchmark, civilizations hear at most $5.5$ others on average, while the mean reply-closing count falls below unity for $\chi\gtrsim1$. Contact may therefore be common even when completed replies remain rare.

papers.title: Using LLM Agents to Evaluate Prosocial Interventions on Social Media Platforms
papers.abstract: Social media platforms are a primary source of information for many users. Although research explores various interventions to promote prosocial content or demote harmful content on platforms, there are few systematic methods for evaluating competing intervention designs before conducting costly human-subject experiments. We develop a simulation-based evaluation pipeline built on the OASIS framework. We generate 13,835 LLM-based agents, each with a unique profile. Over 20 time steps, we expose them to real-world Twitter/X posts and let them comment, like, repost, or follow. We use those agents to systematically evaluate three interventions that increase exposure to verified news: adding content, upranking content, and celebrity source cues. All interventions significantly increase news engagement, with upranking news to prominent feed positions producing the largest effects. These effects hold across agents' gender, age, and education levels. We validate our injection treatment results against a comparable human-subject study and find strong directional alignment and similar dose-normalized efficiency. Our results suggest that LLM-based agent simulations can support early-stage evaluation of platform interventions before human-subject deployment, and upranking may be more effective than news volume or source.

papers.title: Confoundry: Spatial Causal Discovery and Dynamic Effect Mapping from Earth Observation Time Series
papers.abstract: Earth observation time series provide extensive historical observations of environmental change, but causal relationships inferred from them may vary geographically and depend heavily on local model adequacy. We introduce Confoundry, a framework for spatially resolved causal discovery and dynamic effect estimation from heterogeneous Earth observation time series. Confoundry aligns multi-source raster data, removes deterministic seasonal and long-term variation, fits separate structural VAR--LiNGAM models at individual grid cells, and propagates bootstrap estimation uncertainty into mapped dynamic responses. Model diagnostics are evaluated spatially so that mapped responses can be restricted to locations meeting predefined model checks. We demonstrate the approach using monthly MODIS NDVI and ERA5-Land hydroclimatic variables over the Iberian Peninsula from 2005--2024. Of 27,050 fitted pixel models, 14,657 passed the primary diagnostic criteria. The retained models yield geographically heterogeneous model-implied NDVI responses to precipitation, temperature, potential evaporation, and shallow and deep soil moisture. Aggregated responses vary systematically along an external aridity gradient: water-related responses become relatively stronger toward drier environments, whereas temperature responses increase toward wetter conditions. A single-pixel synthetic benchmark illustrates substantial finite-record variation in recovered causal structure and dynamic effects from 20-year monthly time series. The results demonstrate that spatial causal mapping of Earth observation data is most informative when estimated responses, uncertainty, and local model adequacy are reported together.

papers.title: Oscillations in two-stage contagion on networks: contagion structure, turnover and connectivity
papers.abstract: Two-stage contagion describes processes, such as the adoption of an opinion or of a technological novelty, in which an individual must be exposed to an adopter twice before adopting. With demographic turnover these processes can generate waves of adoption and abandonment. We study these oscillations in a two-stage contagion model with turnover through a reservoir of inactive individuals and a small rate of spontaneous activation, and report four main findings. (i) In the mean-field description the oscillations are born at a supercritical Hopf bifurcation and require a predominantly two-stage contagion (first-contact adoption probability $Q\lesssim0.17$) and a slow turnover; spontaneous activation acts as a perturbation that destroys them. (ii) In finite populations demographic noise sustains quasi-cycles also outside this region, with a spectrum and variance predicted by a linear noise approximation away from the Hopf bifurcation. (iii) Reducing the connectivity of the network damps the oscillation, because naive nodes see fewer active neighbours than in a well-mixed population, and correlations measured in simulations confirm this damping mechanism; a pair approximation predicts that the sustained cycle disappears below a critical mean degree $\kc$, which decreases as $Q$ and the turnover rate decrease, and a finite-size test with up to $3.2\times10^5$ nodes confirms this threshold in simulations. (iv) At low connectivity the amplitude no longer depends on $Q$, so that sparsity erases the signature of the two-stage mechanism, whereas a faster turnover reduces the relative amplitude at every connectivity. The irregular dynamics observed in simulations are noise-driven quasi-cycles, not chaos.

papers.title: A domain-specific atomistic model for Earth's core materials
papers.abstract: Understanding Earth's core requires accurate descriptions of multicomponent iron alloys under extreme conditions. Here, we develop the Earth's Core Atomistic Model (ECAM) for Fe-Ni-S-Si-O-C-H alloys through sampling with a foundational atomistic model, targeted ab initio simulations, and iterative exploration. A compact dataset selected from nearly half a million configurations is consistently labeled using high-accuracy first-principles calculations and used to train a lightweight model. The model explicitly includes thermal electronic contributions and runs nearly two orders of magnitude faster than the original foundational model. ECAM corrects artifacts in the foundational model's description of core materials and reproduces the density, seismic velocity, Gibbs free energy, and phase diagrams of Fe and binary alloys in agreement with previous ab initio calculations. ECAM is expected to enable more realistic modeling of chemical partitioning and crystallization in Earth's core. Our workflow also provides a practical route from foundational-model sampling to efficient domain-specific simulation.

papers.title: IntentTwin: Deconfounding Candidate Support and the Oracle-to-Deployment Gap in Offline Web Behavior Prediction
papers.abstract: Offline web-behavior benchmarks frequently insert the demonstrated action into a finite candidate set and then measure reranking. We show that this protocol can create a candidate-support confound: when the target is outside training support while all distractors are sampled from that support, support membership identifies the gold action without modeling behavior. We formalize this effect with support-identifiability rate (SIR), construct support-balanced candidate sets, and evaluate a target-free dual-path proposer that combines support retrieval with open-vocabulary DOM/LM proposals. On filtered OPeRA (4,282/469/992 train/dev/test steps), the original protocol has SIR 1.0000 on target-OOV rows and a support-only rule reaches 1.0000 OOV Exact@1. Support balancing reduces SIR to 0.0000; the strongest conditional reranker obtains 0.7214 overall Exact@1, 0.7988 on IV rows, and 0.5668 on OOV rows. The target-free dual-path system reaches Proposal Recall@16 0.6915 and end-to-end Exact@1 0.5212, compared with oracle conditional Exact@1 0.7450. On Mind2Web, the same audit yields SIR 0.2380 and an oracle-to-proposal gap of 0.2125. A 200-row semantic audit labels 0.7150 of exact-key OOV targets as semantically novel, 0.2450 as locator/string variation, and 0.0400 as ambiguous (Cohen's $\kappa=0.8173$). These measurements show why support composition must be controlled alongside candidate accuracy when offline results are used to reason about deployment.

papers.title: First results from a borehole network for the seismic characterization of the Einstein Telescope Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site
papers.abstract: The low-frequency sensitivity of the Einstein Telescope depends on the seismic environment of its site, both through the mechanical coupling of ground motion to the test masses and through Newtonian noise. We present the first results of the seismic characterization of the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site based on a network of recently instrumented boreholes covering the first seven months of 2026 at four underground stations and their co-located surface sensors. Two of these boreholes were deliberately sited next to railway infrastructure, so that the levels reported here describe how anthropogenic transients propagate to depth at different distances from the source. The analysis was carried out with \texttt{SiteChar}, a Python framework developed for this work to provide a common processing pipeline across different sensors, networks and observation periods. It processes the data in sequential chunks and separates the noise floor from the contribution of transients. We present a characterization of the catalogue of observed transients and a tentative classification. These measurements form part of an integrated site characterization approach that combines the observed seismic field with three-dimensional geological and wave-propagation models to predict Newtonian noise and ultimately guide its mitigation at the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site.

papers.title: One Rater to Score Them All: Frozen Large Language Model Anchoring for Video Quality of Experience
papers.abstract: Quality of Experience results for video streaming cannot be compared across studies, because public databases share neither test material nor subjects. This work introduces a common reference rater: an open-weights large language models with a fixed rubric and greedy decoding that scores the delivery events of every session and supplies the shared items that score equating requires. The rater is used without training, and it reads only the playback event log of startup delay, stalls and quality switches, which most delivery databases retain even when they share nothing else. A monotonic curve then maps each study's native scale onto the common scale. On 3{,}552 sessions from four studies covering four rating scales, the rater attains a Spearman correlation of 0.809 on VL04 of the ITU-T P.1203 collection, exceeding P.1203 mode~0 on the same sessions, with a Krippendorff alpha of 0.974 over repeated scoring and 0.951 across three serving providers. Sessions from three further laboratories give correlations from 0.756 to 0.787. After calibration, the four studies are placed on a single 0 to 100 scale with a held-out error between 7.8 and 13.3 points, and a mean VMAF of 60 corresponds to positions 17 points apart in two of the studies.

papers.title: PyOTIS: an open-source Python package for stream solute transport with transient storage
papers.abstract: OTIS and OTIS-P provide transient-storage transport and parameter estimation, whereas E-OTIS adds coupled water-quality reactions in a separate MATLAB implementation. PyOTIS brings these workflows into an open-source Python package with legacy OTIS input support. Its contribution is software integration: a scriptable interface, structured simulation outputs, Jacobian-based parameter uncertainty, sensitivity analysis, and selectable transport schemes. A browser-based graphical user interface (GUI) provides example loading, custom parameter entry, breakthrough-curve and storage-zone plots, reference overlays, and calibration of supplied cases with confidence intervals. The package retains the OTIS Crank--Nicolson formulation and the E-OTIS reaction network; these are inherited model components rather than new process formulations. Evaluation distinguishes code comparisons, analytical convergence, and fits to observations. For the six OTIS manual examples, the comparisons distinguish model outputs from field observations and include agreement to seven significant figures for the steady-state iron profile. The nine-species E-OTIS comparison reports maximum absolute differences of order $10^{-14}$\,mg\,L$^{-1}$ against MATLAB. The conservative analytical benchmark shows approximately second-order convergence. For Clackamas River calibration, residual sums of squares differ from OTIS-P by 3.65--5.12\%, although individual parameter estimates differ by up to 39.1\%. These results support implementation consistency for the tested cases without establishing unique parameter estimates or validating every reaction pathway. Source code, example inputs, and verification scripts accompany the package.

papers.title: Trace element distribution in coarse-grained Ca-Al-rich inclusions by femtosecond LA-ICP-MS: Implications for U-Pb chronology
authors: Elishevah M. M. E. van Kooten
papers.abstract: Calcium-aluminium-rich inclusions (CAIs) in chondrites are the first solids that formed in the Solar System, as established by U-Pb chronology. After initial condensation, coarse-grained CAIs experienced melting, resulting in igneous partitioning and spatial redistribution of trace elements among constituent minerals. Understanding these distributions is essential for identifying trace-element host phases and interpreting U-Pb ages. Rare earth elements (REEs) and the actinides Th and U are particularly informative tracers, yet actinide behavior in coarse-grained CAIs remains poorly constrained. Here, we present major- and trace-element distribution maps of six coarse-grained CAIs from CV3 (Vigarano-type) chondrites acquired by femtosecond laser ablation ICP-MS. In CAIs lacking perovskite or hibonite, our results show that Al,Ti-pyroxene is the dominant host of U, Th, and most REEs, with strong enrichments observed toward pyroxene grain edges, whereas light REEs reside in melilite. Trace-element zonation reflects igneous fractional crystallization and is overprinted by melt evaporation, which caused depletion of the most volatile REEs (Yb, Eu, Ce) and U in CAI outer regions and rims. Using Nd and Th distribution maps as proxies for Cm, we model the effects of 247Cm-235U decay on mineral-scale U isotopic compositions. Variable Cm-U partitioning among coexisting minerals is predicted to generate resolvable inter-mineral 235U/238U variations, with the largest excesses in melilite.
